news.title: Mothers Help Sons Outwit Draft Board In Wartime Russia

news.abstract: Mali, unable to educate most of its children, is encouraging towns and villages to build own primary schools and hire own teachers as lart of larger effort to decentralize power; many community schools are supported by American-financed private groups; community schools, which first appeared in relatively prosperous south, are now opening in north, centering in Timbuktu; map; photos (M)
news.title: 2 Tents, Some Chalk: For Nomads, a School

news.abstract: Other Latin American nations, free of military coups for decade after two centuries of military adventurism, are concerned about whether coup that toppled Ecuador Pres Jamil Mahuad could happen elsewhere in region; groups of military officers all over region are coming under spell of old ideology that posits system in which armed forces bypass traditional political parties and ally themselves directly with masses; passage of time, combined with political squabbling and economic hardship that have accompanied restoration of democratic rule, have softened some of bitter memories of repressive military rule; map; photos (M)
news.title: Ecuador's Coup Alerts Region to a Resurgent Military

news.abstract: Prime Min Ehud Barak of Israel holds three-hour meeting in Cairo, Egypt, with Pres Hosni Mubarak in hope of re-energizing Middle East peace efforts on several fronts; is optimistic stalled negotiations with Syria will soon resume and that new talks with Palestinians, which begin on January 31, will bear fruit; Palestinian negotiators settle in for talks in Jerusalem to bridge wide gulf on difficult issues, such as refugees, status of Jerusalem and contours of possible Palestinian state; Barak has set February 13 deadline for achieving at least framework peace agreement, with further aim of reaching full-fledged treaty by September; photo (M)
news.title: Barak Visits Egypt's Leader To Give Peace Effort a Push

news.abstract: UN peacekeeping role in Congo, formerly Zaire, remains open question even though African leaders meeting at UN Security Council agree that agency should be given major role; diplomats and UN officials view Congo's complicated war unlike any other organization has faced since disintegration of Balkans into ethnic warfare and collapse of European communism; some major obstacles facing UN discussed; map; photo (M)
news.title: U.N. Faces Big Challenge in Any Congo Peacekeeping Mission

news.abstract: Guerrillas fighting to oust Israeli troops from southern Lebanon kill Col Akl Hashem, second-most-senior officer of Israeli-backed militia with bomb that exploded near home; Iranian-backed Hezbollah, or Party of God, claims responsibility; Israel vows revenge; accuses Syria, which exercises wide influence in Syria, of showing bad faith in negotiations with Israel by failing to rein in Hezbollah (M)
news.title: Israel-Allied Militia Officer InLebanon Killed By Bomb

news.abstract: News analysis of Pres Clinton's shift on trade, outlined in speech before world economic forum in Davos, Switzerland; after seven years of pushing harder than any other postwar president to expand trade between US and rest of world, Clinton warned world leaders American people have had enough and have less enthusiasm for exchanging goods and services with world than they did when he first took office; warned new trade deals will get done only if world reinvents way it thinks about trade and globalization to accommodate new American political reality; photo (M)
news.title: Clinton Shift on Trade: 'Wake-Up Call'

news.abstract: 14-year-old Ugyen Trinley Dorje, 17th Karmapa of Karma Kagyu Buddhist order who fled monastery in Chinese-controlled Tibet in December 1999, was reportedly driven by monks to rugged border area with Nepal and rode unnoticed on horseback before flying to Dharmsala, India; he is only major Tibetan lama recognized as reincarnation of his lineage by both Dalai Lama and Chinese government; map (M)
news.title: Buddhist's Escape From Tibet, by Car, Horse and Plane

news.abstract: Three Israeli soldiers are killed in southern Lebanon as Iranian-backed guerrillas continue to escalate attacks during lull in peace negotiations between Israel and Syria, Lebanon's power broker; Israeli planes respond with artillery attacks and air strikes on Hezbollah guerrilla targets in southern Lebanon; photo (M)
news.title: 3 Israeli Soldiers Killed in Lebanon, Marring Peace Effort

news.abstract: Public commission in Japan rules Aum Shinrikyo religious sect, held responsible for nerve gas attack against Tokyo subway station in 1995 that killed 12 people, still poses threat to society; instructs security authorities to put sect under surveillance for up to three years (S)
news.title: Japan Puts Gas-Attack Sect Under Scrutiny

news.abstract: SEOUL—  In a country where everyone studies English grammar from primary school through high school, Koreans are awakening to a disturbing reality: No one can speak it without private language lessons, and the ability to use it has become a requirement for everything from college to the workplace.
news.title: Inefficient English Programs Being Revised : Koreans Redouble Efforts To Conquer Language Bar

news.abstract: Mystique of former prime minister Pierre Elliott Trudeau remains strong among Canadians, three decades after Trudeaumania swept country; has been fed partly by celebrations for his 80th birthday, his reclusiveness and sympathy for death of youngest son; he ranks as best prime minister of century in poll of Canadians, who also rank him fourth in poll for person of millennium; while his big-government economic policies are in retreat and his bilingual policy has failed to blunt Quebec separatism, preoccupation with his legacy reflects how much Trudeaumania stamped two generations that will lead Canada into new century; photo (M)i
news.title: Montreal Journal; Trudeaumania Lingers but the Policies Fade Fast

news.abstract: Sec of State Madeleine K Albright fails to convince Russia's Foreign Min Igor S Ivanov during Moscow visit to accept new American missile defense system proposed by Pres Clinton year ago; Russians remain wary of American assertions that threat from nations such as North Korea, Iran and Iraq is real and justifies amending cold war's basic arms control treaty to allow building limited national missile defense system (M)
news.title: Russians Wary of U.S. Pitch For Missile Defense System
Chancellor to Review All Superintendents
C.I.A. Inquiry of Its Ex-Director Was Stalled at Top, Report Says
Mannesmann Said to Weigh Dropping Opposition to Vodafone Bid
Refusing to Coast on Familiar Songs and Arias
Merrill Lynch Is Set to Move Into Banking

news.abstract: Roger Cohen analysis holds that European Union demonstrated its abrupt development into serious political force when it demanded that Austria keep party of Jorg Haider, rightist politician, out of government (M)
news.title: If Democracy Is Not Enough

news.abstract: Indonesian Gen Wiranto denies that he was responsible for human rights abuses in East Timor and sidesteps suggestion by Pres Abdurrahman Wahid that he resign (M)
news.title: Indonesian General Denies Guilt in Timor Abuses

news.abstract: House votes, 341 to 70, to expand military ties between Taiwan and US, move that China and Clinton administration warn could aggravate regional tensions and jeopardize landmark trade agreement; critics say bill will upset Washington's 'one China' policy, which treats Taiwan as part of China and recognizes Beijing as China's capital, but also allows US to provide Taiwan with defensive weaponry; senior Republicans, led by Rep Tom Delay, choose security measure as first major bill for floor consideration this year precisely because it will challenge China (M)
news.title: HOUSE APPROVES EXPANSION OF TIES TO TAIWAN'S ARMY

news.abstract: White House officials say that US will consider joining European Union in diplomatically isolating Austria now that Freedom Party, which espouses anti-immigrant platform, and People's Party have agreed to form coalition government (M)
news.title: U.S. Will Reconsider Ties If Haider Joins Coalition

news.abstract: Chechen rebels say they are abandoning Grozny and will carry out attacks on Russian forces from mountains and countryside of breakaway republic; map; photo (M)
news.title: Chechen Rebels Announce Retreat From Battered Capital

news.abstract: Sec of State Madeleine K Albright visits Zagreb, Croatia, and praises government of Prime Min Ivica Racan; says US will support integration of 'new Croatia' into NATO, European Union and West; photo (M)
news.title: Albright Visits Post-Tudjman Croatia and Hails the New Leadership

news.abstract: China protests vote in US House of Representatives to expand military ties with Taiwan, calling it 'serious encroachment on China's sovereignty' (M)
news.title: House Vote on Aid to Taiwan Angers China

news.abstract: British and Irish leaders and Ulster politicians are working feverishly in desperate effort to save new Northern Ireland government from being shut down by dispute over paramilitary disarmament (M)
news.title: In 3 Capitals, Leaders Seek Ulster Solution

news.abstract: ASIA    INDIA: 3 DIE IN JAYALALITHA PROTEST  At least three students were burned to death in Madras when supporters of the power broker Jayalalitha Jayaram, who earlier in the day was convicted on public corruption charges, began burning buses in protest. Jayalalitha, as she is known, is a former actress who became the chief minister of the state of Tamil Nadu. Sentenced to a year in prison, she remains free on bond pending an appeal.   Barry Bearak (NYT)    INDIA: CONFESSION REPORTED  Dara Singh, the accused murderer of an Australian missionary, Graham Staines, and his two sons, has confessed to that crime as well as the killing of a Muslim businessman, according to police officials. Mr. Singh was arrested in a forest hideout after a manhunt lasting more than a year.   Barry Bearak (NYT)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Adrian Lajous Martinez, finance official in Mexico who resigned his cabinet post in 1982 to protest nationalization of the banks, died on Jan 24 at age 79 (M)
news.title: Adrian Lajous, 79, Opponent Of Mexico's Nationalized Banks

news.abstract: Britain moves to suspend power-sharing government in Northern Ireland by next week, but says it will intensify efforts to get paramilitary groups to begin disarming before using that authority; Northern Ireland Sec Peter Mandelson, speaking to somber session of House of Commons, says he will introduce emergency legislation to establish power to shut down two-month-old government and restore direct rule from London (M)
news.title: Britain to Retake Reins of Ulster If I.R.A. Doesn't Move to Disarm

news.abstract: Two American warships enforcing United Nations sanctions against Iraq seize Russian tanker in Persian Gulf after boarding it and discovering evidence that it might be smuggling oil out of southern Iraq (S)
news.title: U.S. Seizes Russia Tanker Said to Carry Oil From Iraq

news.abstract: Austrian Pres Thomas Klestil announces that he will swear in new government on Feb 4 that includes Jorg Haider's anti-immigrant Freedom Party, setting country on collision course with European Union, which regards Haider's party as xenophobic and extremist; Klestil's decision bows to logic of Austrian democracy in that Freedom Party and mainstream conservative People's Party led by Wolfgang Schussel won enough seats in October to govern; but it also gives stature of government office to a rightist party that has not hesitated to employ bigotry and vitriol; photo of Klestil, Haider and Schussel (M)
news.title: RIGHTISTS TO JOIN AUSTRIA'S CABINET

news.abstract: Two struggles are under way in Chechnya: fierce fight between Russian military and thousands of rebels, and more subtle tug of war between Russian high command and nation's media; every day Russia's journalists do battle with military press service, which regulates access to battlefield and is determined to put out message that Kremlin's war is going according to plan (M)
news.title: Muzzle Chafes Chechen War Media

news.abstract: EUROPE    ITALY: ELECTION REFORM VOTE -- The constitutional court gave the go-ahead to seven referendums between April and June, including one that its supporters say would end political instability by abolishing election by proportional representation to a quarter of the seats in Parliament's 630-member lower house. In a vote last April, some 90 percent favored doing away with proportional representation. But the ballot was declared void when the turnout reached only 49.6 percent.   Elisabetta Povoledo
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: United Nations' new chief arms insepctor for Iraq, Hans Blix, says his inspection teams will not force their way into suspected weapons sites in Iraq but would defer to UN headquarters to resolve any confrontations; Blix's intention to bring inspection system into closer alliance with UN bureaucracy differs from his predecessors, who kept their operations largely independent (M)
news.title: Arms Inspector Seeks Bigger U.N. Role in Iraq

news.abstract: Ten million Russians, including one million in St Petersburg, still live in Soviet-era communal flats, makeshift cubicles crammed with people and utterly devoid of privacy; residents share bathrooms, hallways and common kitchen; they are mired in communal milieu by inertia, lack of choice and outright poverty; photos; diagram (M)
news.title: Tight Space. No Privacy. Soviet Decor.

news.abstract: Jakarta, Indonesia, has been swept by rumors of coup since special commission recommended indictment of most prominent general, Wiranto, as one of officers responsible for carnage in East Timor last year; Wiranto has proclaimed his innocence and ignored Pres Abdurrahman Wahid's requst to resign his cabinet post; Defense Min Juwono Sudarsono says he has been instructed by president to ask Wiranto directly to step down; issue will have to wait until Wahid returns from trip abroad; Gen Tyasno Sudarto, army commander, says standoff has created dangerous situation but that he is lobbying with his men not to stage coup; photo (M)
news.title: Indonesia Army Chief Says He Opposes a Coup

news.abstract: Former Prime Min Yevgeny M Primakov takes himself out of running in Mar 26 presidential election; says Russia still has long way to go before becoming civil society and true democracy; Primakov was shoved onto sidelines when Vladimir V Putin became acting president after Boris Yeltsin's resignation on Dec 31; Putin has soared in polls and he now is expected to win presidential election (M)
news.title: Ex-Premier Primakov Drops Out Of Presidential Race in Russia

news.abstract: Pres Thabo Mbeki, addressing South African Parliament in his first state of the nation speech, vows to relax restrictive labor laws, speed pace of privatization and reduce spending in bloated public sector; Mbeki highlights country's brightening economic fortunes and warns that he will not allow organized labor to threaten continued growth; labor has long supported Mbeki's African National Congress but opposes its fiscally conservative policies; Mbeki's remarks are clearly made with eye to investors abroad, who have complained about South Africa's tough labor laws, which make it difficult to transfer, reassign or fire employees; unemployment stands at nearly 40 percent (M)
news.title: South African Leader Warns Unions Not to Impede Development

news.abstract: Prime Min Ivica Racan's new Croatian government moves to keep its promises of social equality and justice, with plans to cut official salaries by 40 percent and to arrest former Cabinet Min Ivan Herak and tycoon Miroslav Kutle for embezzlement; Racan says economic situation is worse than he imagined after nine years of rule by party of late Pres Franjo Tudjman (M)
news.title: Economic Problems Hinder Croatia's Effort at Changes

news.abstract: Clinton administration's $1.3 billion plan to help Colombia fight drug trafficking and leftist insurgents faces skepticism from military and law-enforcement officials concerned that United States could be dragged into long and costly struggle that may ultimately have little impact on drug trade; aid plan is intended to reduce booming production of cocaine and heroin in Colombia, strengthen government and help it take control of large part of its southern territory now dominated by rebels; senior American defense officials say privately that they worry that American military, while engaged in antidrug effort, may be dragged deeper into Colombia's 40-year-long civil war; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. ANTIDRUG PLAN TO AID COLOMBIA FACES SKEPTICISM

news.abstract: United Nations peacekeepers clash with Kosovo Albanians for second day in Mitrovica, pushing back angry crowds from bridge that divides city; two Albanians and eight soldiers are wounded in clash (M)
news.title: In Kosovo, More Clashes Between Peacekeepers and Albanians

news.abstract: Clashes between police and demonstrators leave over 50 people injured in Vienna after coalition government including members of Jorg Haider's anti-immgration Freedom Party is sworn in; photo (M)
news.title: Vienna Riots Leave 50 Hurt As Protests Rise

news.abstract: EgyptAir officials say Hamdi Hanafi Taha, pilot claiming to have information about crash of airline's Flight 990 last Oct, has requested asylum in Britain (M)
news.title: EgyptAir Pilot Seeking Asylum

news.abstract: Study by Human Rights Watch says NATO air campaign in Kosovo caused deaths of 500 civilians in 90 separate attacks, more than Pentagon has acknowledged but much lower than claimed by Yugoslavia; rejects any notion that NATO committed war crimes but argues that in waging war to halt Serbs from killing or driving out ethnic Albanians, alliance officials themselves violated Geneva Convention (M)
news.title: Rights Group Says NATO Killed 500 Civilians in Kosovo War

news.abstract: Mexican federal police seize main campus of National Autonomous University of Mexico in Mexico City, peacefully ending takeover by students that began in April 1999 in protest against plan to charge tuition for first time; arrest more than 600 students; Pres Ernesto Zedillo says action was taken after government concluded that leader of anarchic student movement would never agree to negotiated solution; photo (M)
news.title: A Peaceful Raid Ends Students' Long Siege in Mexico

news.abstract: Jorg Haider, rightist leader whose Freedom Party is part of new Austrian government, says ethnic Germans expelled from what was Czechoslovakia at end of World War II should be entitled to same compensation as Austrian Jews persecuted by Nazis; statement reopens old grievance among Germans; centers on expulsion from their homes or imprisonment in Soviet Union of millions of Germans in aftermath of Hitler's war and lack of compensation for their losses or suffering; remarks seem certain to intensify international unease over Haider, whose intermittently revisionist views have included statements--later apologized for--praising aspects of Hitler's rule (S)
news.title: Haider Opens Old Wound Over Germans Czechs Ousted

news.abstract: Fusae Ota, former civil servant from Prime Minister Keizo Obuchi's party, becomes first woman to win governorship in Japan in race that is regarded as important gauge of support for Obuchi; she won victory in Osaka, Japan's second largest prefecture (S)
news.title: First Woman Is Elected Governor in Japan

news.abstract: German prosecutors estimate more than $70 million was illegally paid in kickbacks to middlemen on sales of military and oil refinery equipment during tenure of former Chancellor Helmut Kohl, whose once glowing reputation has already been battered by revelations of secret party financing; findings--part of investigations in Germany, Switzerland and France--suggest possible corruption at highest levels of Kohl government potentially more damaging to Kohl than unrelated illegal party contributions he has already acknowledged; new allegations discussed; photo (M)
news.title: Big Kickbacks Under Kohl Reported

news.abstract: France gives school nurses right to dispense emergency contraception pills to students, becoming first country in world to do so; pills will be available at high schools and junior high schools, where students are as young as 12 years; although nurses are advised to make efforts to inform child's parents, they are not required to; French health and education officials hope policy will help reduce unwanted pregnancies and lower country's abortion rate, among highest in European Union; while measure faces opposition from some parents and family rights groups nationwide, its has found wide supporters in working-class city of Trappes on outskirts of Paris, where many of students come from North African immigrant families who rarely discuss sex with children; women's groups, abortion rights activists and some parents groups see it as major step toward making contraception more accessible to young people; map (M)
news.title: France Provides Morning-After Pill to Schoolgirls

news.abstract: UN Security Council increases peacekeeping force for Sierra Leone to 11,000 from about 6,000 and tells troops not to shrink from using weapons against brutal rebel army; expanded peacekeeping mission, approved unanimously, becomes organization's largest (S)
news.title: U.N. Increases Peacekeepers in Sierra Leone

news.abstract: Stipe Mesic is elected to succeed late Franjo Tudjman as president of Croatia; is former leader of collective presidency before Yugoslavia disintegrated in 1991; won 56.2 percent of vote, compared with 43.8 percent for rival, Drazen Budisa; photo (M)
news.title: Croatia Elects a Moderate To Follow the Tudjman Era

news.abstract: THE AMERICAS    CANADA: QUEBEC VOTE RULED OUT -- Premier Lucien Bouchard of Quebec gave a cold shoulder to separatist hard-liners at a Parti Quebecois convention, saying his party's main goal should be to win re-election before its mandate expires in 2003 rather than to hold a third referendum on independence. Previously, he promised to hold a vote on separation. But opinion polls indicate that support for independence and his separatist party have sagged to the 35-40 percent range.   James Brooke (NYT)    MEXICO: 745 ARRESTED -- A total of 745 people, including 83 minors, were arrested when the federal police took over the national university to end a nine-month student strike, justice officials said. Several dozen were released on bail but three strike leaders, Alejandro Echavarria, Alberto Pacheco and Mario Benitez, were charged with felony crimes and denied bail. More than 7,000 people joined a spontaneous march in Mexico City to demand the prisoners' release, a call echoed by many intellectuals and opposition leaders.   Julia Preston (NYT)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: KUALA TERENGGANU, Malaysia—  Side-by-side in the corridors of the state capital building here are men wearing flowing robes and pin-striped suits, turbans and silk ties.
news.title: Islamists' Policies Win Allies in Malaysia State

news.abstract: Opposition politicians end 11-day boycott of Japan's Parliament; drop their demand that Prime Min Keizo Obuchi apologize for pushing through without debate bill to reduce number of Parliament seats (S)
news.title: Accord Ends Boycott By Japan Opposition

news.abstract: Gen Augusto Pinochet's hopes of being freed from house arrest and allowed to return home to Chile suffer setback when British court says it will hear appeal of Britain's decision that he is not medically fit to stand trial on torture charges; six human rights groups and Belgium government are challenging Home Sec Jack Straw's refusal to make public examination of Pinochet in Jan by British doctors (M)
news.title: Pinochet Foes Are Granted An Appeal

news.abstract: Colleagues of Andrei Babitsky, Russian reporter for Radio Liberty, appeal for information about him five days after Russia announced that it had handed him over to Chechen rebels (M)
news.title: Friends Fear for Radio Reporter Still Missing in Chechnya

news.abstract: Over 150 passengers spend their third night aboard hijacked Afghan airliner, held prisoner at Stansted, England, airport by armed gang that perplexes police by giving no explanation for their seizure of plane or making any political demands; police say four members of flight crew escaped and one hostage was released on Feb 8 (M)
news.title: Hijackers Still Hold Jet, But Make No Demands

news.abstract: Mexican justice authorities, moving to blunt protests against police occupation of national university, free 654 of 745 people arrested in raid that ended nine-month student strike (M)
news.title: Mexican Police Release 654 Arrested in Raid on University

news.abstract: Tense standoff between police and hijackers of Afghan airliner at Stansted airport outside London ends peacefully with hijackers releasing 150 or so people aboard plane and surrendering to authorities; police say they have not identified hijackers and refuse to discuss their demands (M)
news.title: Hijacking Over; Everyone Safe On Afghan Jet

news.abstract: Austrian Chancellor Wolfgang Schussel, trying to calm foreign fears about his coalition with rightist Freedom Party, presents his government's platform to Parliament and says he wants to compensate people forced into slavery in Austrian factories during World War II (M)
news.title: Chancellor Proposes to Compensate Austria's Wartime Slaves

news.abstract: Chancellor Gerhard Schroder approves draft legislation that would slash taxes and open way for German corporations to sell off extensive cross-holdings that have tended to hinder rise of open competition and shareholders' culture (M)
news.title: Big Business In Line to Get Large Tax Cut From Schroder

news.abstract: Eight corruption cases have been filed against Jayalalitha Jayaram, former chief minister of Tamil Nadu, India; criminal court judge in Madras has been cataloging her jewelry collection for forthcoming trial (M)
news.title: India Politician's Jewels Glare at Her Latest Trial

news.abstract: Serbs in Mitrovica, Kosovo, say Serbian mobs that recently rampaged through city, intimidating Albanians and leaving eight dead, were reacting to grenade attack on Serbian cafe that wounded 15 young people; map; photo (M)
news.title: Serbs Nurse Rage After Attack in Kosovo City

news.abstract: Fighting in Lebanon subsides as people in northern Israel emerge from bomb shelters and US calls meeting of monitoring group to curb hostilities; Israel and Iranian-backed Hezbollah declare victory in latest round of violence, indication that it may be coming to end; photo (M)
news.title: Lebanon Fighting Ebbs in Claims of Victory

news.abstract: Information Center of Human Rights and Democratic Movement in China says at least 2,000 followers of banned Falun Gong spiritual movement have been detained in China in last week, official holiday period for Lunar New Year; says Tracy Zhao, Beijing-born US citizen who did not have her passport when she was arrested, remains in custody (M)
news.title: China Reportedly Detains 2,000 Members of Falun Gong Sect

news.abstract: French prosecutor Pierre Dintilhac asks that former Foreign Min Roland Dumas, his former mistress Christine Deviers-Joncour and six other people stand trial on corruption charges stemming from sex-and-kickback scandal involving former national oil company, Elf Aquitaine (M)
news.title: French Prosecutor Seeks Graft Trial for Ex-Foreign Minister

Warren Hoge (NYT)    BRITAIN: PASSPORTS FOR PETS -- Britain has begun allowing animals with ''pet passports'' proving that they are free of rabies to enter the country without having to spend six months in quarantine. The animals must be fitted with an identity microchip, and be vaccinated and tested by a licensed veterinarian to ensure that the vaccine is working. If there is no outbreak of rabies in Britain within the next year, the plan, which applies to dogs and cats traveling to Britain from 22 western European countries, will be expanded to include pets from the United States, Canada and the Caribbean.   Sarah Lyall (NYT)

news.abstract: PARIS—  Ever since queens and courtesans began to emphasize their necks with precious opalescent spheres, pearl necklaces have been every woman's best friend. In the 1930s, Coco Chanel wore her sumptuous rope of natural pearls — the token of a grand duke's affection — mixed with a cluster of costume jewelry, inventing a style that was to become a classic. In the '50s, their image became proper and ladylike. A few seasons ago, John Galliano triggered a new craze for pearls when he dressed up a Dior collection with spectacular pearl chokers.

Chancellor Gerhard Schroder's Social Democrats called Mr. Kohl's activity ''incredibly embarrassing.'' Parliament's compromise failed to satisfy Catholic bishops, who called the new law ''incomplete and ambiguous.''   Alessandra Stanley

news.abstract: China is engaged in desperate war on smuggling after years of tolerance that has long helped enrich country's prosperous southern provinces at expense of central government coffers, even with cooperation of local officials; campaign, devised to increase revenues and clean up government's tarnished image, resulted in 80 percent increase in tariff income in 1999; has proved to be exceedingly delicate balancing act in part because important regional economies are intertwined with smuggling, and because zealous pursuit of crime often ends up, embarrassingly, at Communist Party's own door; photo (M)
news.title: China's Fierce War on Smuggling Uproots a Vast Hidden Economy

news.abstract: Conditions in refugee camp in Chibuto, Mozambique, for thousands left homeless by calamitous flooding discussed; government's struggle to provide for victims finally begins as flood waters subside; UN reports 250,000 people live in 64 camps nationwide and another 250,000 in devastated villages; relief agencies say shortage of helicopters has made it impossible to deliver enough food and supplies; fear situation in country could worsen if heavy rains return to region, as forecast by South African Weather Bureau; photos; maps (M)

news.abstract: BRUSSELS—  Under a newly activist foreign ministry, Belgium has taken the lead in the European ostracism of Austria and other "moral" issues, seeking to erase its poor international reputation. But many political analysts here say the rhetoric about the rise of the far right in Austria has much to do with fears that an identical phenomenon may be on the rise here as well.
news.title: Belgian Stance on Austria Reflects Worry Over 'Haiderization' at Home

news.title: Colombia And Copters And Clash Over Choice

news.abstract: TOM GROGGIN, Australia—  Bouncing over rocks, the water in the Murray River near its source high in the forested mountains of southeast Australia has the same kind of crystal clarity as the call of the magpies and currawongs that echo through the air.
news.title: Pollution and Water Diversion Blot the Murray : In Downstream Australia, This River Is Running Dry

news.abstract: THE AMERICAS    CHILE: PINOCHET IMMUNITY CHALLENGED  Judge Juan Guzman Tapia requested that the Appeals Court revoke Gen. Augusto Pinochet's immunity so that he can proceed with indictments against the former dictator involving charges of torture, kidnappings and executions. Should the Appeals Court agree, General Pinochet's lawyers can be expected to appeal the decision to the Supreme Court. General Pinochet has been a Senator for Life, a position that grants him broad immunity from prosecution, since 1998.    Clifford Krauss (NYT)    MEXICO: TAKEOVER AT UNIVERSITY  About 60 hooded protesters carrying clubs and rocks took over the building that houses the offices of the president of the National Autonomous University of Mexico in Mexico City. The demonstrators, who broke windows and cut through steel bars to enter the building, demanded the release of dozens of students jailed after the police ended a 10-month strike at the university on Feb. 6.    Julia Preston (NYT)    EUROPE    RUSSIA: COURT RULES ON ZHIRINOVSKY  The Supreme Court ruled that the ultranationalist leader Vladimir Zhirinovsky must be allowed to run in presidential elections on March 26 despite alleged financial irregularities. Mr. Zhirinovsky had been barred from the race by the Central Election Committee for allegedly misreporting his assets. A court spokeswoman said the judge had not disclosed the reason for the reversal.   (AP)    RUSSIA: BLAIR TO VISIT  Prime Minister Tony Blair of Britain will on Friday become the first Western leader to visit Russia since Acting President Vladimir Putin took office. A spokesman for 10 Downing Street said the agenda includes Russia's military campaign in Chechnya. ''Nobody is pretending we like what is going on there,'' he said, adding that Mr. Blair will argue that ''these problems cannot be solved by force without a political process.''    Warren Hoge (NYT)    BRITAIN: 'RED KEN' BREAKS PLEDGE  Ken Livingstone, a Labor left winger known as ''Red Ken,'' defied Prime Minister Tony Blair by declaring himself an independent candidate for mayor of London. He acknowledged that he was breaking a pledge not to break ranks with his party but said that he was justified because the choice of the official Labor candidate in the May 4 election, former Health Secretary Frank Dobson, was ''rigged.'' Mr. Blair said Mr. Livingstone as mayor would be a ''a disaster in terms of crime and police and business.''    Warren Hoge (NYT)    SWITZERLAND: VOTE ON U.N.  Advocates of joining the United Nations have collected enough signatures -- more than 125,000 -- to force a popular vote on membership. The last effort, in 1986, was resoundingly defeated even though Geneva is the United Nation's European headquarters. A nationwide vote will be held within three years.    Elizabeth Olson (NYT)    SPAIN: REBELS SUSPECTED IN BOMBING  A car bomb exploded in the northern Basque city of San Sebastian, injuring two Civil Guard officers and three other people, Spanish news media reported. The blast, six days before the general elections on Sunday, was blamed on the separatist group E.T.A., which is also blamed for two car bombings since January that have killed three people.    Al Goodman (NYT)    GREECE: PROSTITUTES PROTEST  Some 200 prostitutes demonstrated in Athens, demanding that the Socialist government repeal a law barring renewal of their licenses that was intended to clear the city of brothels ahead of the 2004 Olympics. The prostitutes vowed to march to the Prime Minister's office on Tuesday to press their demands.    Anthee Carassava (NYT)    ASIA    VIETNAM: CELEBRATIONS BEGIN  Vietnam began two months of celebrations commemorating the 25th anniversary of the end of the Vietnam War, which came with the fall of Saigon on April 30, 1975. Washington and Hanoi normalized relations in June 1995 and William Cohen will become the first Defense Secretary to visit since the end of the war when he arrives on March 13 for talks on greater cooperation.   (AP)    INDIA: CLINTON'S ITINERARY  Ambassador Richard Celeste said President Clinton would visit New Delhi, Agra -- site of the Taj Mahal -- Jaipur, Hyderabad and Bombay on his visit to India from March 21 to 25. He will land in New Delhi on the evening of March 19, then fly to Dhaka, Bangladesh, the next day. The envoy said it was not clear yet whether the president would visit Pakistan.   Celia W. Dugger (NYT)    INDIA: COPING WITH TB  In India, where two million people develop tuberculosis each year and nearly 500,000 die from it, an intensive treatment program has saved more than 40,000 lives and achieved cure rates of more than 80 percent, according to a review by a team of 25 national and international experts.   Hari Kumar (NYT)    INDIA: DEATH ON THE ROADS  About 70,000 Indians die and more than one million are seriously hurt each year in road accidents caused by faulty vehicles, bad roads, improper traffic controls and other problems, according to Dinesh Mohan, secretary general of an Asian conference on injury prevention in New Delhi sponsored by the World Health Organization.P. J. Anthony (NYT)    INDONESIA: VIOLENCE IN ACEH  Soldiers burned down 15 shops, two houses and a village council office after searching unsuccessfully for insurgents as 27 families fled their homes in the strife-torn province of Aceh, authorities said. It was the latest in a string of violent outbursts in the oil-rich region on the northern tip of Sumatra, about 1,100 miles northwest of Jakarta. (AP)    MIDDLE EAST    YEMEN: POLE TELLS OF KIDNAPPING  Ambassador Krzysztof Suprowicz of Poland, who was kidnapped in Yemen on Wednesday and released unharmed on Sunday after being held for four days by armed tribesmen, told Polish public radio yesterday that he had gone on a hunger strike after he was abducted. ''The aim was to show to these proud and dignified people that they had no power over me and my body, that in fact it was me who would decide the end of the operation,'' he said. The ambassador was freed after the government deployed troops and issued an ultimatum to the hostage-takers, who had wanted to trade him for one of their leaders held by the government.   (Agence France-Presse)    IRAN: PRIVATIZATION BLOCKED  Parliament has endorsed a move by a clergy-based council to block President Mohammad Khatami's plan to revive the economy by ending a state monopoly on banks and major industries. The shift came after the Guardian Council, which reviews parliamentary legislation, rejected most privatization proposals under Mr. Khatami's five-year development plan as unconstitutional. (Reuters)    AFRICA    ZIMBABWE: MORE FARMS OCCUPIED  Squatters occupied at least 214 white-owned farms across Zimbabwe yesterday, defying orders by the police to return home. The squatters are angry about the rejection in February of a new Constitution that would have permitted seizure of white-owned farms without compensation. President Robert Mugabe plans to reintroduce the land provision in 30 days as an amendment to the current Constitution.   (AP)    RWANDA: AIDE AMBUSHED  An adviser to President Pasteur Bizimungu was killed in his car outside his home in the capital, Kigali. The adviser, Assiel Kabera, had been a prominent figure among survivors of the 1994 genocide -- in which at least 500,000 ethnic Tutsi and moderate Hutu were killed by Hutu extremists -- in western Rwanda.    Ian Fisher (NYT)    SUDAN: U.S. ENVOY VISITS  It was a ''mistake'' that Sudanese warplanes bombed a school last month, killing 14 children and a teacher in the rebel-controlled Nuba mountains, the nation's justice minister, Mustafa Osman Ismail, told the United States envoy to Sudan, Harry Johnston. Sudan is under criticism for the bombing of a hospital on March 1 that killed at least two people. Government planes yesterday dropped two bombs on the compound of the Irish aid group, Concern Worldwide, in southern Sudan.    Ian Fisher (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Gen Wesley K Clark, top NATO commander, wants United States to commit additional battalian of 700 to 800 soldiers for Kosovo to prevent Albanian raids across border into Serbia, but Pentagon balks at idea (M)
news.title: Pentagon Balks at Adding Kosovo Battalion

news.abstract: United States Secretary of State Madeleine K Albright will make a major overture to Iran on March 17 by announcing that Clinton administration will lift several sanctions on Tehran; administration officials say she will also acknowledge that United States was shortsighted in its support for Iraq during Iran-Iraq war and its involvement in 1953 coup in Iran (M)
news.title: Major Overture Toward Iran Expected in Speech by Albright

news.abstract: North Korea, in space of a few short weeks, has gone from one of world's most politically reclusive states to most diplomatically ambitious; with little fanfare, but with speed that has surprised many people, Communist government in Pyongyang has established diplomatic relations with Italy and has resumed diplomatic discussions with Japan and Australia for first time in years (M)
news.title: Suddenly, Reclusive North Korea Reaches Out to the World

news.abstract: Japan seeks extradition from Lebanon five Japanese Red Army terrorists who were involved in massacre at Israel's international airport near Lod on May 30, 1972; terrorists were sentenced to life in prison by Israel, but they were released by Israel in 1985 in prisoner exchange with Palestinians in 1985; they have been in prison in Lebanon for three years for living on forged passports; Japan wants to extradite Mariko Yamamoto, one of terrorists, to face trial for terrorism and acts against the state at home, and Lebanon, bowing to popular feelings, rejects Japanese request; photo of Red Army terrorists (L)
news.title: Fate of 5 Terrorists Hangs Between Japan and Lebanon

news.abstract: Russia's regional newspapers are increasingly under thumb of local authorities; this has not escaped attention of Acting Pres Vladimir V Putin, passionate advocate of building a strong federal state in a Russia whose vast and distant lands have slipped from the authority that Moscow enjoyed in Soviet times; one of Putin's first decrees as acting pres authorizes federal subsidies to 2,500 local newspapers, including 19 provincial newspapers; photo (M)
news.title: A Russian Press Beholden to Many

news.abstract: Rev Andrei Davydov is using his art to finance restoration of 12th century church in Pskov, one of oldest cities in all Russia; Cathedral of the Nativity of St John the Baptist, which dates to 1124, was in shambles when Russian Orthodox patriarchate regained it in 1991; Rev Davydov, who has worldwide reputation for his painted icons, now accepts commissions from other churches to pay for his church's repairs and rebuilding; photos; map (M)
news.title: A Calling of Faith and Art in a Russian Church

news.abstract: Judge in Zimbabwe rules in favor of white farmers, saying black squatters on their farms are breaking law; squatters, veterans of Zimbabwe's war of independence, had invaded hundreds of farms to speed pace of land reforms; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Fall of two Indian governments and nuclear tests of May 1998 have conspired against Pres Clinton's long-held desire to visit India; Clinton will embark on five-day, five-city journey to India, and five-hour stop in Pakistan, at time when tensions on subcontinent are high; confrontation between two countries over kashmir is seen as most likely dispute on earth to spark nuclear clash; Clinton hope his trip can somehow defuse situation in Kashmir, although he and his aides are pessimistic about chances for actual progress; Clinton aides fear that original intention of trip, to display India as economic and strategic power of region, will be undermined by increasingly strong-willed attitude of Indian government toward nuclear weapons, Pakistan and Kashmir (M)
news.title: Ambition Turns to Crisis Control as Clinton Visits the Subcontinent

news.abstract: Angela Merkel, who is about to become leader of Germany's Christian Democrats, will be first woman to head major German party; change she represents is greater than gender: it is religious, generational, moral and geographical; Germany is reaching out for entirely new political blood amid financial scandal that has engulfed Christian Democrats and tarnished reputation of Helmut Kohl, who has admitted accepting more than $1 million in illegal payments; photo (M)
news.title: A Political Newcomer Breaks Rules in Germany

news.abstract: India dresses itself up for its first visit from American president in more than two decades; during Pres Clinton's visit, world's largest democracy and its most powerful one will again try to build alliance that has eluded them for half-century; photos (M)
news.title: In Clinton, India Sees a Bridegroom

news.abstract: Illiteracy, sickness and hunger still prevail in India's rural villages like Sheri Ram Reddy Guda, less than 50 miles from software technology park being created in Hyderabad; chasm between India's educated elite and its impoverished multitudes worries economists, politicians and some software entrepreneurs; optimists believe the Internet will eventually help India address problems like illiteracy, but others fear that the boom may be distracting India from its chronic problems and leaving the poor further behind; photos; map (M)
news.title: India's Unwired Villages Mired in the Distant Past

news.abstract: Coming visit to Israel by Pope John Paul II is freighted with multiple layers of sensitivities, and each stop on his carefully negotiated itinerary means different things to different people with different agenda; Vatican seeks to accommodate Israeli and Palestinian demands in equal measure; photo (L)
news.title: The Holy Land, in an Edgy Mood, Awaits the Pope's Visit

news.abstract: Acting Pres Vladimir V Putin assures Russian voters that war in Chechnya is drawing to a close and that some Russian troops will soon be on their way home; Press Ministry demands that rebels leaders in separatist southern region of Chechnya be denied air time on Russian television and radio stations; those commanders' defiant comments in the media would be an unpleasant reminder that a Russian victory is not yet at hand (M)
news.title: Russian Chief Sees an End To Resistance By Chechens

news.abstract: Taiwanese election is a huge defeat for Nationalist Party, which in 20th century controlled first China and then Taiwan and which presided over the emergency of the very democratic forces that ultimately upended it (M)
news.title: Party Undone by Liberty It Nurtured

news.abstract: Nicolas Hardy Walter, influential British anarchist, atheist and humanist, dies at age 65 (M)
news.title: Nicolas H. Walter Dies at 65; Feisty Atheist and Anarchist

news.abstract: Victory by pro-independence party in Taiwan's presidential elections forces many mainland Chinese to reflect for first time on depth of their convictions, pitting abstract belief that return of Taiwan is manifest destiny, against their personal self-interest, since war would mean renewed hardship in country that has only recently raised living standards (M)
news.title: Deep Feeling That Taiwan Is China's Is Put to Test

news.abstract: Rabbi Ovadia Yosef, spiritual leader of Israel's powerful Shas political party, issues blistering and vehement attack in televised sermon against leftist education minister, Yossi Sarid; is incensed over Sarid's perceived attacks against parochial school system, which forms party's political base (S)
news.title: Powerful Israeli Rabbi Steps Up Attacks Over Parochial Schools

news.abstract: Pres Clinton, who will be first American president to visit Bangdladesh, will find country that is still one of world's poorest with per capita income of $289, but one in decidedly in less of mess with poverty rate drifting down and economic growth rates inching up; many Bangladeshi officials express wariness over visit; fear Clinton may be more interested in making deals to exploit country's significant reserves of natural gas than in fostering friendship; map; photos (M)
news.title: Shards of Misery, Not Far From Clinton Stop in Bangladesh

news.abstract: Ford Motor Co plans layoffs of more than 1,000 workers at giant assembly plant in Dagenham, England, and may close entire factory; says pound's strength relative to euro has made it expensive to manufacture in Britain for sale in Europe (S)
news.title: Ford Plans Job Cuts At Plant in England

news.abstract: Unprecedented security preparations by Israel and Palestinian Authority for Pope John Paul II's upcoming six-day visit to the Holy Land discussed; visit has required unparalleled cooperation between two governments, which despite minor sniping of Jerusalem officials on both sides, has gone smoothly; photo (M)
news.title: Holy Land Jitters Heighten Security for Papal Visit

news.abstract: Peru's Pres Alberto K Fujimori, slipping in polls and besieged by international criticism over presidential campaign irregularities, is courting indigenous Indians in flurry of pork-barrel politics; growing number of political experts say for all his efforts he may not win outright majority needed to avert runoff against Alejandro Toledo, probably strongest candidate he has ever faced among poor Indian voters; his image of invincibility has been damaged in recent weeks by widespread perception that he has lost control of election campaign and that election process is badly flawed; photo (M)
news.title: Slipping in Polls, Fujimori Courts Peru's Indians

news.abstract: Band of suspected militants massacre 34 Sikh men in village in Indian state of Kashmir on eve of Pres Clinton's state visit to India, which Clinton had hoped would help bring peace in violence-torn Kashmir; police blame Urdu-speaking foreign mercenaries participating in Pakistan-sponsored efforts to undermine and end rule by India (S)
news.title: 34 Massacred In Sikh Town In Kashmir

news.abstract: While China, US and most countries worldwide hold that Taiwan is part of China, its connections with mainland historically have been tenuous; island's relationship with China, dating back to 1683, discussed (S)
news.title: The Murky Tale of Taiwan: Island With an Unruly Past

news.abstract: UN Human Rights Commission, which opens annual meeting on March 21, faces crowded docket of supposed violations by number of countries, including China and Russia; US will introduce resolution criticizing China for deteriorating human rights, including crackdown on Falun Gong spiritual movement; commission may be forced to tackle Russia's actions in Chechnya (S)
news.title: U.N. to Review Human Rights Of 2 Big Powers

news.abstract: Colombia's minister of defense, Luis Fernando Ramirez Acuna, reports significant decline in human rights violations by country's armed forces, despite reports by State Department and human rights groups to contrary (S)
news.title: Colombian Military, in Report, Says Its Rights Abuses Are Down

news.abstract: LONDON—  The history of Labour governments in Britain has largely been one of economic crises: budget and balance of payments deficits, devaluations, even a bailout by the International Monetary Fund.
news.title: British Boom Lets Tax Cuts Be the Topic Of Contention

news.abstract: NATO Sec Gen Lord Robertson, one year after alliance began its 78-day bombardment of Kosovo, issues report highlighting what he says are unsung accomplishments of campaign; cites resettling of 1.3 million refugees, reopening of hundreds of schools and drastic reduction in crime (M)
news.title: NATO Secretary General's Report Claims Successes in Kosovo

news.abstract: Ramon Mitra, who rose from rural poverty to become leading politician and democratic foe of Marcos dictatorship in Philippines, dies at age 72; photo (M)
news.title: Ramon Mitra, 72, Foe of Marcos Regime During Martial Law

news.abstract: $9 billion spending bill to help Colombia combat drug traffickers and to pay for US military operations in Kosovo is imperiled because of opposition from Sen Trent Lott and fiscal conservatives in House and Senate (M)
news.title: Senate Fight Snags Aid Bill For Kosovo And Colombia

news.abstract: Taiwan stock market jumps 5.5 percent on March 21, more than making up for its 2.6 percent loss on March 20 following victory of opposition leader Chen Shui-bian in presidential election (M)
news.title: Taiwan Market Shakes Off Vote Results

news.abstract: Diplomats say Pres Clinton's scheduled meeting with Pres Hafez al-Assad of Syria could lay groundwork for renewed talks between Syria and Israel, but that peace deal is by no means imminent; Government-controlled Syrian newspapers are calling Assad's meeting with Clinton, in Geneva, a 'last chance' overture to Israel to pledge full Israeli withdrawal from Golan Heights; Israel, under Prime Min Ehud Barak, insists on knowing what kind of peace it will obtain before it agrees unilaterally to withdrawal (M)
news.title: Assad Meeting With Clinton Could Renew Peace Talks

news.abstract: THE AMERICAS    CANADA: SMOKING BAN VOIDED  British Columbia's Supreme Court struck down one of the toughest anti-smoking rules in the country, a total ban on smoking in bars and restaurants. The court ruled that the provincial Workers' Compensation Board had not adequately consulted with the public before imposing the rule on Jan. 1. The ban resulted in hundreds of layoffs from bars and restaurants, and prompted one rural city to try to join neighboring Alberta.   James Brooke (NYT)    MEXICO: U.S. MILITARY WELCOMED  The chairman of the joint chiefs of staff, Gen. Henry H. Shelton, received an unusually warm welcome from the armed forces during a two-day visit. The defense minister, Gen. Enrique Cervantes Aguirre, decorated him with one of the country's highest military medals, saying he had ''distinguished himself for his respect for our country and its men in arms.'' Mexico's military long regarded the United States as a potential invader, but in recent years the two countries have cooperated in the drug war.   Julia Preston (NYT)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Analysis of Pres Clinton's skillful address to Indian Parliament, during which he managed to entertain, flatter and inspire much of country's political leadership, even as he tactfully told them things they would rather not have heard--including United States's disapproval of India's decision to test nuclear weapons in 1998; Clinton seems to be making headway in convincing Indians that US genuinely wants to befriend them, and Clinton mania has seized press as well as ordinary Indians (M)
news.title: Clinton Fever: A Delighted India Has All the Symptoms

news.abstract: Pres Lee Teng-hui of Taiwan, whose governing Nationalist Party was dealt humiliating electoral defeat, has reportedly agreed to step down as chairman of party; Lee is expected to name Vice Pres Lien Chan, losing Nationalist candidate, as chairman of new reform committee, which will run party as Nationalists cast about for new leaders to revive their discredited party; Lee will remain president until May 20, when he is succeeded by Chen Shui-bian, but losing party chairmanship will deprive him of much of his power (M)
news.title: Taiwan's President Is Expected to Quit Party Post Soon

news.abstract: Pope John Paul II's first visit to Israel and Palestinian territories is officially a personal pilgrimage, but he also comes as head of state who has sought to persuade leaders on both sides that he is crucial temporal ally; to Israeli admirers, he is first pope to extend full recognition to their country; for Palestinian leaders, he is pope who began his papacy by telling United Nations in 1979 of need for settlement of Palestinian question (M)
news.title: Visit Casts Pope as Ally To 2 Sides In Mideast

news.abstract: Vice Admiral Charles Moore, American coordinator of international fleet that patrols waters off Iraq, tells Security Council committee that steeply rising oil prices have brought huge increase in smuggling of Iraqi oil; diplomats say, after briefing, that Moore tells committee on sanctions against Iraq that much of oil passes through Iranian water; Moore reportedly says that at current rates of oil shipments, Iraq could eaarn up to billion dollars this year in illegal sales; diplomats say profits go directly to Pres Saddam Hussein or those he chooses to reward (S)
news.title: Smuggling of Iraqi Oil Is Rising, U.N. Is Told

news.abstract: Senior Clinton administration officials say that Iraq has spent tens of millions of dollars in recent months to build military headquarters for an Iranian opposition group that administration considers a terrorist orgn; officials say Iraqis have used profits from illegal sale of oil to build complex for exclusive use of People's Mujahedeen, Iranian military and political movement whose goal is to overthrow Islamic Republic of Iran (M)
news.title: Iraq Builds Base for Rebels Fighting Iran, U.S. Contends

news.abstract: EUROPE    NORTHERN IRELAND: TRIMBLE CHALLENGED -- David Trimble will face a bid to oust him as leader of the Ulster Unionists at a meeting of the party council in Belfast tomorrow from a fierce opponent of the peace accord. Mr. Trimble will be challenged by the Rev. Martin Smyth, above, a former grand master of the militantly Protestant Orange Order. The move threatens further damage to the pact, now stalemated over paramilitary arms.   Warren Hoge (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Mrs Edith Tzirer, Holocaust survivor, is overcome with emotion at Pope John Paul's appearance at Yad Vashem Holocaust memorial, saying she had waited 54 years to thank Pope in person for saving her life in 1945 in small town near Cracow, Poland; photo (M)
news.title: Tears of Gratitude, Remembering Poland

news.abstract: Profile of and interview with Ella Pamfilova, only woman in field of 11 in Russia's presidential election on March 26; photo (M)
news.title: Lagging Happily In Russian Race

news.abstract: Polita Grau, who helped to spirit thousands of children out of Castro's Cuba, and who then spent 14 years in Cuban jail, accused of being CIA conspirator, dies at age of 84; photos (M)
news.title: Polita Grau, 84; Headed Effort On Behalf of Cuban Children

news.abstract: Pres Clinton visits tuberculosis clinic in Hyderabad, India, where he calls for intensified efforts to control epidemic and to find vaccine that will prevent it; estimated two million people develop tuberculosis each year in India, more than in any other country, and about 450,000 die from it; strategy for coping with disease, which administers special regimen and monitors patients over six- to eight-month period, has been used effectively by government since 1993, but is only available to about 15 percent of population of one billion; has doubled cure rates to 84 percent and cut death rates to 4 percent from 29 percent (M)
news.title: India Wins Battles in Its War on TB, but It Has a Long Way to Go

news.abstract: Pakistanis are uneasy over Pres Clinton's upcoming visit, fearing he will deliver scolding in scheduled television address to nation; many are scornful of Clinton's recent visit to India, where he was warmly greeted, notably in Indian Parliament; Clinton will carry message of 'hard realities;' will tell chief executive Gen Pervez Musharraf country is in trouble and that nuclear-arms race with India would be ruinous folly (M)
news.title: Pakistanis Are Uneasy Over Clinton's Visit

news.abstract: Northern Ireland peace agreement faces crucial vote on March 25 as members of Ulster Unionists decide whether to keep David Trimble as leader or return party to hardline past; 850-member party council will vote on leadership challenge by Rev Martin Smyth, former grand master of militant Protestant Orange Order (S)
news.title: Showdown on Irish Pact in Today's Unionist Vote

news.abstract: Russia's state-owned television broadcasts reports that Grigory A Yavlinsky, leading challenger to Acting Pres Vladimir V Putin, is supported by Jews, homosexuals and foreigners; prime-time reports by ORT television are intended to exploit anti-Semitism, homophobia and suspicion of foreigners that still pervade Russian society, as well as its enthusiasm for conspiracy theories; Yavlisnky, who is running distant third in field of 11 candidates, stands to siphon most votes from Putin; poses greatest danger to Putin's chances of winning mandate in first round of voting; Putin implores Russians to go to polls and to pick leader who can restore country's prestige; photos (M)
news.title: State TV Ties a Putin Rival To Jews, Gays and Foreigners

news.abstract: David Trimble holds off surprisingly strong challenge to his leadership of Northern Ireland's Ulster Unionist Party, but emerges with his authority and his room to maneuver in conducting peace negotiations diminished; strong vote for Rev Martin Smyth indicates deepening division over going forward with Apr 1998 peace agreement and sharing power with Catholic minority; delegates say they were particularly angered by Trimble's suggestion in Washington on March 17 that he would be willing to take party back into government with Sinn Fein without prior disarmament of Irish Republican Army (M)
news.title: Ulster Leader Holds On, but Power Lessens in Unionist Vote

news.abstract: Police in Uganda say at least some of 153 people who were killed at secluded compound of Movement for the Restoration of Ten Commandments of God died several weeks before hundreds of followers of doomsday cult died in raging inferno in their church week ago; say fire at compound gutted five small dwellings and scorched much of surrounding earth in eerie prelude to catastrophe that unfolded in Kanungu, where cult made its home; there is growing sense that what happened at compound and in church was carefully orchestrated act by cult's leader, Joseph Kibwetere, and some of his lieutenants, whose whereabouts are unknown (M)
news.title: Evidence Indicates Uganda Cult Held an Eerie Prelude to Fire

news.abstract: Pollsters say Russians clearly want Vladimir V Putin to be elected president, although Putin's intentions remain, so far, largely blank slate; Putin's brief campaign has cast him as all things to all people: brutal warrior against Chechens, dog lover who cries at funerals, supporter of basic rights, supporter of crackdown on politically unruly journalists; Putin has managed to remain remarkably popular because he has religiously shunned any one ideology; beyond war in Chechnya, gamble that paid off royally among voters, Putin's actual policies have been few and uncontroversial; photo; map (M)
news.title: Russians Vote Under the Spell of Putin's Many Promises

news.abstract: Pope John Paul II is cheered by mixed local crowd of Muslims and Christians in ancient city of Nazareth; he visits Basilica of Annunciation, largest Roman Catholic church in Middle East; Muslims have received approval from Israeli government to build mosque in plaza in front of basilica, decision that has been source of tension in town; photo (M)
news.title: Rifts Fall Away at Shrine of Annunciation

news.abstract: OPEC ministers arriving in Vienna for meeting show few signs of support for big increase in oil production that Clinton administration has asked for to relieve high oil prices; grueling negotations are expected among members, who appear to be divided over issue (M)
news.title: OPEC Gives Scant Signs That Oil Flow Will Increase

news.abstract: Mexican prosecutors say they have overwhelming evidence, collected over past two years, that governing Institutional Revolutionary Party leaders engaged in schemes to divert millions of dollars through dummy bank accounts, including three set up under names of two maids and gardener of top party official; Horacio del Norte, party leader in Nuevo Leon, Monterrey State, has admitted using public money for party purposes and state treasurer Xavier Doria Gonzalez, has been jailed for embezzlement and has informed on seven other leaders; map; photo (M)
news.title: Mexico's Ruling Party Accused of Diverting Public Money

news.abstract: News analysis of victory by Vladimir V Putin in Russia's presidential election; likely impact on US-Russian relations assessed; photo (M)
news.title: Washington Nail-Biting

news.abstract: Interview with Kuwaiti oil minister Sheik Saud Nasser al-Sabah; he voices displeasure over US pressure to raise production quotas as oil and gasoline prices have soared in recent months (M)
news.title: Kuwaitis Are Exasperated By America's Oil Politics

news.abstract: JAKARTA—  For someone who has lived three decades in a cramped neighborhood of this sprawling capital, Tuminah, a middle-aged woman, remains keenly in touch with nature.
news.title: City-Wide Crisis / Overhauling the Pipe Network : Jakarta Lays the Groundwork for Clean Water

news.abstract: Pres Clinton meets with Syrian Pres Hafez al-Assad in Geneva and fails to persuade him to moderate differences with Israel; White House says it is impossible to predict when talks between Israel and Syria will resume; quick end to meeting with Assad dashes Clinton's hopes of presiding over comprehensive peace deal that would incorporate Syria, Palestinians and Israel before he leaves office; failure is met with despair by diplomats on both sides; photo; map (M)
news.title: CLINTON'S EFFORT FAILS TO GET SYRIA TO RESUME TALKS

news.abstract: Amnesty International issues sharply worded report accusing government of Saudi Arabia of widespread human rights abuses, including arbitrary arrests, torture of detainees and barring of prisoner access to family members or lawyers; Saudi government emphatically rejects findings as biased and inaccurate (M)
news.title: Saudi Arabia Bridles as Rights Group Charges Widespread Abuses

news.abstract: Interior Min Natan Sharansky says he will restore to Israeli Arab village of Kafr Kassem part of its land that was taken decades ago to develop neighboring Jewish town; move and its far-reaching implications discussed; map (M)
news.title: Israel Says It Will Restore Seized Land to Arab Village

news.abstract: Vladimir V Putin, Russia's president-elect, meets with cabinet day after decisive victory in presidential election; urges it to prepare 'weighty' economic plan; is congratulated by number of prominent world leaders, including Pres Clinton, British Prime Min Tony Blair and Chinese Pres Jiang Zemin; won 53 percent of vote; photo (M)
news.title: Putin Tells Advisers to Prepare 'Weighty' Economic Plan

news.abstract: Senior Clinton administration official says Syrian Pres Hafez al-Assad was immovable during his meeting with Pres Clinton in Geneva, and appears to have arrived with misconception that Mr. Clinton was in position to give him what he wanted from Israel; says administration knew meeting was gamble but believed it had better chance of success than proved to be case; photo (M)
news.title: In Geneva, Clinton Bet That Assad Would Bend, and Lost

news.abstract: Political discord resumes in Israel following visit by Pope John Paul II; Israelis are pessimistic and anxious as prospects for peace with Syria have diminished, as government opens politically explosive criminal investigation of leading Rabbi Ovadia Yosef and amid five separate Parliament votes of no confidence in government; Yosef, who attacked Education Minister Yossi Sarid in recent sermon, is accused of 'praising or encouraging violence' as well as insulting public employee and slander (M)
news.title: As Pope Exits, Israel Resumes Usual Discord

news.abstract: Bao Tong, former senior Chinese official who spent seven years in prison for sympathizing with democracy advocates, challenges authorities to abide by the Constitution and stop restricting his freedom to speak out; photo (M)
news.title: Ex-Official Challenges China's Limits on Speech

news.abstract: OPEC decides to increase oil production without the participation of its second-largest producer, Iran, but the increase, 1.45 million barrels a day, is less than the 2.5 million urged by US; Iran's irritation at US pressures is apparently one reason behind its opposition to any increase; experts estimate that it will take at least six to eight weeks before any additional oil production finds its way to the gasoline pumps; Clinton administration remains optimistic, citing additional production it expects from non-OPEC producers; graph; photos (M)
news.title: WITH IRAN BALKING, OPEC NATIONS PLAN TO SELL MORE OIL

news.abstract: Israeli police recommend that former Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu and his wife, Sara, face criminal prosecution on charges of bribery, fraud and the theft of $100,000 worth of gifts to the state; Netanyahu says charges are baseless, and his lawyer says he welcomes the trial; photo (M)
news.title: Israeli Police Urge Prosecution of Netanyahu and Wife

news.abstract: KUALA LUMPUR—  The prime minister of Malaysia, Mahathir bin Mohamad, delivered unusually firm words on the importance of democracy Tuesday in a meeting with Pakistan's military leader, General Pervez Musharraf.
news.title: On Southeast Asia Tour,Musharraf Hears StrongWords on Civilian Rule : Mahathir Presses Pakistani on Democracy

news.abstract: Turkish Parliament is about to begin delicate work of deciding whether to re-elect President Suleyman Demirel, who is maneuvering to arrange a constitutional amendment that would allow him to serve for another five years; re-election is certain if amendment wins; his supporters say Demirel is a guarantee of stability as Turkey enters a decade that is likely to bring wrenching domestic and international changes; critics view him as symbol of country's political immobility (M)
news.title: Turkey to Say if Leader Can Seek 2nd Term

news.abstract: Pres-elect Chen Shui-bian of Taiwan chooses departing Nationalist defense minister, Tang Fei, as prime minister in his government, which takes office on May 20; Tang's appointment may help persuade Beijing that Chen does not intend to make radical changes in policy toward mainland (S)
news.title: Nationalist Named Taiwan's Prime Minister

news.abstract: Spain is increasingly a magnet for Africans hoping to find jobs in Europe; Spanish police boats regularly patrol Mediterranean, in hope of intercepting small motorboats crowded with clandestine African migrants, mostly young men from Morocco who want to sneak ashore and hunt for work in Europe; tens of thousands of undocumented migrants are taking this route every year, drawn by booming market in low-paying jobs that Europeans do not want; many of their flimsy boats sink, and Spanish Civil Guard regularly finds bloated bodies in water, or flotsam from boats; European Union has tried to enlist Morocco to stem flow of people coming illegally, but European diplomats in Morocco say government there is ignoring problem; photo; maps (M)
news.title: Between Migrants and Spain: The Sea That Kills

news.abstract: JAKARTA—  The president of Indonesia, Abdurrahman Wahid, is pressing for an end to a long-standing ban on the Indonesian Communist Party and a judicial inquiry into the killing of hundreds of thousands of alleged Communists in the 1960s when former President Suharto took power, despite warnings that such steps could cause a military backlash.
news.title: Wahid Seeks Inquiry Into 1960s Killings In Indonesia

news.abstract: House approves $4 billion in additional Pentagon spending for year, and lawmakers edge closer to approving $12.6 billion overall package that would also help Colombia combat drug trafficking and pay for military operations in Kosovo (M)
news.title: House Adds $4 Billion to Pentagon Budget

news.abstract: Russian officer is charged with killing civilian in Chechnya, in rare move by Russian military to crack down on human rights abuses; Gen Anatoly Kvashnin, chief of Russian General Staff, says Russian troops apologized to family of victim, a woman, and expressed regrets by attending her funeral; international human rights organizations have reported numerous cases in which Chechens have been robbed, beaten, killed and raped, but there has been little or no action until now by authorities to bring culprits to justice; Rachel Denber of Human Rights Watch calls for thorough investigation of massacres that have been documented; curbing rights abuses is important for Russia's effort to maintain smooth relations with West, and also for its longer-term effort to build credibility with Chechen people and win peace (M)
news.title: Russia Arrests Officer in Case Of the Killing Of a Chechen

news.abstract: MIDDLE EAST    IRAN: TALIBAN FOE FLEES -- Iran's official news agency said Ismail Khan, the former governor of Herat Province in Afghanistan and a major figure in the opposition to the ruling Taliban, had crossed into Iran and reached the city of Meshed after escaping from a Taliban prison. Mr. Khan, a hero to many Afghans for his fight against Soviet forces in the 1980's, was said to have reached Iran with another anti-Taliban leader who escaped from prison with him, Hafiz Qadir. Iran strongly opposes the Taliban.   John F. Burns (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Talks in Beijing break off without a deal between China and European Union over terms of China's entry into World Trade Orgn (S)
news.title: Talks With Europeans End

news.abstract: Pres Clinton, without winning or conceding anything of substance on his tour of South Asia, may still have helped to modestly reduce risk of war between nuclear-armed India and Pakistan by talking sweet to India and tough to Pakistan (News Analysis) (M)
news.title: In Charmed India, Clinton Wooed, and Maybe Won

news.abstract: Rudolf Kirchschlager, popular and widely respected president of Austria from 1974 to 1986, dies of heart attack at 85; portrait (S)
news.title: Rudolf Kirchschlager, 85, Judge Who Became Austria's President

news.abstract: Samuel R Berger, White House national security adviser, completes two days of talks in Beijing that an American official describes as 'serious and thoughtful'; senior official says that United States reaffirms to China its support for 'one China,' but also stresses need for peaceful dialogue between Beijing and Taipei (M)
news.title: 2 Days of U.S.-China Talks Said to Aid Relations

news.abstract: Residents of teeming and miserable slum in Dhaka, Bangladesh, are relieved that man who had extorted money from them, known as Handcuff Babul, has had his arms chopped off with machete; he could not have operated without blessing of politically well-connected mobsters known as mastans, and rumor is that he angered one of them, leading to his punishment; photos (M)
news.title: In a Dhaka Slum, the Grisly Fate of 'Handcuff' Babul

news.abstract: EUROPE    RUSSIA: RIGHTS OFFICIAL VISITS    The United Nations human rights chief, Mary Robinson, arrived in Moscow on her way to inspect a detention camp in Chechnya where prisoners are said to have been beaten and tortured by Russian soldiers. Mrs. Robinson is also due to meet with top Russian security officials, but so far no meeting with President-elect Vladimir V. Putin is planned.   Celestine Bohlen (NYT)    SWITZERLAND: AUSTRIAN ON TRIP  Chancellor Wolfgang Schussel of Austria was welcomed with full diplomatic honors in Bern on his first official foreign trip. European Union countries have ostracized Austria's new right-wing government, and Mr. Schussel said, ''I hope the Swiss behavior will persuade other European countries to think twice about what they're doing.'' The visit, a traditional one for new Austrian chancellors, was met with protests by Jewish, anti-racism and left-wing groups.   Elizabeth Olson (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Secretary of State Madeleine K Albright says she has dropped her objections to $500 million in loan guarantees from Export-Import Bank to Tyumen, Russian oil company that has been accused of fraud; Tyumen wants money to hire two American companies to rehabilitate oil field and modernize refinery; State Dept official says Tyumen is close to resolving fraud charges, and that company has been privatized (M)
news.title: Albright Drops Objection to Loan Deal for Russia Oil Company

news.abstract: Jacobo Zabludovsky, Mexico's most influential television newsman, parts company with Televisa, extraordinarily powerful network he has worked for for decades; incoming prime-time anchor, Joaquin Lopez Doriga, says he will remain impartial in reporting on presidential campaign now under way; this marks sharp change from Zabludovsky's coverage of last presidential race, in which he was openly favorable to government; muted reaction to Zabludovsky's resignation is itself sign of times in Mexico, authoritarian one-party state that is making its way toward democracy (M)
news.title: In Mexico, Top Newsman And Network Part Ways

news.abstract: United Nations Security Council votes unanimously to allow Iraq to import $1.2 billion in spare parts and other equipment for its ramshackle oil industry, so that more oil can be pumped efficiently and safely to pay for civilian goods and public service projects; Iraq has been allowed to sell unlimited quantities of oil since December, although earnings are monitored and expenditures controlled through UN escrow account; third of profits goes to pay claims arising from Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait, which led to international sanctions against Pres Saddam Hussein (M)
news.title: Security Council Votes to Let Iraq Buy Oil Gear

news.abstract: Armed men wielding machetes and clubs, described by witnesses as supporters of Pres Robert Mugabe, attack people in peaceful anti-government march in Harare, leaving several people seriously injured; marchers claim attackers seemed determined to go after handful of whites in crowd; clash between Mugabe supporters and opponents comes as Zimbabwe braces for its most heated parliamentary election since independence in 1980; Mugabe's party, which has governed for 20 years, faces its most serious challenge ever (M)
news.title: Zimbabwe Protesters Are Beaten by Government Supporters

news.abstract: Vladimiro Montesinos, architect of Pres Alberto K Fujimori's re-election drive, is accused by opponents of running campaign of dirty tricks and has himself become issue in race; opposition newspaper recently obtained detailed information showing that Montesinos has in recent years had annual income of more than $2 million, refueling old charges, never proved, that he is in pay of Peruvian drug traffickers; Montesinos has been crucial ally of Clinton administration in efforts to stop drug trafficking in Andean region, and American officials do not mention him by name in public criticisms of current election campaign; Montesinos has become such a political liability for Fujimori that political analysts wonder why Fujimori does not dismiss him; critics say it is because Montesinos, who was Fujimori's personal lawyer, knows too much about Fujimori's personal life and finances; photo (M)
news.title: Fujimori's Shadowy Aide Highlighted by Election

news.abstract: Organized crime in Japan is feeling pinch of weak economy and aggressive crackdown by police and community groups; this has sparked bitter and often violent struggle among rival gangs for control of shrinking criminal enterprises (M)
news.title: Feeling Pinch, Japan's Mobs Struggle for Control

news.abstract: Russian Defense Ministry reports that as many as 32 Russian commandos died when their convoy was attacked in rebel ambush in Zhani-Vedeno in Chechnya; attack is one of worst in widening partisan war, and is second ambush against elite unit since attack in Grozny left 20 dead (M)
news.title: Rebel Ambush In Chechnya One of Worst For Russians

news.abstract: Ugandan authorities say death toll has risen to at least 924 people among members of Movement for Restoration of Ten Commandments of God, making it highest death toll of any cult in modern history; police now speculate that some cult members rebelled and asked for their money and belongings back when world did not end on Jan 1, as cult leaders had prophesized; photos; map (M)
news.title: Uganda Cult's Mystique Finally Turned Deadly

news.abstract: LONDON—  Congestion in the Sky
news.title: Britain Is Ready to Take a Bet on Privatization : Air Traffic Control PLC?
