news.abstract: Special report, The Nuclear Shield, describes in detail the missile defense system envisioned by Clinton adminstration and its military advisers; Pentago officials and some experts outside government say defense technology has reached new level of maturity, with combination of miniaturized parts and fast rockets that can produce an agile, lightweight weapon capable of finding and ramming an incoming warhead at about 7,000 miles per hour; critics question whether highly complex weapon can survive boost into orbit and whether it can be made to distinguish between attacking warheads and decoys; in fact, since research on so-called hit-to-kill weapons began in 1976, attempts to destroy mock warheads have failed more than 70 percent of time; success of crucial upcoming flight test, in when a ground-based interceptor missile will try to destroy a mock warhead in space, could lead to decision by Pres Clinton or next administration to begin construction of first phase of national missile defense; central feature of system would be a supersmart 'exoatmospheric kill vehicle' designed to be carried atop a rocket and guide itself to collision with incoming warhead; charts, diagram and map show how system is designed to work (L)
news.title: THE NUCLEAR SHIELD: Repelling an Attack; A Missile Defense With Limits: The ABC's of the Clinton Plan

news.abstract: Cuban government is keeping Elian Gonzalez in the news and continuing public rallies in apparent attempt to tap into overwhelming support for boy's return to rekindle some of revolutionary ardor that has cooled in recent years and to restore appeal of Pres Fidel Castro (M)
news.title: After Boy's Return, Castro Tries to Keep Momentum

news.abstract: Mexico's political parties are courting women voters as never before in this year's presidential election; with statistical dead heat between governing party candidate Francisco Labastida Ocho and center-right opponent Vicente Fox Quesada, women's votes may be decisive; some 52 percent of Mexican electorate are women, and more than a third of all voters are homemakers; the courting of women's vote is also changing focus of campaigns, with questions being asked about both candidates' divorces, a subject long considered taboo for public discussion; unusually high-profile roles of political wives and daughters this year signals new opening for women and women's issues in government; photos (M)
news.title: Women Become the Darlings Of the Candidates in Mexico

news.abstract: United States wins agreement to keep door open to further talks on its demand that no American official or soldier be surrendered to world's first permanent court for war crimes as long as US has not signed treaty creating International Criminal Court (M)
news.title: U.S. Gains a Compromise On War Crimes Tribunal

news.abstract: Leading candidates in Mexican presidential election are seen close on major issues; Francsico Labastida Ochoa of governing party and Vicente Fox Quesada of right-of-center opposition, who have been running neck and neck, are so close on economic issues that they use same slogan: 'An economy with a human face'; both candidates play down nationalism that used to be a campaign mainstay and favor good relations with United States (M)
news.title: Leading Candidates in Mexico As Close on Issues as in Polls

news.abstract: Fighting in Maluku islands, Indonesia, between Muslims and Christians spurs many islanders to flee, driving them into risky boats and dangerous seas; nearly 500 people are feared dead following sinking of their battered ferry; passengers were desperately fleeing Moslem gangs that were killing people, apparently in revenge for what they describe as wave of killings by Christians in December; photo; map (L)
news.title: Killings Drive Indonesians Into Risky Boats and Dangerous Seas

news.abstract: AN ARTICLE in the June 24-25 Money Report concerned the investment prospects of bonds issued by pariah states, focusing in particular on North Korean debt and the impact that the recent Korean summit might have on it. Barton Biggs, the global strategist at Morgan Stanley Dean Witter & Co., has been considering another potential impact of the summit meeting on South Korean stocks.
news.title: Korean Summit:Bad for Stocks?

news.abstract: Alfred C Ulmer Jr, officer in US intelligence agencies from World War II until 1962, dies at age 83 (S)
news.title: Alfred C. Ulmer Jr., 83, Officer In U.S. Intelligence Agencies

news.abstract: GENOMICS is frequently compared to the computer industry of the 1980s, but there is at least one big difference: the action is not concentrated in California. Some of the most interesting research is taking place far off the beaten track.
news.title: Iceland, a Natural Genetics Lab
Presbyterians Vote to Ban Clergy From Conducting Unions of Gays
Leading Candidates in Mexico As Close on Issues as in Polls
U.S. Farmers Still Planting Biotech Crops
New Cinema And New Hope In Harlem
Hong Kong Is Debating Its Land Policy, a Vestige of Colonial Rule

news.abstract: Terry Forrestal, British stuntman who staged and performed action sequences for such Hollywood films as Braveheart and Titanic, died on June 10 in jumping accident in Norway; he was 52 years old; photo (M)
news.title: Terry Forrestal, 52, a Stuntman In Bond Films and 'Braveheart'

news.abstract: Pres Andres Pastrana, who took office in 1998 with highest vote total of any candidate in Colombia's history, finds his standing sinking, even though he has just received vote of confidence from US in form of $1.3 billion in emergency military aid (M)
news.title: U.S. Helps Colombian Leader, But His Woes Pile Up at Home

news.abstract: Fidel Castro vows to press campaign to change American policy on Cuba, but suggests he does expect immediate success with either of candidates to succeed Pres Clinton; message is read at first rally since return of six-year-old Elian Gonzalez, subject of custody battle between father and Miami relatives; photo of rally protesting US embargo; map (M)
news.title: Castro Says He Will Press Effort to Change U.S. Policy

news.abstract: Iranian judge convicts 10 of 13 Jewish men accused by Revolutionary Court of spying for Israel and sentences them to prison terms ranging from 4 to 13 years; two Muslim men convicted of aiding spy ring are sentenced to two and four years; two other Muslims and three Jews are acquitted; Pres Clinton says he is deeply disturbed at trial that did not give defendants due process of law; close-knit Jewish community in Shiraz, where many defendants were among religious leaders, is grim, viewing ruling as warning; photo; appeal will cite lack of any evidence other than confessions made after defendants had been jailed for nearly 16 months without counsel; convictions may have tangible effect on Pres Mohammad Khatami's bid for warmer relations with West (M)
news.title: 10 JEWS CONVICTED BY IRANIAN COURT IN ESPIONAGE CASE

news.abstract: Quick deployment of UN peackeepers and Lebanese forces in stretch of southern Lebanon abandoned by Israel has been thrown into doubt by apparent Israeli inscursions across 1923 border; map (S)
news.title: Israeli Incursions Add to Friction Over Border

news.abstract: Sec Madeleine K Albright, who has visited 82 nations since taking office, wants to stress her vision of democracy in last six months of her term; says her travels show how job has changed since end of cold war and how foreign policy issues have expanded; photo (M)
news.title: With Time Short, Albright Stays Aloft

news.abstract: Canada has become one of the world's most tolerant countries regarding homosexuality; Scouts Canada has inaugurated its first official gay and lesbian scout troop; Canada has also just adopted omnibus law that erases virtually all legal distinctions between heterosexual marriages and same sex unions; photo (M)
news.title: In Canada, Gay Pride Can Be Part of Scouts' Honor

news.abstract: International team of archaeologists is racing to unearth and save mosaics and artifacts in Zeugma, Turkey, site of ancient Roman town, which will soon be inundated by lake forming behind new Euphrates River dam; some Turkish archaeologists and government officials seem uncomfortable with widespread publicity abroad, apparently viewing foreign clamor as interference that borders on insult; plans for at least 10 more dams in region in coming decades could spur growing conflict between advocates of economic development and of historical preservation; photo (M)
news.title: A Race to Save Roman Splendors From Drowning

news.abstract: Final returns show Ugandan voters overwhelmingly endorsed Pres Yoweri Museveni's 'no-party' political system; Museveni and Pres Paul Kagame of Rwanda, nominal allies in fighting in Congo, meet to defuse tensions in wake of June skirmishes between their troops in Kisangani, Congo; fighting in Congo is unpopular in Uganda, and Museveni's opponents raised issue in pressing for return to traditional political parties; opponents hold low voter turnout reflects success of their boycott and widespread discontent with Museveni (M)
news.title: Ugandans Vote to Continue One-Party System

news.abstract: Supporters of Vicente Fox Quesada in Mexico's presidential campaign carefully monitor voting in places like Orizaba to guard against fraud by ruling party, which backs Francisco Labastida Ochoa; Fox's campaign, boosted by palpable desire for change among peasants who have long backed ruling party, watches carefully over newest and most vulnerable supporters; map; photo (M)
news.title: An Anxious Vigil in Mexico's Political Trenches

news.abstract: Mexicans of various backgrounds, professions and political stripes seem stunned and excited by Vicente Fox Quesada's decisive triumph over one of longest ruling political machines in world; Mexicans express pride in peaceful way votes were cast and counted, in way they overcame their fear of change and embraced it, and in feeling that their country will be more widely viewed as sophisticated world player now; photo (M)
news.title: Strong Feelings of Pride Over Orderly Balloting

news.abstract: Pres-elect Vicente Fox Quesada of Mexico begins transition from republic led for decades by autocratic presidents to one in which political power is now up for grabs; election returns show he won 43 percent of votes, while Francisco Labastida Ochoa, candidate of governing party, won 36 percent and Cuauhtemoc Cardenas Solorzano, leftist candidate, got 17 percent; Fox's victory over governing party is far more decisive than any poll had predicted; Fox receives contratulatory phone calls from world leaders, including Pres Clinton, and meets with Pres Ernesto Zedillo; Fox says he assured Zedillo that he will not carry out purge of government bureaucracy after he takes office Dec 1; says two will meet frequently before than to plan next year's budget and to discuss transition; Fox will preside over government unused to coalition politics; photos (M)
news.title: MEXICO, VOTING IN NEW LEADER, BEGINS A POLITICAL SEA CHANGE

news.abstract: United States request to set up military logistics point in El Salvador for its war on drugs touches nerve in that country; American advisers, intelligence and money not long ago helped fuel devastating civil war there; encroaching role of United States is seen by some as infringing on national sovereignty; legislators from FMLN, who form largest single bloc in Assembly, say accord turns over to US monitoring and enforcement tasks that rightly belong to El Salvador's own police and military; they bristle at general references that allow American personnel access to any government institutions needed to carry out their mission; for El Salvador, larger issue is what role their own military should play in addressing internal security after dozen years in which it took part in war that left 60,000 Salvadorans dead; photo; map (M)
news.title: Salvadorans Balk at American Plan to Use Airport

news.abstract: Chechen suicide bombers set off series of blasts throughout breakaway republic, killing at least 37 Russian soldiers and wounding 74; five trucks laden with explosives blow up in towns and cities ostensibly under Russian control; carefully coordinated rebel attack occurs just a week after Russian military declared that war is all but won; as toll of dead and wounded mounts, Moscow vows to break back of rebel resistance; rebels respond by saying they plan still more bombings; rumors are rife that Grozny, Chechen capital, will be attacked next; photo; map (M)
news.title: Chechen Rebels Kill 37 Russian Soldiers In Truck Bombings

news.abstract: Chancellor Wolfgang Schussel of Austria says his country will block expansion of European Union until it lifts sanctions imposed last February to punish country for letting party of Jorg Haider into government; sanctions have had no serious economic effect on Austria, but they rankle with Austrians; approval of any of dozen countries seeking admission to European Union must be unanimous, so Austria could play spoiler if it does not get its way (M)
news.title: A Threat By Austria On Sanctions

news.abstract: Nikolai Patrushev, chief of Russia's intelligence service, blames negligence by Russian commanders for suicide bombings by Chechen rebels that killed more than 30 soldiers; says that Federal Security Service alerted military that attacks were being planned but that someone failed to take proper precautions (M)
news.title: Moscow Blames Poor Security for Bombing Deaths in Chechnya

news.abstract: PARIS—  Can life really be this good — bright sunshine colors even for work? A Palm Pilot encased in a Day-Glo purse? Hawaiian print shirts that bring vacation wear to main street? Even pastel shoes?
news.title: France's Boom Sends Some Bright Ideas Into Summer 2001 : Optimistic Color Sweeps Paris

news.abstract: Battle erupts within Mexico's governing Institutional Revolutionary Party following its election defeat, with several rival leaders maneuvering for control during painful transition that party leaders say will test its powers of survival; near chaos grips party after leader, Dulce Maria Sauri, resigns with expectation that entire cabinet will leave with her (M)
news.title: Mexico's Defeated Leadership Squabbles Over the Next Step

news.abstract: United Nations' annual Human Development Report states that Africans south of Sahara, convulsed by wars and weakened by natural disasters, suffer broadest range of social and economic disadvantages (S)
news.title: Misery Index Of U.N. Panel Finds Africa Is Worst Off

news.abstract: Mexico's president-elect, Vicente Fox Quesada, pledges to rebuild country's federal law enforcement system and wipe out corruption that has crippled nation for decades; is likely to use executive powers to create a Ministry of Security and Justice, similar to Federal Bureal of Investigation, that would be responsible for all federal police, significantly reducing powers of Interior Ministry and attorney general; says he will meet with Pres Clinton and both major presidential candidates to press proposal to open US-Mexico border to less restricted flow of immigrants; expounds on measures his new government will take to deal with range of Mexico's most persistent and complex problems, including fight against poverty, efforts to stem flow of drugs and unresolved conflict in Chiapas; photo (M)
news.title: VICTOR IN MEXICO PLANS TO OVERHAUL LAW ENFORCEMENT

news.abstract: Residents of Kanungu, Uganda, are avoiding compound where hundreds of members of religious sect, Movement for the Restoration of the Ten Commandments of God, were murdered in March; circumstances surrounding deaths still remain mystery; death toll put at 780; map; photo (M)
news.title: Ugandan Villagers Avoiding Cult Massacre Site

news.abstract: Colombia, under pressure from US, reluctantly agrees to take first step toward developing powerful biological herbicide against its coca and heroin-poppy fields; US has been quietly debating for years ways of conducting field tests of such a herbicide, developed from fungus that occurs naturally in many types of cocoa and other plants; Colombian officials say they are completing proposal to UN that will include testing for presence of fungus, Fusarium oxysporum, in coca, raw material of cocaine; government is suporting project as Pres Clinton is about to sign bill providing $1.3 billion in aid to Colombia to fight drug traffickers and insurgents who protect their trade (M)
news.title: FUNGUS CONSIDERED AS A TOOL TO KILL COCA IN COLOMBIA

news.abstract: Pentagon gives preview of test of missile defense system, scheduled for July 6, in Roslyn, Va, office of Boeing Co, prime contractor for program; exercise, third and most demanding in series of 19 tests for national missile defense system, will last for 30 minutes (M)
news.title: Pentagon Gives a Preview of Missile Defense Test Tomorrow

news.abstract: EUROPE    FRANCE: U.S. ESPIONAGE INQUIRY  The European Parliament in Strasbourg has voted to form a committee to investigate allegations that Washington's vast surveillance system, called Echelon, is being used to conduct industrial espionage now that the cold war is over. The system, maintained by the United States and several allies including Britain, listens to and watches millions of telephone, fax and e-mail messages each day. The committee is expected to report back in about eight months.    Suzanne Daley (NYT)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Focus on plans by Mexican president-elect Vicente Fox Quesada to fight crime and corruption by overhauling country's federal law enforcement institutions; experts say plans, which would require several constitutional amendments, suggest that he intends to bring power of presidency to bear in crackdown more than his recent predecessors; photo (M)
news.title: Familiar Foe for Mexico's New Leader: Corruption

news.abstract: Yugoslav Parliament approves constitutional changes that allow Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic to run for a new term and that diminish influence of Montenegro, Serbia's small sister republic; changes require direct popular election of the Yugoslav president and upper house of Parliament, allow two four-year terms for president and raise threshold for impeachment; effect will give Milosevic chance of remaining in power past July of next year, when his current term expires; until now, Yugoslav president was elected by Parliament and could serve only one four-year term; upper house of Parliament was itself elected by Parliaments of the two republics, Serbia and Montenegro; changes make Milosevic's plans for elections less dependent on Montenegro's consent and may hasten Montenegro's effort to break away (M)
news.title: Change in Yugoslav Constitution Allows Milosevic to Seek Another Term as President

news.abstract: Palestinian Authority divulges details of its long-hidden investment porrtfolio; chief economic adviser Mohammed Rachid says that he will preside over dissolution of the financial empire he amassed at Yasir Arafat's request, pledging that holdings will either be divested or transferred to a new, publicly accountable Palestinian Investment Fund by year's end; according to audited statement sent to International Monetary Fund and published on authority's Web site, the holding company now boasts assets of $345 million, including $292 million in equity stakes in three dozen companies (M)
news.title: Palestinian Investment Fund, No Longer Secret, Will Close

news.abstract: Dr Theodore A Postol, a leading critic of national missile defense, says in letter to Pres Clinton that Clinton's advisers have made misleading statements about proposed missile shield and urges creating an independent commission of top scientists to evaluate plan; American Physical Society, Federation of American Scientists and Union of Concerned Scientists jointly announce that they have urged Clinton not to deploy missile defense system, regardless of how its ground-based interceptor performs in coming test; Greenpeace is sending a Dutch icebreaker, Arctic Sunrise, to designated 'hazard zone' near launching site at Vandenberg Air Force Base in California to try to stop test; Defense Department issues statement defending integrity of program (M)
news.title: Critics Asking Clinton to Stop Advancing Missile Plan

news.abstract: Prime Min Tony Blair of Britain, who has made a point of keeping his four young children out of news, is embarrassed by front-page headlines reporting arrest of his 16-year-old son, Euan, for public drunkenness (S)
news.title: Oldest Son's Revels Embarrass Blair

news.abstract: General Accounting Office says that pervasive crime and corruption are blocking success of Dayton peace accord in Bosnia and that Clinton administration should consider suspending its extensive aid until local authorities show a determination to fight such abuses; says corruption could interfere with eventual withdrawal of United States and other NATO troops (M)
news.title: Congressional Report Says Corruption Is Stifling Bosnia

news.abstract: United Nations-sponsored study finds that while a simple drug regimen can stop many mothers with HIV from infecting their children during pregnancy and childbirth, the protection does not last for as long as experts had hoped and that the therapy appears to leave children vulnerable to infection from breast milk; finding safe alternatives to breast-feeding is daunting challenge in Africa, where overwhelming majority of women breast-feed their infants for long periods; findings are certain to renew often bitter controversy over breast-feeding (M)
news.title: REPORT DIMS HOPE FOR AIDS THERAPY TO PROTECT BABIES

news.abstract: Clinton administration's hopes for moving forward with national missile defense system are dealt setback when missile fired from Marshall Islands in Pacific fails to hit a mock warhead launched 4,300 miles away in California; test failure is certain to reinforce calls in Congress that decision on whether to move forward with a national missile defense program should be left next president (M)
news.title: ANTIMISSILE TEST FAILS OVER PACIFIC, PENTAGON REPORTS

news.abstract: Chinese government backs Linux operating system in effort to prevent country from becoming overly dependent on Microsoft Corp's Windows operating system; some Chinese warn that secret holes in Microsoft's computer code might allow US government access to Chinese networks or even enable it, in time of war, to shut those networks down; Microsoft says such fears are nonsense; Linux source code, unlike Microsoft's, is open for all to see and is freely distributed, and this touch of communist ideal appeals to China's Marxist leaders (M)
news.title: China Moves To Cut Power Of Microsoft

news.abstract: SEOUL—  A little bit of garlic goes a long way toward spicing up Korea's national dish, kimchi. But lately a little bit of Chinese garlic has injected a foul odor into trade relations between South Korea and Beijing.
news.title: Just a Little Garlic Overpowers Asian Trade Ties

news.abstract: People of Cardenas, Cuba, the home of Elian Gonzalez, begin to reclaim their daily routines now that the boy is back in Cuba; photo; map (M)
news.title: Cardenas Journal; The Town That's Proud to Say Elian Lives Here

news.abstract: Special report, Medicine Merchants, examines titanic struggle between pharmaceutical companies and public health advocates over price of drugs and right to produce and market them in third world countries as epidemics increase worldwide; situation in Ongata Rongai, Kenya, where critically ill are unable to obtain drugs because of high costs discussed; maps; photos (M)
news.title: MEDICINE MERCHANTS: Patents and Patients; As Devastating Epidemics Increase, Nations Take On Drug Companies

news.abstract: Crucial test in Pentagon's complex, $60 billion antimissile defensive system fails after high-speed interceptor 'kill vehicle' designed to destroy dummy warhead fails to separate from booster rocket; failure will make it politically and diplomatically more difficult for Pres Clinton to move ahead with plan administration contends is crucial to defend against attack, but which opponents say is technically unsound, militarily unnecessary and waste of money; reinforces calls in Congress to leave decision to next president; failure was in well-developed technology, used successfully in rockets that have launched satellites and missiles for decades; photo (M)
news.title: KEY MISSILE PARTS ARE LEFT UNTESTED AS BOOSTER FAILS

news.abstract: Russian Pres Vladimir V Putin presents forbidding state-of-Russia address to Parliament and national television audience; says Russians have built only 'carcass' of civil society, and have yet to shoulder basic obligations, such as obeying laws; warns falling birthrate and aging population threaten to make country 'senile' nation; says economy is actually house of cards supported by high oil prices; warns growing gap between advanced nations and Russia is pushing country into third world; says not much can be remedied until Parliament ratifies his plans to concentrate power in Kremlin and destroy barnacled system of regulations, hidden favors and political empire-building that is strangling economy (M)
news.title: Putin Describes an Ill Russia and Prescribes Strong Democracy

news.abstract: Even though residents of Israel, West Bank and Gaza are prisoners of dreary pursuit for peace, only Jewish settlers are treating Camp David summit as pivotal event; only in sttlements has daily life been altered to plan for what many see as most significant battle of political lives; photo (M)
news.title: Two Sides Share Subdued View of Mideast Summit Talks

news.abstract: News analysis: Clinton administration has reaped all of diplomatic disadvantages of program to build national missile defense and none of potential rewards with recent failure of Pentagon's antimissile test (M)
news.title: Strategy Misfire: Missile Failure Carries Political Cost

news.abstract: Israeli government of Prime Min Ehud Barak crumbles as three rightist parties quit in protest against anticipated concessions to Palestinians, leaving him on uncertain ground on eve of departure for Camp David summit with Yasir Arafat and Pres Clinton; loses parliamentary majority and broad coalition, constructed precisely to build stable foundation of support for difficult peace moves; three parties reject Barak's pleas for unity, defecting to previously weak opposition and upsetting political balance of power; Barak addresses nation; defiantly says coalition will not affect trip to summit, which he maintains is backed by Israelis who elected him by overwhelming majority on peacemaking platform; says as lifelong soldier and fledgling politician he has direct bond with voters; possible effects of government's collapse on three-way retreat-style summit discussed; photos (M)
news.title: BARAK'S COALITION CRUMBLES ON EVE OF SUMMIT TALKS

news.abstract: Pope John Paul II sxpresses 'bitterness' over gay pride festival held in Rome during Roman Catholic Holy Year; says event is affront to church and Christian values of Italian capital (S)
news.title: Pope Declares His 'Bitterness' Over Gay Event

news.abstract: Senior advisers to Pres Clinton say they still expect him to make decision before end of summer on whether to proceed with missile defense system, while acknowledging that recent failure of major test makes it far more likely that his successor will ultimately decide fate of project; comments by national security adviser Samuel R Berger and others noted (M)
news.title: Decision on Defense System May Fall to Next President

news.abstract: Two bombings in southern Russian provinces close to Chechnya kill seven people, week after Chechen rebels killed 33 Russian soldiers in wave of truck-bomb attacks (S)
news.title: 7 Killed in 2 Bombings in Southern Russia, Not Far From Chechnya

news.abstract: First agreement between Serbs and UN administration in Gracanica, Serbia, which may provide better protection for Serbian minority, threatens to unravel key Albanian participation in international efforts to build democratic, tolerant Kosovo; year into effort to rebuild new Kosovo, many in UN administration express weariness over recalcitrance of Albanian leaders who are jostling for power and seem willing to fight out differences on streets; map; photo (M)
news.title: U.N.'s Plan for Kosovo Threatens to Unravel

news.abstract: South African government, striking defiant and combative tone, lashes out at critics at 13th international conference on AIDS in Durban who expressed disappointment with Pres Thabo Mbeki for opening conference by describing extreme poverty, rather than AIDS, as biggest killer in Africa (M)
news.title: South Africa Faults Critics of Its President on AIDS Stance

news.abstract: Patrick Henry, whose trial in 1977 for killing seven-year-old boy helped abolish death penalty in France, is refused parole (S)
news.title: French Killer In Pivotal Case To Stay in Jail

news.abstract: PARIS—  France has decided to send its governing elite, including its redoubtable diplomats, back to school to learn how to cope with new challenges in a more competitive, globalized world.
news.title: Report Challenges the Policymaking Elite : French Diplomats Told To Go Back to School

news.abstract: Tens of thousands of pilgrims from around world have trekked to San Salvador, El Salvador, since end of civil conflict to seek out Jesuit residence, where soldiers killed six priests and their housekeeper and daughter in 1989, as well as chapel of local hospital, where Archbishop Oscar Arnulfo Romero, was shot dead during Mass in 1980; have transformed both places into local shrines; others also visit place in countryside where four American churchwomen were killed by soldiers in December 1980; maps; photo (M)
news.title: San Salvador Journal; Pilgrims Take Inspiration From Martyrs of the 80's

news.abstract: Major issues facing Israeli and Palestinian negotiators at Camp David peace summit discussed; map (M)
news.title: Moment of Truth on Tough Issues

news.abstract: International AIDS conference in Durban, South Africa, hears promising report from Dr Scott Holmberg of Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on trials aimed at giving long breaks in treatment to people infected with HIV; aim is to help body cope with virus on its own for varying periods and make it easier for infected people to take the drugs; Dr Mauro Schechter of Brazil says drugs other than protease inhibitors deserve some of the credit they regularly get for lowering death rates from AIDS; Dr Anthony S Fauci of National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases says that eradicating HIV is not possible with drugs currently available and that prolonged courses of drug combinations are not feasible for most infected people (M)
news.title: Intermittent Drug Therapy for AIDS Is Tested

news.abstract: Prime Min Ehud Barak, Yasir Arafat and Pres Clinton begin their summit meeting at Camp David in Maryland, and Clinton speaks in idealistic tones of securing a just and enduring end to Israeli-Palestinian conflict; Israeli officials say they will soon resolve their dispute with Clinton administration over contract to sell Phalcon advanced radar system to the Chinese; photos (M)
news.title: Arab-Israeli Talks Open at Camp David

news.abstract: MIDDLE EAST    IRAN: ACQUITTED IN STUDENT ATTACK  A military court acquitted a former Tehran police chief of ordering an attack on a student dormitory that led to a week of pro-reform protests. The verdict brought immediate criticism from students. Farhad Nazari and 17 subordinates were charged with injuring scores of students and killing one in the attack last July. Two defendants were found guilty. ''Such rulings will lead to social insecurity and people will lose their confidence in the judiciary,'' said Ibrahim Sheik, a student leader, a sentiment echoed by other students.   Nazila Fathi (NYT)    IRAN: KHATAMI PLEA TO U.S.  President Mohammad Khatami, on a visit to Germany, urged the United States to take the next step toward reviving diplomatic relations with Tehran. ''You can be sure that when the United States has the key in its hand, it will not give it away,'' he said on German public television. He said he recognized a ''new turn'' in Washington, but that the shift did not go far enough.   Victor Homola (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: US seeks extradition from Mexico of Agustin Vasquez Mendoza, who is suspected of the 1994 murder of Richard Fass, an American anti-drug agent (S)
news.title: Mexican Murder Suspect Is Sought by U.S.

news.abstract: Russian prosecutors search offices of Media-Most, media conglomerate owned by Vladimir A Gusinsky, for the second time in two months; skeptics suspect that Kremlin is trying to silence one of its few prominent critics (M)
news.title: Russian Media Conglomerate Searched Again by Authorities

news.abstract: United States and Vietnamese officials meeting in Washington reportedly complete sweeping trade agreement that would allow generally unfettered commerce between the two nations for first time since end of Vietnam War; agreement, which comes after four years of fitful negotiations, is expected to be signed within a week; but Congress will still have to approve agreement and extend normal trade privileges to Vietnam, a vote that some Clinton administration officials believe is unlikely this election year (M)
news.title: U.S. AND VIETNAM ARE SAID TO AGREE ON NORMAL TRADE

news.abstract: Elder statesmen of Mexico's Institutional Revolutionary Party agree on formula aimed at maintaining internal discipline as party's long monopoly over Mexican power and wealth draws to a close; 21 state governors, after meeting with Pres Ernesto Zedillo, announce that they have convinced party's top leader, Dulce Maria Sauri, to remain in her post for a few months while party decides how to choose her replacement (M)
news.title: Mexico's Ousted Party Tries to Regroup After Stunning Defeat

news.abstract: Warming relations between South Korea and Japan after years of mistrust and disdain are reflected by explosion in tourism between the two countries; Fukuoka, which is close to Korean peninsula, has become favored jumping-off point for Japanese travelers; map; photos (M)
news.title: Travel Boom Pulls Japan and South Korea Closer

news.abstract: Russian authorities bring tax evasion charges against top executives of AvtoVAZ, country's biggest carmaker, as part of Pres Vladimir V Putin's efforts to loosen grip of Russia's richest men on country's most profitable enterprises; charges against executives may be a move against Boris A Berezovsky, influential member of Parliament and friend of former Pres Boris N Yeltsin's family; Berezovsky holds major stake in AvtoVAZ (M)
news.title: Russian Auto Executive Faces Tax Charges

news.abstract: Nira Schwartz, senior engineer who leveled charges of fraud in antimissile research against military contractor TRW, is becoming caught in clash between Defense Department, which is trying to question her about leaks of military secrets, and Congressional and criminal investigators, who are gearing up to examine merits of her accusations that TRW falsified work that was meant to help antimissile interceptors distinguish incoming warheads from decoys; Schwartz says Pentagon plans to have security investigators question her are clearly aimed at shielding $60 billion antimisile plan from scrutiny (M)
news.title: Engineer Charging Antimissile Fraud Is Snared in a Federal Clash

news.abstract: Unknown to their American hosts, Prime Min Ehud Barak of Israel and Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat held private, impromptu meeting at Arafat's cabin on night of July 12; substance of what was said is not described in brief account given by State Department, if indeed it is known, but fact that such encounter took place is taken as sign that serious effort is being made by both sides (M)
news.title: Barak and Arafat Hold Impromptu Meeting

news.abstract: THE AMERICAS    CANADA: NEW INDIAN CHIEF -- Canadian Indian tribes have elected as their national chief a Quebec Cree known for leading a North American protest campaign that stopped a major hydroelectric dam planned for northern Quebec. Matthew Coon Come, a former Cree chief, told delegates of the Assembly of First Nations that his main priority will be securing self-government and land rights.     James Brooke (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: United States and Vietnam sign lengthy trade agreement that, if put into effect fully, would transform America's onetime enemy from quasi-socialist reboubt into Asia's newest capitalist recruit; Pres Clinton hails agreement as 'historic event'; Vietnam, with its small, troubled and highly protected economy is risking far more than United States; but agreement requires US to reduce its tariffs substantially on Vietnamese imports, concession that has often proves a tough sell in Congress; it is unlikely vote will come on agreement during Pres Clinton's term (M)
news.title: Vietnam and the U.S. Sign Pact Aimed at Promoting Trade

news.abstract: Massacre in tiny village of El Salado highlights United States and human rights groups' reservations about Colombia's military leadership, its human rights record and its collaboration with paramilitary units; more then 300 armed men marched into village in February, and with list of names began summoning residents for judgment; troops ordered liquor and music, then embarked on calculated three-day rampage of torture, rape and killing of scores of people they accused of collaborating with left-wing guerrillas who have long been presence in area; military and police units just few miles away not only made no effort to stop slaughter, but also set up roadblock, preventing human rights groups from getting to village; while military has opened three investigations into massacre, top officials insist that fighting was under way in village between guerrillas and paramilitary forces, not a series of executions; they also insist that colonel in charge of region, Rodrigo Quinones Cardenas, who has since been promoted to general, has been persecuted by government and human rights groups; map; photos (L)
news.title: Colombians Tell of Massacre, as Army Stood By

news.abstract: Britain has most congested roads in Europe, and probably more road rage than any other country; much of this hostility is focused on so-called 'white van men,' drivers of country's estimated 2.5 million, traditionally white, commercial vans, who are viewed as aggressive, no-holds-barred kings of the road; several van drivers in town of Leatherland comment on their driving habits and criticism directed at them; map; photos (Leatherland Journal) (M)
news.title: Leatherhead Journal; The White Van Man of England: Oh, He's a Devil!

news.abstract: Russian government campaign against tycoons who run five of nation's most powerful business combines has puzzling political implications, for it is hard to tell, yet, whether it is the payoff on Pres Vladimir Putin's pledge to apply the same laws to both the tycoon and kiosk operator or the beginning of some darker and more subtle bloodletting (M)
news.title: Russian Puzzle: What Does War on Tycoons Mean?

news.abstract: European Union is moving to lift the sanctions imposed on Austria after Jorg Haider's far-right party joined the government; France, the leader in imposing sanctions, has just taken over rotating presidency of European Union, and both its presige and, perhaps, the timely expansion of the union are riding on its being able to deliver on a difficult agenda; Austrian officials have threatened to use their veto to block any sort of progress (M)
news.title: European Union Is Moving to Lift Sanctions It Imposed on Austria

news.abstract: German Parliament passes radical tax program that will slash rates and allow corporations to sell subsidiaries or shares in other companies without paying any tax on their profit; change is expected to revolutionize structure of German business because it clears the way for the big banks and insurance companies to sell more than $100 billion in shares in industrial companies like DaimlerChrysler and Siemens; vote is unexpected victory for Chancellor Gerhard Schroder, a Social Democrat; his tax plan has made him the hero of corporate elite; photo (M)
news.title: Radical Tax Plan, a Spur for 'Germany Inc.,' Is Approved

news.abstract: Israeli and Palestinian leaders spend their fourth day in secluded negotiations at Camp David, but serious decision-making has yet to begin (M)
news.title: Camp David Talks in a Lull Before an Expected Whirl of Decision-Making

news.abstract: AFRICA    ZIMBABWE: LAND REDISTRIBUTION -- President Robert Mugabe said his government was to start redistributing land today to war veterans who invaded hundreds of white-owned farms earlier this year in support of his land seizure program. Speaking at the burial of an independence war commander, he said he would not brook domestic opposition or accept foreign criticism. Last month, the government listed 804 farms for seizure for its black resettlement program.   (Reuters)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Haitian officials say they will stand by results of their recent elections despite threats from international donors to suspend aid because of vote-counting method they deem unfair and unacceptable (M)
news.title: Haiti Refuses To Back Down On Elections

news.abstract: Canada, traditionally North America's liberal bastion in abortion war, is suddenly gripped by polarizing debate that has gone beyond ideology to an array of violent attacks and threats; in space of one week, right-wing politician with strong anti-abortion views is elected of Canada's main opposition party, Vancouver gynecologist who performs abortions is stabbed in back and death threat is telephoned to leader of national trials of abortion drug (M)
news.title: Canada Sees Violent Turn In the Fight On Abortion

news.abstract: John Morgan, British etiquette expert, dies at age 41; photo (M)
news.title: John Morgan, Etiquette Maven For the British, Is Dead at 41

news.abstract: Lawrence K Altman news analysis of Africa's AIDS crisis, as 13th annual International Aids conference ends; finds that what is implicit in remarks of both South Africa Pres Thabo Mbeki, who emphasizes social factors like poverty as major force behind AIDS, and former Pres Nelson Mandela's forceful call for action to stop AIDS epidemic, is idea that some AIDS problems can be attacked now, even without vaccines and cures that have yet to emerge from laboratories in developed world (L)
news.title: Africa's AIDS Crisis: Finding Common Ground

news.abstract: Black American veterans who fought in Italy in World War II return to village of Sommocolonia to honor their comrade, Lt John Fox, who was killed in battle on Dec 26, 1944; Fox, who ordered his own men to fire on his position to stem enemy attack, was awarded Medal of Honor more than 50 years later; anguish that black veterans relive is echoed among Italian war survivors who welcome their return; just as black comrades and their relatives cannot shed their bitterness over United States' long refusal to recognize combat records of black servicemen fully, many Italian veterans cannot forgive their own countrymen who fought against them more than 50 years ago; photos; map (L)
news.title: Italy Journal; On a '44 Battlefield, a Salute for a Black Hero

news.abstract: University Teachers for Human Rights, a Tamil rights organization, charges that Tamil rebels preparing for showdown with Sri Lankan Army for control of Jaffna, Sri Lanka's most important Tamil town, have been invading schoolrooms and rounding up children in early teens to send into battle; describes reign of terror in region (M)
news.title: Tamil Rebels Said to Recruit Child Soldiers

news.abstract: Pres Clinton breaks strict news blackout surrounding Camp David summit between Prime Min Ehud Barak of Israel and Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat to tell New York Daily News that he is more optimistic than when talks began six days ago, but is not sure agreement will be reached; says talks are difficult and are unlike anything else he has ever dealt with; says what troubles him most is prospect of what could happen if they fail; comments while rebutting allegations in new book that his wife, Hillary Rodham Clinton, made anti-Semitic remarks about one of his campaign managers nearly three decades ago (M)
news.title: Clinton Voices Some Optimism On Peace Talks

news.abstract: Prosecution hits roadblocks in trial of two Libyans accused of blowing up Pan Am Flight jetliner over Lockerbie, Scotland, in 1988; some witnesses fail to appear in Netherlands for trial, and testimony of others is less than crystal clear (M)
news.title: Lockerbie Bombing Prosecution Hitting Roadblocks at Trial in the Netherlands

news.abstract: Ireland is in throes of economic boom, growing faster than any other in Western world but struggling to cope with prosperity and its downsides; incomes have risen and jobs are plentiful, but inflation is running at 5.2 percent or three times average of other 10 countries in euro zone; young professionals no longer leave, since there are many job opportunities at home, and those who did a generation ago have returned; disruptive consequence of happy turnaround has been 20 percent-per-year spiral in cost of housing that is pricing middle class out of cities; new prosperity has changed social habits, breaking down traditional pattern of association, but is also source of shame; country is proving to be inhospitable to outsiders, some asylum seekers, arriving in droves and seeking jobs that are going unfilled; maps; photo (M)
news.title: Money, Jobs, Big Cars: How's an Irishman to Cope?

news.abstract: Outside his powder-blue shack, Antonio Alejo waits quietly for customers in need of an oil change or a brake job. He smiles faintly as his youngest child plays with his two stepchildren, running around some burning trash on the sand dune that is his front yard. With business slow, he tends a few geraniums and sunflowers and occasionally fixes a bowl of rice.    Mr. Alejo is slowly picking up the shards of his life.
news.title: THE INNOCENTS/A Special Report; Jailed Unjustly, Peruvians Try to Rebuild Shattered Lives

news.abstract: Election of Ujjal Dosanjh, Sikh who was born in Punjab, as new premier of British Colombia reflects Canada's rapidly changing ethnic nature, as well as its widespread acceptance of diversity; province's 250,000 Indo-Canadians are increasingly visible as political and economic force and are rapidly entering country's mainstream; most of country's estimated half a million residents of Indian origin are Sikhs; photo; map (M)
news.title: Sikhs on the Rise in British Colombia

news.abstract: Mokhtar Haouari, Algerian, waives his right to extradition hearing in Canada and will be turned over to US to face charges of helping Ahmed Ressam, who was arrested in December in Washington State after crossing Canadian border carrying explosives and bomb-making equipment (M)
news.title: Terrorism Suspect Waives Extradition Hearing

news.abstract: Pres Vladimir V Putin of Russia arrives in China on first stop of Asian tour intended to revive his country's faded diplomatic role in region and build what could become Chinese-Russian axis to counter American influence; is expected to sign at least six accords with Chinese leaders, including statement condemning US proposals for missile defense system (M)
news.title: Putin Visits China In Hope of Strengthening a Strategic Axis

news.abstract: Nasser Ntege Sebaggala, uneducated populist businessman running for president in Uganda, has become local political phenomenon despite the face he served one year in US prison for passing bad checks; will face Pres Yoweri Museveni, who is his opposite in nearly every way, in elections in 2001; photos (M)
news.title: Kampala Journal; When a Questionable Past Pays Political Dividends

news.abstract: US and Germany approve $5 billion agreement to compensate forced laborers from Nazi era; under agreement German government and German companies will contribute equally to fund to compensate former laborers who were slave workers in concentration camps or German factories; Stuart E Eizenstat, who negotiated on behalf of US, says agreement fills void that has existed for 55 years; historic bargain will compensate Nazi-era victims in more than 20 countries; photo (M)
news.title: Germans Sign Agreement to Pay Forced Laborers of Nazi Era

news.abstract: PARIS—  Thomas Quinn Curtiss, who wrote about film and theater for the International Herald Tribune for nearly four decades and contributed to many other publications, including The New York Times and Variety, died Monday in Poissy, outside Paris.
news.title: Thomas Quinn Curtiss Dies, IHT Critic

news.abstract: Pres Clinton, seeking to finalize Mideast peace accord, delays his trip to Japan for meeting of leaders of seven leading industrial nations by one day and will stay at Camp David with Israeli Prime Min Ehud Barak and Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat; talks, described as increasingly intense and heated, again continue into night; both sides are playing to their constituents at home and preparing public opinion for possible outcomes; photos (M)
news.title: Clinton Delays Trip to Remain at Peace Talks

news.abstract: Proposal by William Thomas to build new city near Kilmovee, in Ireland's isolated west, has spurred national debate and is being embraced by local leaders; comes at time when government planners are working on strategy to spread nation's resources and opportunities more evenly; map; photo (M)
news.title: Kilmovee Journal; The Gleam in an Irishman's Eye: An Emerald City

news.abstract: Hezbollah leader Sheik Nabil Qaouk cites guerrilla group's successful use of television as weapon of modern warfare against Israeli occupation of southern Lebanon, interview; details how group evolved from small band of amateurish gunmen to highly sophisticated tactical operation; cites use of demoralization to help drive Israelis from Lebanon; map; photo (M)
news.title: In Long Fight With Israel, Hezbollah Tactics Evolved

news.abstract: LONDON—  Britain's chancellor of the Exchequer on Tuesday announced a major increase in public spending over the coming three years, saying the Labour government was determined to use its big budget surplus to finance improvements in health care, education, transportation and crime-fighting.
news.title: Blair Aims Big Surplus At Crime and Health Issues

news.abstract: British Prime Min Tony Blair's government is embarrassed by leaking to press of memo from government's pollster, Philip Gould, warning New Labor brand has become object of ridicule; note echoed many of concerns raised in secret memo by Blair himself that made its way into newspapers earlier in week (M)
news.title: One More Leaked Memo on Party's Woes Embarrasses Blair

news.abstract: Russian Pres Vladimir V Putin, in announcement intended to remove prime rationale for American missile defense plan, says North Korea will abandon its missile program if other nations will provide it with rockets to launch satellites into space; announcement comes during meeting, Pyongyang, with North Korean leader Kim Jong Il; visit, first by Russian president to North Korea, is part of his intensive round of Asian diplomacy aimed at mobilizing opposition to American anti-missile plan; United States expresses willingness to explore deal in which North Korean satellites would be launched from other nations; photo (M)

news.abstract: Analysis of refusal of Israeli Prime Min Ehud Barak and Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat to let Camp David peace talks end in failure as Pres Clinton prepared to leave; intractable issue of Jerusalem's sovereignty, which Mideast leaders have never dared discuss before, remains threat to talks, but could be deferred in partial accord (M)

news.abstract: Interview with Svetlana Broz on her crusade and book against hardline nationalism that has destroyed Yugoslavia created by her late grandfather, Josip Broz Tito; book recounts stories of gestures of goodness from people who were often on opposing sides in war told to her by patients at hospitals and clinics she served in as doctor after fighting broke out in Bosnia; photos (M)
news.title: A Tito Grandchild Battles Nationalism's Excesses

news.abstract: EUROPE    CORSICA: AUTONOMY PLAN ACCEPTED  Corsican nationalists said they had accepted French proposals to grant autonomy to their island in a crucial step toward ending 20 years of separatist violence. Speaking after a key round of talks with officials in Paris, Corsica's politicians said they were satisfied with proposals that opened the door for the island eventually to make its own laws.    (Reuters)

news.abstract: With full United Nations membership on the horizon and a recent vote supporting economic alignment with the European Union, Switzerland seems ready to break with the neutrality of its past. news.title: Q & A / Adolf Ogi : Switzerland in No Rush to Join the EU

news.abstract: Arabs of East Jerusalem follow reports from Camp David summit with anticipation and anxiety, as well as quiet ambivalence about radical political and economic change if status of Jerusalem is altered; photo; Christian Arabs are alarmed by reports that control of Christian sites is also under discussion; three patriarchs of major Christian churches issue unusual joint protest against any division (M)
news.title: Jerusalem Arabs Look Expectantly and Anxiously to Camp David

news.abstract: Leaders of South Africa, Nigeria and Algeria hold news conference in Tokyo to lambast major powers for not acting more swiftly on debt relief and other issues vital to third-world economic growth; photo of Olusegun Obansanjo and Thabo Mbeki; session is held during economic summit meeting; third-world leaders meet with delegations from industrialized nations and with heads of several international corporations (S)
news.title: Africans Fault Rich Nations On Aid to the World's Poor

news.abstract: Okinawa, Japan's choice as site of economic summit meeting, is backwater province plagued by tragic past and lacking infrastructure to handle major international gathering; Japanese and American officials fret about potential for mishap and mayhem, given Okinawans' anger at large US military presence; recent arrest of US marine accused of molesting schoolgirl heightens outrage among islanders who have vowed to disrupt summit meeting; about 27,000 people form human chain around Kadena Air Base; photo; map; Pres Clinton is first US president to visit Okinawa since it reverted back to Japan in 1972 (M)

news.abstract: Alassane Ouattara, mild-mannered international banker, vows to win presidential election in Ivory Coast even though constitutional amendment before voters on July 23 is intended to disqualify him; accuses country's military rulers, led by Gen Robert Guei, of trying to hold on to power; photo (M)

news.abstract: Just over a year ago, a politically floundering Gerhard Schroeder came to London and met Europe's preeminent politician, Tony Blair, to share his aura of invincibility and embrace Mr. Blair's Third Way brand of moderate, center-left politics.

news.title: Chipping Away at Embargo Reflects a New Vision of Cuba

news.abstract: Tar-like oil from breakup of tanker Erika continues to wash onto beaches at La Turballe and elsewhere in Brittany; towns have been caught in a sort of moral quandary for months about whether to speak up and demand that government do something about pollution or to stay mum and avoid publicizing the problem; only people who have houses in La Turballe or prepaid vacations are returning this summer; some of merchants say their business is off by as much as 50 percent; photo; map (M)

news.abstract: Ruth Werner, colorful, daring and successful Soviet spy, dies at 93; her life and espionage exploits reviewed; photo (M)
news.title: Ruth Werner, Colorful and Daring Soviet Spy, Dies at 93

news.abstract: Jorg Haider, whose party's entry into Austrian government was reason 14 other European Union members imposed sanctions on Austria, is technically not in power, but he does not remain in obscurity; on domestic issues, most of his campaign promises have been ignored, but on issue of European Union sanctions, he is very influential; sanctions have done no economic damage, but they humiliate Austrians; Haider has demanded referendum asking Austrians whether they want Austria to use its veto to block all European Union actions until sanctions are lifted; recent poll shows 70 percent favor that move; photo (M)
news.title: Austria Politician Sometimes Down but Never Out

news.abstract: Annette Eddie-Callagain, former United States Air Force lawyer stationed in Okinawa, is waging war on American servicemen who leave after their tour of duty and refuse to pay support for children they fathered with Okinawan women; until recently, there was little that thousands of abandoned Okinawan women and children could do; there is no agreement in force between Japan and United States to make them pay child support; despite lack of bilateral agreement, Eddie-Callagain, now in private practice, is taking her clients' cases directly to child enforcement offices in each of 50 state governments in United States, in hope they will prosecute deadbeat fathers in family court; Amerasian children are treated badly in Japanese public schools, which are notorious for bullying children who do not fit in; photos (M)
news.title: A Hard Life for Amerasian Children

news.title: John Campbell, 88, an Expert On American Foreign Policy

news.title: Deutsche Telekom Deal: Did Barriers Fall in Europe, Just to Rise in the U.S.?

news.abstract: Maria Bernal, former mistress of Raul Salinas, imprisoned brother of Mexico's former president, Carlos Salinas de Gortari, writes lurid memoir describing scandalous affair with Salinas that in early 1990's fed public anger with Institutional Revolutionary Party; book, Raul Salinas and I, gives details of sex, graft and abuse of power that are likely to fuel resentments and desire for reform that led Mexicans to vote governing party out; photos (M)
news.title: Lurid Memoir Reminds Mexicans of Salinas Days

news.title: Perils of Summer Travel /Dos and Don'ts for a Happy Holiday : Scams and Land Mines:Avoiding Headaches (and Worse) in Asia

news.abstract: Carolyn McAskie, UN's emergency relief coordinator, is seeking to bring its existing relief agencies into common effort to alleviate plight of millions of internally displaced people, mostly forgotten victims of war who are not regarded as refugees and are struggling to survive without much international help; American UN ambassador, Richard C Holbrooke, is skeptical about so-called collaborative approach and favors designating a new or lead agency to deal with problem (M)
news.title: A New Crisis Over Refugees Adrift in Their Own Lands

news.abstract: Approximately one million Azerbaijani refugees who fled Nagorno-Karabakh after outbreak of fighting in 1992 between Armenians and Azerbaijanis remain scattered throughout 40 or more camps in Azerbaijan, former Soviet republic whose promised oil riches have yet to materialize; they are insufficiently cared for by their government and on verge of abandonment by international aid organizations; Western diplomats and humanitarian workers say Azerbaijani government is using camps as political pawns in its efforts to negotiate return of Nagorno-Karabakh, which represents 20 percent of its former territory and is occupied by ethnic Aremenians; government reached cease-fire with Armenian forces but no peace agreement that would allow refugees to return home; photos; map (M)
news.title: Hope Erodes for Azerbaijan's Sea of Refugees

news.abstract: EUROPE    YUGOSLAVIA: NEW LAWS AID MILOSEVIC  Yugoslavia's federal Parliament approved new election laws that provide President Slobodan Milosevic with the legal framework to stay in power. The laws define new election procedures under which a president is elected by a majority in a popular vote, regardless of turnout, in a country where the opposition may boycott the polls. They also allow the president a second four-year term. Mr. Milosevic, who was elected in 1997 after serving two terms as president of Serbia, is widely expected to run.   (AP)

news.title: Battle Heats Up as Airbus and Boeing Showcase Rival Visions

news.title: 113 Die in First Crash of a Concorde

news.abstract: EUROPE    BRITAIN: NANNY'S PARENTS CLEARED  The parents of Louise Woodward, a former nanny who was convicted in Massachusetts for the second degree murder of a baby in her care, were cleared of trying to defraud an appeal fund set up for their daughter. Judge John Roberts ordered jurors in Chester to find Gary and Susan Woodward, both 44, not guilty of defrauding the fund of more than $13,500, saying the prosecution failed to prove some of the money in the fund was not donated solely for the parents' use. The conviction of Louise Woodward, now 22, was later downgraded to manslaughter and she was freed after serving 279 days in jail.   (AP)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Palestinian officials say they will presss ahead with plans to declare independent state on Sept 13 in wake of failure of Camp David talks to produce accord; hold Yasir Arafat made all concessions possible from Palestinian side before talks; say firm stance he apparently took at talks will boost his standing among Palestinians; blame Israeli Prime Min Ehud Barak for impasse; photo (M)
news.title: Arafat's Allies Say He Stands Taller at Home for Firmness at Talks

news.abstract: Canada prepares to open Trans Canada Trail, new 10,000-mile network that will link Atlantic, Pacific and Arctic Oceans; building of trail, billed as world's longest recreational trail, has become exercise in nation building as thousands have volunteered for relay teams snaking way across nation with water from three oceans for Sept inauguration, near Ottawa; 250,000 Canadians have donated money for trail; map (M)
news.title: A Long Long Trail Is Awinding, Right Across Canada

news.title: Hero's Welcome for Arafat, From Those Who Showed Up

news.abstract: Pres Clinton's praise for Israeli Prime Min Ehud Barak at end of failed Camp David peace talks means Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat may get less international sympathy and financial aid than he hoped if he declares Palestinian state unilaterally in Sept; Barak has been working to tilt world opinion back toward Israel since he took office year ago; his aides say he believes he has made Israel seem more reasonable party in peace effort and perhaps even bolstered Israel's ties with United States; Arafat seen having won needed domestic support (M)

news.abstract: Senate, under strong pressure from Clinton administration to act on stalled China trade bill, votes to open debate, overcoming procedural hurdle to schedule full consideration of measure in early September; bill, which was passed by House with sense of urgency in May, has become hostage to other legislative goals, efforts to punish China for weapons proliferation, political maneuvering and general gridlock (M)
news.title: Playing for (Political) Time on China Trade

news.abstract: Prim Min Ehud Barak and Yasir Arafat make it clear that they are eager to put failed Camp David talks behind them and move forward with renewed peace effort; two sides confirm that negotiators will meet on July 30 at border of Gaza Strip, and say that ideas floated at Camp David have carried peace effort further than ever before; two leaders suggest that some form of agreement, perhaps only partial and possibly excluding deal-breaking issue of Jerusalem, may yet be possible in weeks and months ahead; photo (M)
news.title: An Eagerness For New Talks In the Mideast

news.abstract: Opening of Arctic to commercial navigation, result of global warming, could bring biggest change in American shipping routes since Panama Canal opened in 1914, situation that concerns environmentalists and native Americans who rely on polar sea for basic items; over all, late summer icecap of North Pole has shrunk 6 percent over last 20 years, and average thickness of Arctic icecap has thinned 42 percent since 1950's; some scientists say that if these trends continue, polar icecap, which covers 80 percent of Arctic Ocean at its September minimum, could vanish every summer within next 50 years; even now, shipping lines are finalizing plans to send freighters with reinforced hulls steaming in summer months through Northeast Passage; photos; map (M)
news.title: Arctic Shortcut for Shipping Raises New Fears in Canada

news.abstract: EUROPE    NORTHERN IRELAND: GUERRILLAS FREED  Eighty-six hardened guerrilla fighters walked free from prison in the last wave of 428 early releases of convicted bombers and killers mandated by the Northern Ireland peace accord. The Maze prison, home to 1,800 inmates during the years of sectarian violence that claimed more than 3,600 lives, was left with only 15 prisoners and is to be closed by the end of the year.   Warren Hoge (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: JOLO, Philippines—  Jewelers are trekking into the jungle surrounding this once-flourishing commercial center of the southern Philippines in search of new customers for gold and jade. Gun dealers are offering American and Chinese rifles and pistols. Drug dealers provide shabu, an amphetamine called the "poor man's cocaine," produced in makeshift local laboratories or smuggled from China.
news.title: Ransom Money Buys Guns, Gold and Jade : Filipino Rebels Discover Kidnapping Is Lucrative

news.abstract: 1,000th anniversary of Leif Ericson's landing on L'Anse Aux Meadows, establishing short-lived Viking colony on Newfoundland's northernmost tip, is re-enacted by group of Icelandic men, who sailed from Greenland aboard replica of old Viking vessel; commemmoration is part of Newfoundland's efforts to shake off label as Canada's poorest province; long isolated from rest of North America, it is well on way to meeting self-imposed goal of attracting one tourist each year for each of 540,000 residents; map; photos (M)

news.abstract: ASIA    INDIA: TOP ACTOR KIDNAPPED  Rajkumar, one of southern India's best-known movie stars, left, has been kidnapped by Veerappan, one of India's most notorious criminals, the police said. The actor, who is active in politics, was abducted from his farmhouse in Gajanur village in the state of Tamil Nadu, along with his son-in-law and two other men. The police said Mr. Veerappan, who has kidnapped other people, usually for ransom, had threatened the actor. The kidnappers left an audio cassette with the family, saying a government representative should contact the gang's mediator for demands.   Barry Bearak (NYT)

news.abstract: THE AMERICAS    MEXICO: PLEA TO END DRUG CERTIFICATION -- President-elect Vicente Fox will propose ending Washington's certification of Latin American countries' anti-drug efforts when he meets with President Clinton on Aug 24, said Aguilar Zinser, a foreign relations adviser to Mr. Fox. The certification program has been criticized as a symbol of American domination, and countries that refuse to take part risk losing economic benefits. Mr. Zinser argued that the United States should instead help set up a regional anti-narcotics group made up of countries fighting the drug trade. Tensions were particularly high in the state of Merida, where the latest results showed a pro-Chavez candidate, Florencio Porras, edging out the incumbent, Gov. William Davila, by less than 1 percent.   (Reuters)
