news.abstract: Israeli Prime Min Ehud Barak's political problems deepen as his right-wing opponents vow new efforts to bring down his government; Likud Party leader Ariel Sharon calls for new elections; warns his coalition will call Parliament, set to begin three-month vacation, back into session if Barak tries to 'sneak' through Palestinian peace accord; bars division of Jerusalem; Moshe Katsav, first Likud candidate ever elected president, is sworn in amid turmoil and consternation within remnants of Barak's battered coalition; photo (M)
news.title: Israel's Leader Faces Turmoil on All Sides

news.abstract: Members of Sept 30th Foundation have been holding weekly protest in Port-au-Price, Haiti, since 1997 against beatings, rapes and murders committed under former military regime; are part of national movement seeking to end tradition of impunity that has allowed those with money or political clout to escape judgment; officers that led 1991 coup are finally being brought to trial in absentia, along with soldiers and paramilitary forces accused in massacre during coup era; second trial is expected in case of six policemen accused of executing several gang members last year and of killing witnesses; map; photo (M)
news.title: Port-au-Prince Journal; So That Tyrants Won't Rest, Haitians Keep a Vigil

news.abstract: JERUSALEM, Aug. 1 — Prime Minister Ehud Barak's political problems deepened today as his right-wing opponents, sensing blood with their stunning defeat of Shimon Peres, his presidential candidate, vowed new efforts to bring down his government.
news.title: Israel´s Leader Faces Turmoil on All Side

news.abstract: EUROPE    CROATIA: MISSION TO WASHINGTON  The new, democratic leaders of Croatia have been granted the official visit to Washington that the late president, Franjo Tudjman, was never allowed. President Stipe Mesic and Prime Minister Ivica Racan, opposition leaders elected this year, arrive on Monday for meetings with President Clinton and other administration officials. They have moved Croatia away from Mr. Tudjman's strident nationalism and closer to Western aims in the Balkans, but face huge fiscal problems and unemployment.    Steven Erlanger (NYT)    BRITAIN: GOOD NEWS FOR PETS  Fifteen rabies-free islands -- including Australia, Japan and Hawaii -- will be added to the ''pet passport'' program that allows cats and dogs to enter Britain without being quarantined for six months. The program got under way in February, beginning with 22 rabies-free European countries. Each passport certifies the pet has a microchip implant verifying its identity and that it has been vaccinated and tested. Other regions will be considered for inclusion in the program in the near future, including the continental United States.    (AP)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: UNITED NATIONS, Aug. 1 — Diamonds have become unfashionable as never before among Western powers struggling to snuff out civil wars in Africa. Appalled by pictures of children with limbs hacked off by diamond- smuggling rebels in Sierra Leone and humiliated when those rebels kidnapped international peacekeepers in May, the United States, Britain and several other countries are making control of the diamond trade a foreign policy priority.
news.title: West Hopes to Curtail Diamond Trading, but Without Money and Troops

news.abstract: WASHINGTON, Aug. 1 — The United States and Jordan are close to reaching an agreement to cut trade barriers, the top American negotiator said today.
news.title: U.S. and Jordan Move to Cut Trade Barriers

news.abstract: Indian Prime Min Atal Behari Vajpayee blames Pakistan for massacres in Kashmir in which at least 93 people have been killed in six separate incidents; holds Pakistan has ordered other militant groups to step up attacks in response to bid by Hizbul Mujahedeen for cease-fire and talks; Pakistan and several of groups critical of peace effort deny any role in attacks (M)
news.title: Massacres in Kashmir May Be Effort to Sabotage Peace Initiative

news.abstract: United States and Russia agree to work together to draft and win support for expanded United Nations sanctions against Afghanistan; cooperation aims to force ruling Taliban to end support of Islamic terrorists (M)
news.title: Russians Join U.S. to Seek New Sanctions On Taliban

news.abstract: JOHANNESBURG, Aug. 2 — South Africa's minister of safety and security has ordered an indefinite moratorium on the release of crime statistics, saying the system for collecting such information here in one of the world's most crime-plagued countries is flawed and unreliable.
news.title: South Africa Veils Crime Data, Faulting System

news.abstract: EUROPE    CZECH REPUBLIC: JEWISH CEMETERY -- The government has been sued in the European Court of Human Rights in a dispute over how to preserve a 13th-century Jewish burial ground on the Prague site where an insurance company is building its headquarters. The suit was brought by the Committee for the Preservation of Jewish Cemeteries despite a March agreement between the government and local Jews on encasing the cemetery in concrete, and building above and below it.   Steven Erlanger (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Yugoslav Army says it has arrested two Britons and two Canadians in Montenegro, accusing them of possessing weapons and explosives, in what appears to be another effort to stimulate fears of NATO encirclement before elections next month; arrest comes on heels of detention of four Dutch citizens earlier in week and days of Serbian and Yugoslav Army statements about need to preserve unity of Yugoslavia, which is made up of Serbia and Montenegro (M)
news.title: Yugoslavs Hold 4 Westerners in Arms Case

news.abstract: Trying to maintain a fixed price for books in the Internet age may seem like the fable of King Canute vainly trying to hold back the waves.
news.title: Resistance to E-Commerce Makes Online Book Bargains a Rarity : German Publishers Fight Web Tide

news.abstract: Seven thousands Christian evangelists from around the world turn exhibition center in Utrecht, Netherlands, into one of the most ethnically diverse, but purposefully homogenous, encampments on earth; Billy Graham Evangelistic Association is paying for their transportation and lodging at cost of millions of dollars; nine-day event is also attended by 3,000 others who can stay at hotels; photos; map (M)
news.title: Utrecht Journal; An Evangelist City Built On a World Foundation

news.abstract: CAMP SARMIENTO, Philippines—  The bullet-spattered walls of the local mosque, the crumpled heaps of flimsy homes, the craters by the dirt road all testify to the ferocity of the attack a month ago on what was once the military headquarters of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front.
news.title: Philippines Faces Long Guerrilla War : On Mindanao, a Victory but No Peace

news.abstract: Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother celebrates her 100th birthday, waving to cheering well-wishers from Buckingham Palace balcony; photo with her children and grandchildren (M)
news.title: Britain's Queen Mother Marks 100th Birthday

news.abstract: State Dept and Pentagon are at odds over extent of North Korea's nuclear weapons program, arguing over photos or snippets of intelligence from agents; State Department says Pentagon's Defense Intelligence Agency, known for its hawkish outlook, has been painting far too black a picture, surmising on sketchy evidence that North Korea has up to 10 new installations working on a covert nuclear program; DIA says State Department is too willing to overlook reports of suspicious activity; this dispute lies behind the other debate over whether to build a new national missile defense against countries like North Korea (M)
news.title: Ferreting Out North Korea's Nuclear Secrets: U.S. Intelligence Experts at Odds

news.abstract: China criticizes United States for giving Taiwan's president, Chen Shui-bian, a visa to stop in Los Angeles on his way to Caribbean and expresses indignation at the island's annual effort to join United Nations (S)
news.title: China Objects to Taiwan Leader's U.S. Visa

news.abstract: Senior official of Council of Europe warns Belarus that human rights body will refuse to send observers for parliamentary elections planned in October if government of Pres Alexander G Lukashenko fails to ensure that vote is free and fair (S)
news.title: Belarus Is Warned to Conduct a Fair Election

news.abstract: Withdrawal of Israeli troops from Lebanon spells disaster for some 2,000 officers or men of South Lebanon Army, militia force of Christians, Muslims and Druze that had helped Israel maintain its grip; militia members handled many of occupation's less appetizing tasks; with their wives and children, they dash helter-skeklter across border into Israel in cars laden with personal belongings, as towns and villages where they were once overlords are overrun by Hezbollah, militant Islamic guerrilla forces that harassed Israeli forces; photo; map (M)
news.title: For Former Israeli Allies in Lebanon, Refugee Life

news.abstract: peØ
news.title: Peppery Plea For Tolerance From a Chef In Montreal

news.abstract: United Nations peacekeeping troops finally begin spreading out in force along Lebanon's border with Israel, after weeks of haggling over just where border is and 22 years after their presence was first authorized; photo of Finnish troops setting up positions in Lebanon (M)
news.title: U.N. Peacekeepers Arrive to Guard Israel-Lebanon Border

news.abstract: Special report, Crossing Borders, on quiet influx into Germany of Jews from former Soviet Union; Jewish population recently surpassed 100,000 for first time since Hitler dispersed and destroyed prewar community of more than 500,000; many Germans feel re-establishment of Jewish community represents victory over Nazis and what they tried to do, but ambivalence and hostility also exist over Jewish immigration in German population whose full range of feelings over new arrivals is unknown for simple reason that they have never been consulted; awkward moment has been reached in German-Jewish relations as Jews pour at rate of 5,000 per year with support of state payments of tens of millions of dollars amid rising impatience with Holocaust-induced obligations; with recent agreement for multibillion-dollar payment to Nazi-era slave laborers and three major Jewish institutions under construction in new capital of Berlin, Germans have feeling of 'enough already' (L)
news.title: Former Soviet Jews Find Uneasy Peace in Germany

news.abstract: Astronomers at University of California (Berkley), MacDonald Observatory at Texas University and Geneva Observatory (Switzerland) report discovery of 10 new planets as well as tantalizing hints of another multiplanet system; Drs Debra A Fischer, Michel Mayor and William Cochran will make official announcement at International Astronomical Union meeting this week in Manchester (England) (M)
news.title: Scientists to Announce Discovery of 10 Planets

news.abstract: Holy Theological School of Chalki, one of most historic and important seminaries in Orthodox Christianity which operated for more than 1,000 years before Turkish government closed it in 1971, remains shuttered under law that gives government control over higher education in religious and military affairs; authorities insist that school must remain closed, despite appeals of Orthodox leaders and Turkey's allies, most recently Pres Clinton; while primary motive for law was to impose government authority over training Islamic clerics, it has ended up snaring theological seminary run by Greek Orthodox Church; photo; maps (M)
news.title: Historic Seminary in Turkey Is Ready but Empty

news.abstract: British government says it will urgently press for stricter laws on child molesting but resists widespread calls for public identification of released violators, who have been associated with current vigilante attacks nationwide (M)
news.title: Britain Fights Tide of Anti-Pedophile Attacks

news.abstract: Egyptian state prosecutor today expands list of accusations against Saad Eddin Ibrahim, prominent democracy advocate detained since June 30 without being formally charged, to include espionage for US; Ibrahim and supporters believe imprisonment is meant to prevent him from monitoring parliamentary elections scheduled for November; Pres Hosni Mubarak's National Democratic Party holds 97 percent of seats in People's Assembly, but elections have usually drawn charges of voter fraud; Egyptian Constitutional Court has ruled that last three parliamentary elections were flawed (M)
news.title: Egypt Says Democracy Backer Spied for U.S.

news.abstract: Map of Mexico City's 70,000-odd streets, with plethora of esoteric and surreal street names, is like literary masterpiece; many streets have same names, and guide reads as if mapmakers translated encyclopedia, cut work into confetti and sprinkled it over city; maps; photo (M)
news.title: Mexico City Journal; In a City Where Good Luck Meets Hope, Signs of Magic

news.abstract: Two Jewish cemeteries are desecrated in western German state of Rhineland-Palatinate and explosive device is found outside Jewish family's home in Bavaria, contributing to climate of mounting concern in Germany over anti-Semitic and anti-immigrant violence by rightists; while attacks reflect activities of small minority, evidence that racist criminals are now better armed and organized has alarmed government of Chancellor Gerhard Schroder, which is promoting new initiative in which famous Germans will exhort nation via advertising campaign to show zero tolerance for racists; recent bombing in Dusseldorf, which wounded nine people including six Jews, noted; map (M)
news.title: New Attacks Raise Fears About Anti-Semitism in Germany

news.abstract: South Korea's Pres Kim Dae Jung, worried about slow pace of financial reforms and stubbornly high debts of its big businesses and banks, replaces almost half of his 19-member cabinet, including nation's top economic officials; changes are almost entirely related to performance of economy, which made remarkable recovery since severe crisis nearly three yaers ago but has lately shown signs of stress; most significant change is appointment of Jin Nyum, former planning and budget minister in charge of privatizing state-run companies, as new minister of finance and economy replacing Lee Hun Jai; photo (M)
news.title: South Korea Replaces Top Economic Officials

news.abstract: Article on Russian government's effort to reconsolidate control over lucrative vodka industry that has set off latest round of business battles; country is riveted on struggle for control of Krystall factory near Moscow that makes Stolichnaya brand and is one of its oldest vodka-producing plants; map; photo (M)
news.title: Moscow Journal; With Bunkers Manned, Vodka War Is in Stalemate

news.abstract: Indonesia's Pres Abdurrahman Wahid apologizes in state of the union speech for falling short of expectations as country struggles to build working democracy and says he will name executive minister to bring order to his flailing administration; says he will concentrate more on foreign affairs in future and create sort of prime ministerial post to handle day-to-day domestic administration; admired for his integrity, democratic ideals and intellect, he has drawn constant criticism for disorganized and impulsive leadership style (M)
news.title: Indonesia's Quirky Leader Apologizes and Pledges Order

news.abstract: EUROPE    YUGOSLAVIA: TERROR CHARGES FOR 4 WESTERNERS -- The Yugoslav Army says it will press terrorism charges against two Canadians and two Britons arrested in Montenegro last week. Britain has described its two citizens, Adrian Prangnell and John Yore, as policemen helping to train a new force in Kosovo. They were traveling with the Canadians, Shaun Going, who also worked in Kosovo, and his nephew Liam Hall. Like many Westerners visiting Montenegro, the four did not have Yugoslav visas. Dutch officials are also seeking access to four of their nationals arrested some three weeks ago in Serbia and accused of plotting to kidnap President Slobodan Milosevic.   (Reuters)    YUGOSLAVIA: NEW MILOSEVIC CHALLENGER -- Formalizing the breach in opposition ranks and dimming chances of voting out Mr. Milosevic, a coalition chose a new challenger, Vojislav Kostunica, left, to run against him. Most opposition parties endorsed Mr. Kostunica, a moderate nationalist. But the Serbian Renewal Movement, the single largest opposition party, chose another candidate, the Belgrade mayor, Vojislav Mihajlovic.   (AP)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: TEHRAN—  Iran's conservative leadership on Tuesday closed the country's last major progressive newspaper, just days after the supreme leader, Ayatollah Sayed Ali Khamenei, declared that the progressive press threatened the national interest.
news.title: Iran's Conservative Press Court Claims New Victim

news.abstract: Malaysian convicts Anwar Ibrahim, former deputy prime minister, of sodomy and sentences him to nine years in prison; trial called into question motives of Malaysia's leaders and credibility of courts and exposed deeply traditional nation to sordid spectacle; Anwar charges Prime Min Mahathir Mohamad orchestrated conspiracy to destroy him and scores judiciary for doing Mahathir's bidding; court also finds Anwar's brother, Sukma Darmawan, guilty of sodomy; sentences him to six years and four strokes with rattan cane; both men were convicted of engaging in homosexual relationship with family's former driver; Anwar escaped caning because of his age; plans to appeal sentence, which supporters expect to spur political unrest; there is little evidence outside courthouse of outrage that drew thousands to streets after Anwar's corruption conviction (M)
news.title: End of a Malaysian Drama, and Very Likely of a Career

news.abstract: WASHINGTON—  Vice President Al Gore warmly introduced his running mate Tuesday in Tennessee, saying Senator Joseph Lieberman, as the first Jew on a U.S. major-party presidential ticket, offered Americans an opportunity "to tear down a mighty wall of division."
news.title: Gore and Running Mate Hail 'Common Ideals'

news.abstract: Chilean Supreme Court divests Gen Augusto Pinochet of his senatorial immunity, removing legal hurdle to charging former dictator with role in kidnapping, torture and murder of thousands of people during his 17-year rule; demonstrators hail decision, Santiago; decision, which also ratifies legal doctrine that anyone who disappeared during dictatorship and is still missing is victim of ongoing kidnapping not covered by amnesty, will likely lead to prosecution of dozens of other retired military and police officers; ruling provokes veiled sniping between Pres Ricardo Lagos, Socialist, and army commander Gen Ricardo Izurieta, who has tried to coexist with civilian presidents and keep right-wing elements at bay; Izurieta makes provocative visit to Pinochet's home to express army's support for him; photo (M)
news.title: Pinochet Ruled No Longer Immune From Prosecution

news.abstract: Gen Barry R McCaffrey, visiting Mexico as United States drug policy director, lauds Pres-elect Vicente Fox's transition team; says he shares Fox's opposition to American drug-certification program but sees no chance that Congress will end it soon (M)
news.title: McCaffrey Voices Confidence in Mexico's Anti-Drug Efforts

news.abstract: Russia detains number of suspects in terrorist bombing of Moscow underground pedestrian walkway; says none can so far be directly linked to blast; Pres Vladimir V Putin rebukes Mayor Yuri M Luzhkov for blaming Chechen rebels without proof; says Russia will complete military campaign in Chechnya and finish off terrorists; security forces scour subway stations and passageways for more bombs; reportedly find explosives at railway station (M)
news.title: Moscow Arrests Suspects but Can't Link Any to Fatal Bombing

news.abstract: MIDDLE EAST    EGYPT: DEFENDING PEACE EFFORTS -- In the first high-level response to Clinton administration critics, Osama el-Baz, an aide to President Hosni Mubarak, gave a spirited defense of the Egyptian role in advancing Arab-Israeli peace. ''It is utter nonsense to think we are urging the Palestinian negotiators to harden their positions,'' he said. ''We have every interest to encourage a closing of the gap between the parties.''    Susan Sachs (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Iran's reformist Parliament shows its determination to forge ahead with social change and grant women additional rights by raising marriage age, changing law allowing fathers to marry off daughters as young as 9; will probably raise age to 15 or 16, although many reformers favor 18 (M)
news.title: Iran Assembly Pushes on Women's Rights

news.abstract: Highly classified intelligence report reportedly warns that deploying American national missile defense could spur China to expand its nuclear arsenal tenfold and lead Russia to place multiple warheads on ballistic missiles; says Chinese expansion would prompt buildups by India and Pakistan; report underscores warnings by opponents that Clinton administration's proposal for limited defense system could lead to new arms race with Russia and, to lesser extent, in Asia; also underscores emerging threat to United States from missile proliferation (M)
news.title: STUDY SAID TO FIND U.S. MISSILE SHIELD MIGHT INCITE CHINA

news.abstract: SEOUL—  The North Korean leader Kim Jong Il, apparently signaling a shift in the North's long-standing insistence that U.S. troops leave South Korea, has opened the way to having at least some of them stay here, analysts said Wednesday.
news.title: A North Korean Shift On Opposing U.S. Troops?

news.abstract: Rev Radivoje Panic, having watched as Albanians fled from Kosovo and then as Serbs were driven from their homes, now serves at last remaining Orthodox church in town of Kosovo Polje, the Church of St Nicholas; few Serbs come to church, which is surrounded by barbed wire and patrolled by troops, mostly the old and those who want to light candles for the dead; Panic comments; map; photo (Kosovo Polje Journal) (M)
news.title: Kosovo Polje Journal; His Serbian Flock Scattered, the Priest Reflects

news.abstract:
EUROPE

NORTHERN IRELAND: NO OBJECTIONS TO A PARADE
Residents of the main Catholic neighborhood of Londonderry have dropped objections to a parade by 30,000 Protestants through the city on Saturday after rare direct talks between the rival communities produced agreements on limiting routes and reducing the police presence. Under an agreement hailed as a model for settling disputes during the so-called summer marching season, the Bogside Residents Association will not protest the annual parade by the Apprentice Boys organization celebrating the relief of the city in 1689 from the siege by the forces of the Catholic King James II.   Warren Hoge (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Basque violence has exploded since last December, when separatists, angry at what they saw as lack of progress in negotiations with Spanish government, ended a 14-month truce; since then ETA has taken responisibility for widening wave of death and destruction; Spaniards are angry over renewed violence; vigils have been held across the country, and more than half a people marched recently in Madrid to protest ETA's resort to more assassinations and car bombings; scene in Durango described; map; photo (M)
news.title: Fear Spreads as Spanish and Basque Blood Flows

news.abstract: Saad Eddin Ibrahim, Egyptian human rights activist who has been under investigation, is released on bail after being held in prison for 45 days without being charged; photo (M)
news.title: Russians Say Anti-Mine Group Aids Rebels

news.abstract: French investigators looking into crash of Air France Concorde last month say that 16-inch piece of metal found on runway probably caused a tire to blow out, sending debris from it through fuel tanks and starting fire that erupted as plane took off (M)
news.title: Concorde Panel Says Metal Strip Probably Caused Tire to Burst

news.abstract: Canadian officials, acting to protect their country's emerging diamond industry, are taking steps to ensure that their stones are never confused with 'blood diamonds' that help to finance guerrilla armies in Sierra Leone and Angola; Royal Canadian Mounted Police are developing technology to 'fingerprint' diamonds, identifying them by trace impurities that could be traced to known mines; map; photos (M)
news.title: Canada Tries to Make Clear Its Diamonds Are Different

news.abstract: Czech officials and private businesses are taking measures to guard against possibility of violent protests accompanying meeting of International Monetary Fund and World Bank in Sept; map; photo (M)
news.title: Czech Police and Army Get Ready for Protests at I.M.F.-World Bank Meeting

news.abstract: US temporarily halts trade in Argentine beef because of concerns of possible outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease in Argentina (M)
news.title: U.S., Seeing Threat of Disease, Halts Trade in Argentine Beef

news.abstract: EUROPE    POLAND: WALESA CLEARED -- Lech Walesa, who fought Communist rule for two decades before its fall in 1989, was cleared of collaborating with the Communist-era secret police and will be allowed to run for the presidency, which he lost in 1995. He was forced to defend his reputation in a special screening court, which dismissed suggestions in old police files that he spied on fellow dissidents. Mr. Walesa, the founder of Solidarity, was scrutinized under a 1998 law that requires candidates to declare whether they cooperated with the Communist secret services. There is no penalty for admitting collaboration, but anyone found to have lied is banned from public office for 10 years.    (AP)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Gen Augusto Pinochet and his supporters have started campaign to gain support to help him avert trial on charges of kidnapping, murder and torture (M)
news.title: A New Drive Gathers Steam To Avert Trial For Pinochet

news.abstract: Prince Soulivong Savang, exiled grandson of last king of Laos, seeks to reassert his claim of leadership; prince escaped from Laos 20 years ago, fearing he would be killed by Communists who had taken control of country and who had killed his grandfather, father and other relatives; says he is more interested in restoring democracy than in future of monarchy; prince, who lives in Paris, has been following reports of student unrest and surreptitious return of Vietnamese military to Laos; he is also concerned about domination of Thai business on fragile economy of Laos; prince is in New York on visit to Laotioan exile communities in United States; photo (M)
news.title: Exiled Laotian Prince Seeks a New Role

news.abstract: North and South Koreans involved in family reunions that will bring 100 North Koreans south and take 100 southerners north, are at forefront of effort to rebuild single Korean nation by first mending hearts broken long ago; exchange of family members separated by Korean War was given top priority at historic summit meeting in June between South Korean president, Kim Dae Jung, and North Korean leader, Kim Jong Il; meetings are regarded as strongest evidence to date that Kim Jong Il is committed to rapprochement; information is tightly controlled in North Korea; Kim is taking big gamble by allowing North Koreans even tiny glimpse into lives of their more affluent relatives in South Korea; photos; map (M)
news.title: Koreans, Divided by War, Await Loved Ones' Return

news.abstract: San Juan Chamula, in Chiapas State, is epicenter in Mexico's lingering conflict between Catholics and evangelical Christians; battles--often pitting Indians determined to preserve traditional customs against those who want change--have blazed for 30 years, dividing fathers from sons, turning violent, leaving hundreds dead and at least 30,000 displaced in Chiapas alone; that may be changing with new church, Prince of Peace Temple, which is being built with donations trickling in from evangelical groups across country; many evangelicals who left Chiapas to flee religious persecution have returned to help build church; Catholics seem to have begun grudging acceptance of growing evangelical congregation in their midst; photo; map (M)
news.title: In a Warring Mexican Town, God's Will Is the Issue

news.abstract: Taiwan's new president, Chen Shui-bian, abruptly cancels informal reception with members of Congress after vigorous protests from China and expressions of concern by State Dept; reception had been organized by Rep Sam Gejdenson as chance for Chen to meet bipartisan group of lawmakers; Clinton administration officials say they do not favor Chen's meeting with lawmakers or other American officials in way that could be construed as official contacts; Gejdenson, a Democrat, issues curt statement about Chen being pressured by administration and State Dept to refrain from meeting members of Congress; cancellation appears to avoid potentially divisive diplomatic confrontation with China (M)
news.title: Taiwan Chief Drops Plan For Meeting In California

news.abstract: United Nations criticizes Lebanon for its very limited deployment of soldiers and police into south, 10 weeks after Israel ends its 22-year occupation of region; UN peacekeepers on ground hint that their mission, begun in 1978, could end when latest mandate expires in six months; Lebanon's refusal to have its forces go all the way to border is widely seen as move by Syria, which has virtually controlled Lebanon for decade, to maintain pressure on Israel to return Golan Heights; Lebanese government says it will deploy troops on border only when complete regional peace agreement is reached, including turnover of Golan Heights and return of Palestinian refugees (M)
news.title: U.N. Criticizes Lack of Help By Lebanon

news.abstract: Interview with Mexico's Pres-elect Vicente Fox, who says he will press US to open border to Mexican workers during upcoming visit to US and will begin dialogue on formation of North American common market; photo (M)
news.title: Fox Urges Opening of U.S.-Mexican Border to Build New Partnership

news.abstract: PARIS—  After the Web comes ... not the Matrix, but the Grid. And it's being brought to you by the same Swiss lab that created the World Wide Web.
news.title: 'The Grid' Is Next Wave of Computing, Labs Hope

news.abstract: White House is prepared to convene new summit between Israelis and Palestinians, but has concluded that effective deadline for final settlement during Clinton presidency is end of September; senior official says Pres Clinton is prepared to reconvene summit, but only if he is assured that Israelis and Palestinians are ready to settle all outstanding issues, including Jerusalem (M)
news.title: Washington Feels Time Is Short for Restarting the Mideast Talks

news.abstract: China is seeking to put end to tradition of bigamous conduct, viewing wholesale adultery as social menace; is focusing efforts of 'concubine villages' that have sprouted in Guangdong province and elsewhere where hundreds of women live as mistresses or common-law wives of Hong Kong men, whose jobs require them to spend days or weeks at time on mainland; New Garden Village, one of most notorious concubine villages in Dongguan described; maps; photos (M)
news.title: Dongguan Journal; For Hong Kong Men, Mistresses on the Mainland

news.abstract: Large number of teachers are dying of AIDS in Ivory Coast and other parts of Africa, weakening continent's already troubled educational system; Ivory Coast, long economic crossroads as richest nation in French-speaking Africa, has highest rate of AIDS and HIV in region; nearly 11 percent of adult population is believed to carry virus, which killed 72,000 in 1999; government study found 641 educators died of AIDS between September 1996 and August 1998; ignorance regarding disease and condom use appears to be one of main causes of spread; difficulty of educating largely illiterate population is emphasized by fact that most teachers are not knowledgeable about disease either; spread of disease in neighboring countries and its high toll among educators discussed; maps; photo (M)
news.title: AIDS Cuts a Swath Through Africa's Teachers

news.abstract: Russian nuclear submarine Kursk plunges to seabed in Barents Sea during naval exercises, possibly after explosion on board, trapping more than 100 crew members 450 feet below surface; officials say vessel is badly damaged; are unsure how many of crew are alive or how long they can survive; Russian navy begins desperate rescue attempt; says odds of saving crew are slim; says submarine carried no nuclear weapons and that nuclear reactors were turned off, calming fears of possible radioactive contamination; Pres Clinton is briefed about accident and offers US help; American experts say vessel, unlike most Russian submarines, was probably not equipped with pressurized escape chambers that could have carried crew to surface; Russia's loss of at least four nuclear submarines from 1960's through 1989, and crippling of others by reactor malfunctions, fires or other problems recalled; photo; maps (M)
news.title: Frantic Russian Effort To Rescue Crew of Sub

news.abstract: Ethnically mixed families in Kosovo, Serbia, are under threat both in Kosovo and rest of Serbia and are seeking refuge elsewhere; many have found refuge in Sarajevo, Bosnia, and elsewhere in Balkans; are seeking help from UN high commissioner for refugees to emigrate; photos; map (M)
news.title: Mixed Blood Makes Balkan Outcasts

news.abstract: Crackdown on reformers in Iran continues with detention of popular satirist, Ibrahim Nabavi, and newspaper columnist, Mohammad Qoochani; both are interrogated by hard-line court and detained; worked for banned daily (M)
news.title: 2 More in Iran Are Detained In Crackdown On the Press

news.abstract: Gloom deepens in Sri Lanka as peace efforts of Prime Min Chandrika Kumaratunga, which would preserve Sri Lanka as unified nation while satisfying demands of Tamil minority for greater self-rule, collapse; many Sri Lankans hold out little hope that 17-year war with Tamil rebels will end soon; photo (M)
news.title: As Peace Plan Falters, Sri Lanka's War Has No End in Sight

news.abstract: Italy is awash in annual summertime sex surveys, which fill vacuum of political intrigue and soccer championships; while no country is exempt from weakness for news stories about sun and sexuality, Italy is perhaps one most adept at crafting bold headlines from slimmest scientific findings (M)
news.title: In Summer, Italy Loves Sex Surveys; It's Just Talk

news.abstract: British Airways grounds Concorde fleet after French and British investigators recommend withdrawal of supersonic plane's airworthiness certificate in aftermath of fatal crash in Paris; France says concern is about risks linked to aircraft's tires; Air France grounded its flights after July crash, first in Concorde's history; chronology of Concorde; photo; investigators believe 16-inch piece of metal on runway at de Gaulle Airport probably slashed tire as plane hurtled toward takeoff, creating debris that ruptured fuel tanks; emphasize that ruptured tire should not have such deadly consequences (M)
news.title: With Safety in Doubt, British Ground Concordes

news.abstract: London Journal recalls scandalous 1960's divorce of Margaret, Duchess of Argyll, which left behind tantalizing question of identity of one of her lovers, man photographed naked from neck down; new Channel Four television documentary concludes that two leading suspects, Duncan Sandys and Douglas Fairbanks Jr, were both involved; case recalled; photos; government's concern at time was for potential security breaches, since case coincided with Profumo sex scandal (M)
news.title: London Journal; A Sex Scandal of the 60's, Doubly Scandalous Now

news.abstract: Independence Day, as observed in Srinagar, unhappy summer capital of India's unhappiest state, is eerie kind of national holiday, with almost everyone staying indoors; Indian forces beef up security after Islamic separatist rebels threaten to disrupt celebrations; photo; prevailing sentiment in Kashmir Valley, place of legendary beauty and unremitting bloodshed, is wish for freedom and belief that India will never let go (M)
news.title: Kashmir Endures Its Holiday of Contradictions

news.abstract: COLOMBO, Sri Lanka, Aug. 12 — This war-haunted nation's president, blinded in her right eye by a suicide bomber's attack, still talks of peace. But many ordinary Sri Lankans are more convinced than ever that no end to the country's 17-year conflict with the Tamil rebels is near.
news.title: As Peace Plan Falters, Sri Lanka´s War Has No End in Sight

news.abstract: NEW YORK—  Crude oil prices touched 10-year highs Tuesday thanks to a strengthening world economy that is increasing demand for energy.
news.title: Demand Drives Oil Prices To Decade-High Levels

news.abstract: On their first full day in South Korea, 100 North Koreans get taste of capitalism when they are taken to giant shopping mall in Seoul as part of heavily orchestrated trip to visit relatives; with each Northerner officially allowed to see only five Southern relatives, some who did not make the cut seek quick meetings in mall and other public places; photos (M)
news.title: Like It or Not, North Koreans Tour a Mall in Seoul

news.abstract: Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, visiting Argentina on Latin American tour, pledges that she will work to declassify United States government documents that may shed light on kidnappings of hundreds of children from dissidents captured and imprisoned by Argentine military from 1976 to 1983 (M)
news.title: Albright to Try to Shed Light on Missing Argentine Children

news.abstract: Residents of Russian city of Kursk tensely follow attempts to rescue crewmembers from crippled submarine named after city; many local young men are aboard Kursk submarine; map; photo (M)
news.title: Submarine's Namesake City Hurts As Minute After Minute Ticks Away

news.abstract: Plans for celebration of 10th anniversary of German unity on Oct 3 are turning into fiasco, revealing enduring divisions in the country and bitter feuding within Christian Democratic Party; Chancellor Helmut Kohl decides not to attend (M)
news.title: German Party Poopers Do Their Best to Ruin a Celebration

news.abstract: British and French regulators withdraw Concorde's airworthiness certification, effectively ruling world's only commercial supersonic airliner unfit to fly until it can be protected against safety flaws behind last month's fatal crash near Paris (M)
news.title: Concorde Is Stripped of Certification to Fly

news.abstract: British group known as Marie Stopes International, for pioneering champion of birth control, offers vasectomies to Frenchmen, and Bernard Schnakenbourg becomes overnight celebrity by being first to cross Channel and have procedure performed; reaction in France, which is largely Roman Catholic, is largely one of outrage over what is perceived as English attempt to sterilize the French (M)
news.title: British Vasectomy Offer Brings French Outrage

news.abstract: KURSK, Russia, Aug. 16 — Valentina Staroseltseva thought she was lucky, because her draft-age son could have been sent to fight in Chechnya, the worst nightmare of most Russian mothers.
news.title: Submarine´s Namesake City Hurts As Minute After Minute Ticks Away

news.abstract: Though no one knows just what agonies have befallen the men on the Russian submarine Kursk, other seamen who have been trapped beneath the sea describe how quickly the air can turn toxic and serious physical and emotional deterioration can set in.
news.title: Survivors Tell of Submarine Horrors s

news.abstract: Russian naval forces failed again today to dock a rescue vehicle onto the sunken and disabled submarine Kursk as President Vladimir V. Putin ordered his military commanders to accept Western offers of assistance.
news.title: Russia Calls for Help From West As Hope for Sub Survivors Fades

news.abstract: On their first full day in South Korea after half a century, 100 North Koreans — in two controlled groups of 50 — experienced the capitalistic excess of a giant shopping mall today.
news.title: Like It or Not, North Koreans Tour a Mall in Seoul

news.abstract: Many Somalis say warlords there do not wield as much power as they once did, but still enough to make trouble; courts and police units set up by Islamic groups have siphoned off their authority, as have business people, who not only hire their own militias but also provide jobs and money to people other than thugs; warlords' remaining power will be put to test if, as expected, the first Somali government sice 1991 is formed and actually tries to govern; photo (M)
news.title: Mogadishu Journal; A Peace-Starved City Weighs the Warlord Factor

news.abstract: British and French aviation regulators form committee to examine ways to return the Concorde to service under conditions that would protect it against the flaws behind July 25 crash near Paris (S)
news.title: France and Britain Create Panel To Improve Safety of Concordes

news.abstract: Sec Gen Kofi Annan sends Gen Abdulsalami Abubakar of Nigeria to Congo to salvage what is beginning to look like a doomed United Nations peacekeeping mission (M)
news.title: As Peace Mission Deteriorates, U.N. Sends an Envoy to Congo

news.abstract: Turkey's Kurds welcome government's decision to sign two United Nations conventions dating to 1966 that guarantee the social and political rights of minorities; are looking to the government for progress on granting them new rights, including assurances that Kurdish can be spoken freely and that young people can be educated in Kurdish (M)
news.title: Kurds Warily Welcome Turkey's Changes in Human Rights Policy

news.abstract: FRANKFURT—  At precisely 12:20 p.m. on Sunday, a Lufthansa 747 cargo freighter with 55 horses, 44 grooms and two veterinarians on board will taxi ever so gently away from a high-security warehouse at Frankfurt International Airport.
news.title: Sydney-Bound Horses Face Toughest Animal Import Rules on Planet : Hooved Olympians Set for Longest Ride

news.abstract: Independent United Nations watchdog organization, Campaign for United Nations Reform, says Vice Pres Al Gore would give more unqualified support to UN and be more willing to sign international treaties than Gov George W Bush; group had sent questionnaire to both men; Bush said he would never place American troops under UN command and would not pay United States debts to UN until its bureaucracy was reformed and American dues lowered; Gore said US should pay dues 'in full, on time and without condition' but he declined to endorse International Criminal Court, saying its treaty had significant flaws (M)
news.title: U.N. Reform Group Assesses U.S. Candidates

news.abstract: Many Poles and Western diplomats believe that Marian Krzaklewski, Solidarity's current leader and presidential hopeful, was behind charges that Pres Aleksander Kwasniewski and former Pres Lech Walesa spied for Communist secret police; special court has cleared both men, and Kwasniewski, now that he has been cleared, is almost guaranteed re-election; photos (M)
news.title: Poland Spy Inquiry Said to Be a Failed Political Tactic

news.abstract: Vice Adm Mikhail Motsak of Russian Navy says all 118 members of crew of wrecked submarine Kursk are now probably dead; says that in frantic initial hours, survivors trapped in sunken vessel had signaled their comrades on surface to send down air because their sealed compartments were filling with water; say some men may have tried what would have been suicidal exit through rear hatch, causing one of last dry compartments to flood; says most of sailors died in first minutes after still-unexplained explosion sent Kursk crashing to seabed; Norwegian divers with video equipment begin descent to assess damage to Kursk; Motsak, in statement broadcast on state television, says navy is investigating three possible causes of blast: collision with another vessel or World War II mine, or some unknown internal accident that set off explosion; photos; map (M)
news.title: All 118 on Sub Probably Dead, Russians Assert

news.abstract: Colombian government promises full-scale investigation of army attack on elementary school hiking trip that left six children dead; top commanders of army initially blamed guerrillas for deaths, but various witnesses have come forward to say there were no rebels near shootings; episode comes at particularly embarrassing moment for Pres Andres Pastrana, who is preparing for Pres Clinton's six-hour visit on Aug 30 and for Secretary of State Madeleine K Albright to certify whether Colombia has met human rights conditions and is eligible to receive military component of new $1.3 billion aid program (M)
news.title: Colombia Pledges to Investigate Killing of 6 Children by Troops

news.abstract: Hassen Mall, Indian immigrant who became South Africa's first nonwhite judge, dies at age 78 (S)
news.title: Hassen Mall, 78, the First Nonwhite Jurist in South Africa

news.abstract: Team of Norwegian divers finally open damaged outer hatch of Russian submarine Kursk, lying on ocean bed more than 300 feet below surface in Barents Sea following accident, probably caused by onboard explosion; find rear escape chamber flooded but no bodies or any signs of life; rescue teams prepare plan to use ship's crane to rip hatch off vessel and to begin grim task of recovering bodies and lengthy and dangerous mission of salvaging submarines twin nuclear reactors; maps; photo (M)
news.title: NORWEGIAN DIVERS OPEN SUB'S HATCH BUT FIND NO BODIES

news.abstract: Tragedy of sunken nuclear submarine Kursk, and apparent deaths of 188 sailors aboard, rattles residents of Murmansk, port that is home to large contingent of Russian navy personnel; photo (S)
news.title: A Seaport Used to Pain Hurts Again

news.abstract: Correction of map accompanying August 18 article about research on chances of an earthquake at Hayward Fault in Northern California
news.title: Corrections

news.abstract: JAFFNA, Sri Lanka—  The Tamil Tigers, the guerrillas fighting for an independent state in Sri Lanka, are poised for a major offensive intended to consolidate their hold on the Jaffna Peninsula, the commander of government forces on the peninsula warned over the weekend.
news.title: Sri Lankan Army Braces For Major Rebel Offensive

news.abstract: INTERNATIONAL   A3-9    Rescuers Plan to Enter Sunken Russian Sub  Rescue teams were preparing a plan to use a ship's crane to rip a hatch off of the Russian submarine Kursk more than a week after it plunged to the bottom of the Barents Sea. They will then begin recovering the bodies of the 118 crew members and try to salvage the submarine's nuclear reactors.   A1    In a Russian navy town, the tragedy of the sunken submarine has rattled residents and brought a hush to the streets.   A6
news.title: NEWS SUMMARY

news.abstract: Russia's defense minister, Marshal Igor D Sergeyev, defends military's failure to rescue crew of stricken nuclear submarine Kursk, blaming it on budgetary problems of past decade that have 'robbed and stripped' military; suggests military may have erred in rescue attempts, but insists no fundamental mistakes were made; says foreign assistance may have helped save crew; reiterates strongly held theory that Kursk may have collided with another submarine, which suffered severe damage but eventually managed to escape; his less than contrite remarks are seen as partial attempt to quell political storm incident has wreaked on government of Pres Vladimir V Putin; Norwegian divers end rescue operations after opening inner and outer hatches of vessel's escape chamber and finding no signs of life, and after failing in attempts to open rear escape hatch; say entire vessel was flooded; Kursk sank in 350 feet of water after unexplained but powerful explosions sundered hull during military exercises in Barents Sea on August 12; US and British governments categorically deny any of their submarines or surface vessels were involved; photos (M)
news.title: Russians Blame Cuts in Budget For Sub Fiasco

news.abstract: Balkans have become latest gateway to Western Europe for tens of thousands of immigrants from China, South Asia and Middle Eastern countries like Iran and Iraq; Yugoslavia in particular, which has cultivated strong ties with China, has opened gates to thousands of Chinese intent on reaching Western Europe; its consulates in China freely grant tourist visas to Chinese, and legal passage into Yugoslavia eases way for illegal entry to rest of Europe; Bosnia has its own flow of illegal immigrants from Iran and Iraq and other countries with which Muslim-led government in Sarajevo has maintained strong ties, and Croatia is experiencing staggering increase in human traffic; influx underscores growing alarm among Western diplomats and migration officials that sophisticated and far-reaching network of human traffickers from Asia has switched attention from US and is looking to Europe; traffickers have found troubled and unruly countries of former Yugoslavia, with porous borders and lack of immigration laws and agreements, are ideal gateway to West; map; photos (M)
news.title: China's Migrants Find Europe's Open Back Door: The Balkans

news.abstract: Former British security agent David Shayler, who has lived in self-imposed exile for past three years infuriating British government with series of disclosures about Britain's MI-5 and MI-6 ultra-secret security agencies, returns from France to face charges; is taken into custody and later freed on bail; is charged with violations of Official Secrets Act, sweeping law that outlaws unauthorized disclosure of any kind about workings of government; is ex-agent of MI-5 who quit in 1997, citing dissillusionment with agency; photo (M)
news.title: Ex-Intelligence Agent Arrested in Britain on Return From Exile

news.abstract: UN assembles new team of arms inspectors to reenter Iraq within weeks, raising prospect of another confrontation with Pres Saddam Hussein over weapons programs; move comes two years after Iraq halted cooperation with previous group of inspectors, provoking diplomatic crisis and ongoing American and British air strikes; government has warned it will not cooperate with UN's new weapons commission, which Security Council ordered nine months ago in hopes of resolving objections to previous commission by Iraq, Russia and France; new team, with members from 19 countries, will be more accountable to UN Sec Gen Kofi Annan; will be headed by Hans Blix; members will work directly for UN, not for own countries as before; photo (M)
news.title: U.N. READIES TEAM TO CHECK WEAPONS HELD BY THE IRAQIS

news.abstract: Assertions by Russian officials that submarine Kursk sank in Barents Sea after collision, most likely with foreign vessel, echoes suspicions common during cold war, when on more than dozen occasions Russian and Western submarines banged into each other; Russians have long resented fact that many of collisions occurred in or near their waters and amounted to hit-and-run affairs, as American and British spy submarines quickly fled to safety; maps (M)
news.title: Russia's Suspicion of Foreign Sub a Reminder of Cold War Chases

news.abstract: German widow of African killed by neo-Nazis breaks down in court after facing three young men accused of murder in Dessau park; three show no remorse as trial opens; photos; map; slaying of Alberto Adriano has become symbol of virulence of rightist anti-immigrant sentiment in former East Germany, which has twice the unemployment of western Germany (M)
news.title: Neo-Nazis Show No Remorse at Trial, and a German Widow Is Overcome

news.abstract: Pres Clinton defends his decision to sign a waiver freeing up $1.3 billion in anti-drug assistance for Colombia, saying that country is improving on human rights even though government of Andres Pastrana has yet to meet all the conditions imposed by Congress (M)
news.title: Clinton Defends the Outlay Of $1.3 Billion to Colombia

news.abstract: Panel of international experts recommends that United Nations peacekeeping department be enlarged and professionalized, with intelligence-gathering functions that were essentially forbidden during the cold war; urges that more effort go into preventing situations from becoming crises and that peacekeeping officials resist allowing larger countries to exert too much influence over their day-to-day activities; recommendations are sure to displease American isolationists and some third world leaders who fear that a stronger, more independent organization would mean a new kind of colonialism (M)
news.title: U.N. Is Urged to Upgrade Peacekeeping Department

news.abstract: Cambridge University seeks donations to buy collection of letters, notebooks and autographed texts relating to work of Sir Isaac Newton, an alumnus, which is being offered for sale by Earl of Macclesfield; fears that collection will otherwise go abroad or be split among private collectors (M)
news.title: Newton's Alma Mater Is Passing the Hat to Purchase His Papers

news.abstract: MIDDLE EAST    ISRAEL: SHAS CHIEF'S SENTENCE UPHELD -- The Supreme Court denied a request for a new hearing on a three-year jail term for fraud, bribery and breach of trust imposed on Aryeh Deri, former leader of the ultra-Orthodox Shas Party. It ordered Mr. Deri to begin his sentence on Sept. 3. Mr. Deri, a charismatic former interior minister of Moroccan descent who built Shas into a powerful legislative bloc, was convicted of taking bribes at the Interior Ministry.   John F. Burns (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Death of P Rangarajan Kumaramangalam, a popular and lively leader of India's governing party, shakes country's political elite, many of whom believe that he got faulty medical care at one of New Delhi's most prestigious privately run hospitals; quality of health care for hundreds of millions of Indians is acknowledged to be miserable, but country's elected officials, and especially cabinet ministers like Kumaramangalam, are expected to get only the best (M)
news.title: Cabinet Member's Death Puts Spotlight on India's Health System

news.abstract: Pres Clinton's upcoming visit to Colombia comes as country's neighbors fear increased US military aid will step up fighting that could push coca growing, drug trafficking, refugees and conflict across their borders; Colombian conflict has already led to guerilla incursions into Panama and Venezuela, rebel influence among Indian dissidents in Ecuador, and new Colombian plantings of coca and poppies in Peru; regional leaders fear impact of $1.3 billion in additional US aid over next two years to train and equip anti-narcotics brigade; Sec Madeleine Albright, visiting region, hears warnings from nervous Ecuadorean and Brazilian leaders; photo of Pres Gustavo Noboa of Ecuador and Pres Andres Pastrana of Colombia; map (M)
news.title: Neighbors Fear Fallout of Aid To Colombians

news.abstract: Poles feel discontent even though their country's new market economy is flourishing; largest, most successful transformation in central Europe has created two million small- and medium-sized private enterprises, such as wood-processing plant built from scratch by Urszula Malinowska and her husband in Biala Rawska; photos; map; Malinowska, who is likely to vote for reformed Communists, says changes have come with mixed blessings: small businesses do not get much help from government, tax laws are complex and contradictory, and being outside European Union allows Western trading partners to 'take advantage' of Poland; sourness is widely felt by Poles whose rapid progress is nonetheless falling behind their own expectations (M)
news.title: Despite Soaring Prosperity, Poland Still Isn't Sure of Itself

news.abstract: One hundred and thirty evangelical Christians, including three visiting Americans on religious mission, are arrested in Henan Province in central China during revival meeting; detained Chinese are followers of China Fangcheng Church, one of largest of many fervent Protestant groups evanglizing across country without government approval (M)
news.title: China Arrests Evangelicals, Including 3 From the U.S.

news.abstract: Vicente Fox Quesada, next president of Mexico, arrives in Washington to start laying out his vision of US-Mexican relations to present and future leaders of US: Pres Clinton congratulates Fox for winning fairest election in Mexico's history (S)
news.title: Mexican President-Elect Warmly Greeted in Washington

news.abstract: Mexican Supreme Court orders Pres Ernesto Zedillo to turn over to Congress secret banking data relating to questionable financing of Zedillo's 1994 campaign; decision to uphold congressionanl authority marks clear declaration of independence from all-powerful executive branch (S)
news.title: Mexico Court Makes History By Siding With Congress

news.abstract: Rev John Anthony Kaiser, American Roman Catholic priest, is murdered in Kenya; human rights groups suspect someone in government whom Kaiser had angered with frequent, and public, denunciations; he was found shot to death on rural roadside; photo (S)
news.title: American Priest Dies in Kenya, And Authorities Suspect Murder

news.abstract: Pres Clinton will add brief stop in Cairo, Egypt, to trip to Africa, to discuss Middle East peace talks with Pres Hosni Mubarak (S)
news.title: Clinton Adds Mideast Meeting

news.abstract: A New York Times article in editions of Aug. 17 about new information on a 1960s sex scandal in Britain that involved the Duchess of Argyll misattributed a lyric written for "You're the Top," the Cole Porter song inspired by the duchess. The lyric, with a reference to Mussolini, was written by P.G. Wodehouse for the 1935 London production of "Anything Goes." The lyricist was not Mr. Porter.
news.title: Correction

news.abstract: Huang Beiling, Boston-based Chinese poet arrested in Beijing on August 11 in connection with literary journal he edits, will be released and deported to US; is Chinese citizen with permanent-residence status in US; arrest drew protests from literary figures worldwide, as well as from US Embassy in Beijing; police confiscated hundreds of copies of Journal, Tendency, which is published in US, but gve no reason why they detained him; China's State Council Information Office says he was jailed because of illegal business activity (M)
news.title: China Agrees To Free Poet After Protests From Writers

news.abstract: Foreign Min Joschka Fischer is pessimistic about eradication of rightist violence in eastern Germany; says it will take more than generation to overcome wounds of area that remains in 'twilight zone' between democracy and authoritarian tradition; says anti-immigrant violence that is chief focus of German political debate in past month is not confined to eastern Germany (M)
news.title: German Official Pessimistic About Far-Right Violence

news.abstract: United Nations relief coordinator
news.title: U.N. Reports Afghan Curbs Hurt Populace

news.abstract: Lebanon is entering key parliamentary election marked by deepening economic crisis, widespread public cynicism and startlingly open criticism of vote rigging and Syrian domination; Rafik Hariri, multibillionaire builder who has raised hopes for rebirth of glittering Beirut of old, runs free-spending drive to become prime minister again; Pres Emile Lahoud's government attacks him with hours of special programming on state-run television; photo (M)
news.title: Lebanese, Sunk in Crisis, Deride Vote

news.abstract: Somalis, despite mixed feelings about Americans, have strong affection for former Pres George Bush and back his son, Gov George W Bush, in United States presidential race; hope Gov Bush will reverse Pres Clinton's policy against American military involvement, although he has not signaled any plan for re-engagement; are growing optimistic that peace talks now under way in Djibouti may lead to return of government, but say any new government would need some funding (M)
news.title: Somalis Take Close Look At Election In the U.S.

news.abstract: Pres Clinton visits Nigeria in bid to boost nation's transition to civilian rule; meets with Pres Olusegun Obasanjo; speaks to National Assembly; urges Obasanjo to press other oil producers to increase output and cut prices; Obasanjo pledges to seek lower, or at least more stable, prices at Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries summit meeting; Clinton plans to announce series of new aid packages for Nigeria; says he will urge European nations to reschedule their loans to Nigeria and eventually forgive debt if nation stays on reform path; map; photos (M)
news.title: CLINTON IN NIGERIA TO SHOW SUPPORT FOR CIVILIAN RULE

news.abstract: shut-out
news.title: Shut-Out Nigerians Talk Of Leaders With Scorn

news.abstract: Five foreign hostages are released by Muslim separatist kidnappers in southern Philippines for reported $5 million ransom; releases are half-step toward ending four-month-long standoff on island of Jolo; four of freed are from original group of 21, kidnapped at nearby diving resort in Malaysia; fifth is French television reporter, taken hostage after trekking into jungle to film them on July 9; seven other Westerners remain hostage; map; photo (M)
news.title: Philippine Rebels Free 5 Foreign Hostages

news.abstract: Poland's frontier with Belarus will soon become European Union's future eastern border with wild, untameable and unformed east, and burden of blocking illegal trade and immigration across it will fall on Poland, which is being asked by union to erect new, post-Communist barrier near Nieznany Bor as price of membership; maps; photo (M)
news.title: Poland Finds Itself the Border Cop of West Europe

news.abstract: Voting begins in Lebanon's two-stage parliamentary election, overshadowed by Syrian dominance and bitter struggle between current government and its critics; acrimonious campaigns in Mansuriya, Christian heartland of Mount Hermon between Michel Murr, Syrian supporter, and opposition slate headed by wealthy businessman and former ambassador Nassib Lahoud discussed; map (M)
news.title: Tense Election in Lebanon Mired in Bitter Power Plays

news.abstract: Sir Lynden O Pindling, former Bahamas prime minister, dies at age 70; photo (M)
news.title: Lynden Pindling, 70, Who Led the Bahamas to Independence

news.abstract: Pres Clinton urges Nigerians to eliminate taboos associated with AIDS in Africa, and to confront 'tyranny' of disease with same resolve they showed during decades of dictatorship; offers American support for Nigeria's efforts to confront disease, but pledges no new assistance; comments at women's conference in Abuja are bold challenge to Africa, where stigma surrounding AIDS and inadequate public education about dangers have contributed to its spread; Clinton visits rural village of Ushafa with daughter Chelsea for glimpse of how vast majority of Nigerians live; they receive rousing welcome; he winds up two-day visit by encouraging Nigerian businessmen to work to expand economy beyond its heavy reliance on oil; map; photos (M)
news.title: PRESIDENT URGES NIGERIA TO FIGHT TYRANNY OF AIDS

news.abstract: Acoustical tapes made by US nuclear-powered attack submarine Memphis and other vessels contain strong evidence to support leading American theory that onboard explosion, probably misfiring of torpedo, caused sinking of Russian nuclear submarine Kursk in Barents sea with loss of 118 lives; American officials rule out collision with another submarine, as claimed by Russians; say rocket-propelled torpedo being loaded or launched as part of exercise misfired, with its engine and fuel exploding; refuse comment on whereabouts or mission of Memphis and another American submarine that were spying on largest Russian naval exercise in years, when disaster struck Kursk on morning of August 12; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Spy Sub Said to Record Torpedo Blast Aboard Kursk

news.abstract: Opponents deal sharp blows to government of Pres Emile Lahoud and Prime Min Salim el-Hoss, in first round of parliamentary elections, apparently winning 35 of 63 seats in northern Lebanon (S)
news.title: Lebanese Opposition Registers Gains in Early Vote

news.abstract: Peru's Supreme Military Justice Commission, top military court, revokes life sentence of Lori Berenson, New Yorker imprisoned since 1996 following conviction for treason; grants her new trial in civilian courts, but she must remain in prison; lawyer says trial will begin soon; human rights officials and Berenson family members voice dissatisfaction; say first trial was unfair and that there is no confidence that second will be any better; case has long bedeviled relations between Peru and US and new trial may represent gesture by Peru to soothe relations, especially following country's tarnished presidential election; Pres Alberto K Fujimori, who was re-elected in May after campaign marked by irregularities and charges of voter fraud, declines comment; Berenson was charged with helping rebels of Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement plan aborted attack on Peru's Congress; photos (M)
news.title: New Yorker Imprisoned in Peru Gets New Trial in Treason Case

news.abstract: US State Department accuses Cuba today of causing widespread suffering by refusing to allow citizens to leave island even if they hold American visas; will bar Ricardo Alarcon, president of Cuban National Assembly, from attending meeting of international lawmakers at UN; denies move is in retaliation (S)
news.title: U.S. Says Cuba Causes Misery With Its Hard Line on Emigres

news.abstract: Mexican abortion rights groups celebrate victory against resurgent efforts by conservative politicians and church leaders seeking to chip away at already limited rights to abortion after Gov Ramon Martin Huerta sends backs to state Congress for further study bill passed by Legislature that would have made state only one in Mexico to extend ban on abortions to cases of rape; map; photo (M)
news.title: A Victory of Sorts for Abortion Rights in a Mexican State

news.abstract: EUROPE    RUSSIA: BRINGING UP SUB'S VICTIMS -- Russian and Norwegian divers will begin next month to remove the bodies of the 118 sailors who died in the sinking of the nuclear submarine Kursk. Deputy Prime Minister Ilya Klebanov said that the divers would cut six holes in the sub and that Russian divers would enter to retrieve the bodies. The sub will be raised next year, he said. Mr. Klebanov repeated that Russia believes that a collision with a foreign vessel caused the sinking, rejecting American reports that a torpedo exploded inside the sub.   Michael Wines (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: TIANJIN, China, Aug. 29 — The brick-walled Meite Packaging factory compound is nearly deserted now, its managers and machines hastily transferred in the last couple of days to a special development zone 30 miles outside this industrial city.
news.title: Factory Closings in China Arouse Workers to Fury

news.abstract: Pres Clinton meets with Pres Hosni Mubarak at Cairo airport to build Arab support for Middle East peace; he will continue effort in separate talks with Yasir Arafat and Prime Min Ehud Barak, both of whom will be in New York for UN meeting; Clinton makes refueling stop in Egypt on way home from Africa; he will leave for South America after brief return to Washington, continuing barrage of diplomacy in waning months of his term (M)
news.title: Clinton Meets Mubarak on Mideast Peace Effort

news.abstract: Increasingly confident and assertive Brazil is emerging as both US partner and rival in Latin America, steering own course on political and economic matters and stepping onto world stage as never before; photo (M)
news.title: Brazil Begins to Take Role on the World Stage

news.abstract: CARTAGENA, Colombia, Aug. 30 — President Clinton made a one-day visit today to this secure oasis of Colombia to lend backing to the nation's counternarcotics program.
news.title: Clinton Defends Colombia Outlay

news.abstract: Muslim rebel gunmen who kidnapped American Jeffrey Schilling in southern Philippines belong to particularly brutal faction that has tortured and killed hostages in past; United States State Department rules out talks with rebels; says US would welcome mediation by nations like Libya, which has longstanding contacts with rebels (M)
news.title: American's Philippine Captors Known for Torture

news.abstract: Pres Clinton, accompanied by Republican and Democratic lawmakers, visits Colombia to lend backing to nation's counternarcotics program; insists $1.3 billion in planned military aid is limited to drug fight, and will not involve United States in government's battle with rebels; says continuing aid will depend on government's breaking ties with paramilitary groups and adhering to strict human rights standards; rebels and protesters are active in advance of visit; Clinton tours port used by smugglers, with Pres Andres Pastrana acting as translator; photos; map (M)
news.title: CLINTON DEFENDS COLOMBIA OUTLAY

news.abstract: Mysterious subway derailment injures 24 passengers in Paris; car that tipped over skids to halt just three feet from train on opposite track (S)
news.title: Train Derails in Paris Subway, Injuring 24

news.abstract: Judge Albrecht Hennig finds three young neo-Nazis guilty of murder in beating death of an African immigrant, Alberto Adriano, in Dessau, Germany; finds Adriano was killed because of his skin color; cites need to put end to long series of such attacks in former East Germany; sentences Enrico Hilprecht to life imprisonment; sentences two juveniles, Christian Richter and Frank Miethbauer, to nine years in detention; Chancellor Gerhard Schroder calls for mass movement against racism and urges police and courts to crack down on extremists (M)
news.title: Three Neo-Nazis Are Convicted of Murder of African Immigrant

news.abstract: Israeli Supreme Court rules unauthorized early publication of Dr Elisha Qimron's reconstruction of important Dead Sea Scroll violated his copyright on work; rejects appeal by Biblical Archaelogy Society president, Hershel Shanks, of lower court ruling that he infringed Qimron's copyright by including reconstruction in his forward to collection of photographs of scroll fragments society published in 1991 to bring previously unpublished documents to light (M)
news.title: Israeli Court Upholds Scholar's Rights to Dead Sea Scrolls Work

news.abstract: Canada's Inuit in new northern territory of Nunavut are having rocky cultural transition from nomadic existence to modern, sedentary life of snowmobiles, heated homes and satellite television; map; one price is Canada's highest rate of violent crime, particularly violence against women; Levi Barnabas, former speaker of legislature, has been convicted of sexual assault, and education minister James Arvaluk is charged with assaulting woman (M)
news.title: Long Nomads, the Inuit Find a Settled Life Unsettling

news.abstract: MOGADISHU, Somalia, Aug. 30 — Somalia finally has a government, and its first president in nearly a decade arrived here today escorted by at least 120 pickup trucks carrying more than 1,000 militiamen armed with rifles, rocket launchers, even double-barreled antiaircraft guns.
news.title: Somalis Get Leader; Now They Need a Nation

news.abstract: Five veterans of 1989 Tiananmen Square democracy movement sue Chinese leader Li Peng in federal court in New York for human rights abuses stemming from his role in military crackdown; photo; Li, in New York for UN parliamentary conference, is served with court summons at Waldorf Towers (M)
news.title: Chinese Leader Sued in New York Over Deaths Stemming From Tiananmen Crackdown

news.abstract: Iranian legislators in New York for UN parliament meeting attend Metropolitan Museum reception and talk with Sen Arlen Specter, Repr Bob Ney, Repr Gary Ackerman and other Americans; issue of Iranian Jews convicted of espionage noted; Mouris Motamed, sole Jewish member of parliament, says Iranian Jewsare living as well as Muslim neighbors (M)
news.title: For Iran's Visiting Legislators, A Useful, Low-Key Exchange

news.abstract: Russian news agency identifies second US submarine in Barents Sea when submarine Kursk sank as the Toledo (S)
news.title: Russia Identifies U.S. Sub

news.title: Palestinians Convict and Sentence Terrorist
