news.abstract: Pres Clinton to lift many of trade and economic sanctions against Yugoslavia intended to speed fall of former Pres Slobodan Milosevic; will immediately end ban on American flights and oil embargo; will join with European Union in sweeping away variety of other sanctions over next few weeks, except for those aimed at barring Milosevic, his family and allies from sending assets abroad; will retain so-called 'outer wall' of sanctions' that bar World Bank and International Monetary Fund aid until United States discusses Milosevic's legal fate with Pres Vojislav Kostunica (M)
news.title: CLINTON TO SCRAP BELGRADE EMBARGO ON OIL AND TRAVEL

news.abstract: NEW YORK—  You're a young creative American fashion designer and you want to make your name. Should your first move be to catch a plane to Europe?
news.title: In America, New Names Face an Uphill Struggle

news.abstract: Dr Zhores Ivanovich Alferov, Nobel Prize winner in physics, scores Russia's failure to spend enough money on basic scientific research, speech to Russian Parliament, where he is member of Communist faction; wins prize for work conducted almost entirely when Russia was under Communist rule and scientists were cherished; photo (M)
news.title: Nobel Winner Laments Poverty of Russian Science

news.abstract: Interview with farmer Brynie Williams, who led fuel price protest at refinery near his Cilcain, Wales, home that rapidly spread across Britain; he expresses surprise that his efforts helped undermine popularity of Prime Min Tony Blair; map; photo (M)
news.title: Cilcain Journal; Farmer Who Sowed Wind That Rattled Britain

news.abstract: RAMALLAH, West Bank, Oct. 12 -- Youths stormed a Palestinian police station in the West Bank on Thursday and killed two Israeli soldiers who were in custody, police sources and witnesses said.
news.title: Palestinians Kill 2 Israeli Soldiers in Police Custody

news.abstract: RAMSTEIN AIR BASE, Germany, Oct. 13 — The remains of five American sailors, killed on Thursday during a terrorist attack on the U.S.S. Cole near Yemen, arrived here today aboard the first of several Air Force cargo planes that are evacuating the dead as well as the injured.
news.title: Five Bodies of U.S. Sailors Killed in Blast Flown to Germany

news.abstract: PARIS—  Fashion is having a do-it-yourself moment. It seems everywhere you look, there's a brand or designer encouraging the customer to get involved in the design process: to tear your T-shirt apart, create your own running shoes, customize your cocktail dress, all in the name of individuality.
news.title: Craze for Customization Tears Up the Rules

news.abstract: White House says Pres Clinton may travel to North Korea later this year, in what would be first visit by American president to that country; Clinton trip, still tentative, would follow visit by Secretary of State Madeleine K Albright (M)
news.title: Clinton Trip to North Korea Is Possible This Year

news.abstract: PARIS—  For three years, Europe has been buzzing about a massive secret payment allegedly made in 1992 by Elf Aquitaine, the French oil company, to the political slush fund of Chancellor Helmut Kohl of Germany. Elf officials have said that the payment was ordered by the late French president, Francois Mitterrand.
news.title: Imbroglio Over the Elf-Kohl Payoff:Was It a Hoax to Hide Kickbacks?

news.abstract: NEW YORK—  One in the morning: I am working late in the office, but fancy a spot of shopping. Bergdorf Goodman is closed, but Luxlook.com is open 24 hours a day, and I quickly find a flamboyant Versace tie with the designer's signature medallions for dollars 115. A few clicks, and the tie is ordered.
news.title: Little by Little, Designers Take To Web Sales

news.abstract: EUROPE    FRANCE: MAYOR OUSTED FROM PARTY  Mayor Jean Tiberi of Paris, who has been trying to hold onto his job despite being the focus of several investigations into corruption and vote fixing, has been dealt another blow. Already forced to give up leadership of the local branch of the Rally for the Republic, he has now been ousted from the party altogether. Mr. Tiberi, who insisted he would run for re-election, said he had been ''humiliated and mistreated'' by his Gaullist party.    Suzanne Daley (NYT)    RUSSIA: KURSK THEORIES  Experts investigating the sinking of the submarine Kursk no longer believe a collision with a foreign submarine is the likely cause of the tragedy. No evidence of a collision was found during a search of the seabed floor, Deputy Prime Minister Ilya Klebanov said. Mr. Klebanov said that a collision had not been ruled out, but that other theories -- that the sub struck a World War II mine, or that a torpedo exploded -- appeared equally valid.      Michael Wines (NYT)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Palestinians, faced with United States vow to veto any Security Council resolution on fighting between Israel and Palestinians, weigh seeking special United Nations General Assembly session to condemn Israel; Amb Richard C Holbrooke says Pres Clinton made decision to veto any further resolutions, interview; meets with several Arab diplomats to discuss what role UN should play (M)
news.title: Palestinians May Seek General Assembly Vote to Condemn Israel

news.abstract: NEW YORK—  Not so long ago in New York, the Gucci flagship reopened on Fifth Avenue with a grand celebration. The store had been renovated with great expense and folks were eager to see the revitalized building which also happened to be the Gucci empire's first home in the United States.
news.title: 'Ghetto Fabulous' Glitter Fades

news.abstract: Israel buries Vadim Norzich, who along with fellow reserve soldier, Yossi Avrahami, was stabbed, beaten and burned to death by mob at Palestinian police station, Ramallah, after getting lost in West Bank; Israelis and Palestinians are in state of shock over incident and Israeli retaliatory attack, which have greatly dimmed hopes for peace; Israel, which prides itself on allowing freedom of worship at Al Aksa Mosque, Jerusalem, bars Muslims younger than 45 from attending prayer; photos (M)
news.title: Israel in Shock as It Buries Mob's Victim

news.abstract: Bomb rocks Britain's Yemen Embassy, jarring memories of Britain's uncomfortable ties with its former colony and of terrorist underworld that seems to be at work there; British experts comment (M)
news.title: Bomb Jars Embassy, A Reminder Of Tense Tie

news.abstract: Retired Gen Anthony C Zinni, architect of plan to send United States Navy ships into port of Aden to improve ties with Yemen, holds he sought to keep Yemen from becoming 'rats' nest' of terrorist groups; says several planned ship visits were vetoed by Amb Barbara K Bodine, who worried about terrorist threat; notes he also sent American special forces to Yemen to train local military in counterterrorism (M)
news.title: Ex-Pentagon Planner Defends Sending U.S. Ships to Yemen

news.abstract: Analysis of view that Clinton administration, now scrambling for new Israeli-Palestinian summit to arrange simple truce, may have erred in rushing Camp David peace talks in quest for grand peace accord; even administration officials now see little chance of restoring peace effort during Clinton's presidency; photo (M)
news.title: Falling Short of Peace

news.abstract: SARAJEVO, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Oct. 14 — The Bosnian Muslim leader, Alija Izetbegovic, who led the resistance to the Serbs in the 1992-95 Bosnian war, stepped down today from the country's tripartite presidency, two years before his mandate was to expire.
news.title: Muslim Leader in Bosnia Retires

news.abstract: ADEN, Yemen -- The crew of the crippled USS Cole gathered on its listing deck Sunday to pay tribute to 17 shipmates killed in an apparent suicide bombing that also ripped into the U.S. Navy's strategic plans in the Middle East.
news.title: Specialists Scour U.S.S. Cole for Clues to Deadly Blast

news.abstract: Opposition joy over their sweep in June of over third of parliamentary seats in Zimbabwe has quickly dissolved into discontent as opposition legislators repeatedly find selves outnumbered and ignored; opposition is warning for first time that its supporters may turn to violence if Pres Robert Mugabe's government continues to block their efforts at change; map; photo (M)
news.title: Mugabe's Foes in Zimbabwe, Stymied, Talk of Violence

news.abstract: A showdown is shaping up within the dominant Protestant political party that could lead to the ouster of its longtime leader, David Trimble, and an end to the power-sharing government at the heart of Northern Ireland's peace accord.     ''This is more serious than it's ever been,'' Paul Bew, professor of Irish history at Queens University, said of the struggle to salvage the 1998 accord. ''Can the agreement be lost over the next few weeks? The answer sadly is yes, it's more likely to be lost than be saved.''
news.title: Protestant's Slipping Hold Imperils Ulster Peace Accord

news.abstract: The doctor at the central blood bank advised Nagwa Omar not to donate because she is breast-feeding her fourth child. But the 37-year-old university professor was adamant.     ''I insist,'' Dr. Omar said, as she rolled up her sleeve today, offering her right arm to the nurse who would draw her blood. ''If I could even go to Palestine to fight, I would.''
news.title: Anti-Israeli Anger Swells Flow of Aid

news.abstract: The Pentagon today suspended all naval refueling operations in Yemen until officials determine whether lax security in the port at Aden left the American destroyer Cole vulnerable to a presumed bombing attack that killed 17 sailors and wounded more than three dozen others.    The security at the port -- and with the private contractor that oversaw the refueling -- has become a focus of the widening investigation into what officials have called a suicide attack. Since the attack is believed to have involved a harbor boat helping the Cole moor at a refueling site in Aden's port, officials say they believe that those involved skillfully infiltrated the port's operations or the contractor itself.
news.title: U.S. Suspends All Refueling in Yemen for Security Inquiry

news.abstract: The last time a top Chinese leader came to Japan, he lectured at every stop over the nation's past war crimes, demanding an apology. The visit quickly degenerated into a fuming, finger-pointing session that damaged relations between the two countries, Asia's most powerful.    So there was a palpable sense of relief here this weekend when Prime Minister Zhu Rongji of China soft-pedaled the bitter question of Japan's conquest of his country in the 1930's as he made the rounds of official banquets and meetings with business groups and ordinary Japanese. He focused instead on economic and security issues whose resolution both countries say could bring them closer together.
news.title: China's Premier, on Japan Visit, Wears a Friendly Face

news.abstract: Setting an urgent goal of a truce between Israelis and Palestinians, President Clinton headed today for a Middle East summit meeting in Egypt that aides described as potentially the most difficult of his presidency.     Instead of playing the role of triumphant peacemaker that he had hoped for just a month ago, Mr. Clinton will arrive in Egypt trying to quell the violence that has left more than 100 people dead and that the White House fears could spill trouble across the region.
news.title: PRESIDENT HEADS TO MIDEAST TALKS HOPING FOR TRUCE

news.abstract: Stone-throwing clashes punctuated by exchanges of gunfire erupt across West Bank and Gaza Strip as thousands of Palestinians take to streets in message of defiance over peace summit in Sharm el Sheik; Palestinians report 13-year-old boy and policeman killed in resurging violence; dozens of protestors are wounded; Israeli Army reports two soldiers wounded by gunfire; armed members of Yasir Arafat's Fatah movement are visible in many of dfemonstrations after group's leadership urges Palestinians to keep up wave of violent protests; photo (M)
news.title: Clashes Continue as Palestinians Protest Summit Meeting

news.abstract: Pres Charles Taylor of Liberia suggests to UN Security Council peace mission that peacekeeping troops be allowed to move into rebel-held diamond-producing areas of Sierra Leone while the rebels return to negotiations that were shattered in May by their breach of peace accord; some council members remain skeptical; say proposal may be tactical ploy by Taylor, who has been close to rebel's United Revolutionary Front but has denied widespread allegations that he is prospering from diamonds and arms trade with them (M)
news.title: Liberian President Urges U.N. to Move Into Rebel-Held Areas in Sierra Leone

news.abstract: Federal Bureau of Investigation assigns its New York office to lead investigation into terrorist attack against US destroyer Cole in Yemen (S)
news.title: Case Goes to New York F.B.I. Office

news.abstract: FRANKFURT—  Europe's common currency slid back toward its record low Monday after Wim Duisenberg, president of the European Central Bank, appeared to cast doubt on the commitment of central banks to intervene anew in support of the euro.
news.title: Currency Nears Its Low As ECB Leader Seems Hesitant on Intervention : New Doubts On Support Push Euro Downward

news.abstract: SHARM EL-SHEIK, Egypt (AP) -- Israel and the Palestinians agreed Tuesday to end the street violence that has torn their region apart for more than two weeks and to get back on the path toward a permanent solution to their conflict.
news.title: Leaders in the Middle East Agree to Seek a Cease Fire

news.abstract: East Timor, destroyed by rampaging militias after its Aug vote for independence from Indonesia, is struggling to rebuild and forge national identity; United Nations, which saved nation from vandals, will continue to run it for year and help put in place basic structures of nationhood; process, after slow start, is well under way, with aid reaching people, job programs functioning and policies being made; local leaders have begun to squabble over political power; map; photo (M)
news.title: Emerging From Its Crisis, East Timor Rebuilds

news.abstract: Pres Clinton, after intensive summit meeting in Sharm el Sheik, Egypt, with Israeli Prime Min Ehud Barak and Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat, says they have agreed to work to stop violence in West Bank and Gaza and to try to bar it from escalating; warns of difficulties ahead; cease-fire accord calls for Israel to reopen Gaza airport, end border closings and withdraw its forces stationed at edge of Palestinian territories; calls for Palestinians to act to stop riots and gun battles, crack down on incitement against Israel and rearrest Islamic fundamentists freed from prison last week; some West Bank Palestinians complain Arafat, who left Egypt quickly to return to Gaza, was railroaded into accepting watered-down compromises; sporadic gun battles continue in West Bank and Gaza Strip as Palestinian militants reject call to end fighting; accord returns United States to its former role as broker, policeman and judge, role Barak sought to end when he took office; Egyptian Pres Hosni Mubarak admits accord will disappoint many; Palestinians are particularly disappointed that accord does not mandate international inquiry into recent violence; American-led fact-finding committee will instead work in consultation with United Nations Sec Gen Kofi Annan; photos (M)
news.title: 2 SIDES IN MIDEAST PROMISE TO WORK TO STOP VIOLENCE

news.abstract: Gov Luis Singson, who threatens to bring down Philippines government with charge that Pres Joseph Estrada accepted over $8 million in kickbacks from illegal gambling, sounds more like cheerful accomplice than angry avenger, interview; describes Estrada's gambling habits; ex-Pres Corazon C Aquino joins calls for Estrada's resignation; photos (M)
news.title: Manila Journal; This Whistle-Blower Could Topple a President

news.abstract: Pres Clinton played pivotal role at Israeli-Palestinian summit conference in devising mechanism to defuse deadly eruption of violence; his personality and ability to connect with Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat reportedly provided constant thread in talks; his back-to-back, separate sessions with Arafat and Israeli Prime Min Ehud Barak were key bridge between two men no longer able to meet face to face (M)
news.title: For Clinton, the Suspense Is Not Over

news.abstract: Concern over United States military aid to Colombia to fight drug traffickers and guerrillas who protect them overshadows formal agenda as Western Hemisphere defense ministers assemble, Manaus, Brazil, for meetings aimed at strengthening regional military and security cooperation; US Sec William Cohen and Colombian Sec Luis Fernando Ramirez Acuna are on hand to allay concerns; Cohen insists US will not become involved militarily; leaders of bordering nations fear effort will push coca cultivation, refugees and fighting onto their territories; Cohen warns any effort to ignore crisis or stay aloof from it is likely to backfire (M)
news.title: U.S. Aid to Colombia Worries Hemisphere's Defense Leaders

news.abstract: Analysis of treacherous problems that abound in Balkan region even after removal of Slobodan Milosevic in Serbia; Vojislav Kostunica, new Yugoslav president, has made conciliatory signals toward Croatia, which long battled Belgrade for its independence, and Montenegro, where secessionist currents are strong; Kostunica's past nationalism makes some neighbors skeptical, and his popularity in West makes other neighbors envious; his arrival has come so late in process of Yugoslav disintegration that it is far from clear that process can be arrested; American officials say Washington's twin priorities are consolidating Serbia's democratic transition and encouraging Kostunica to reassure Serbia's neighbors; photos (M)
news.title: Balkans After Milosevic: Still Perilous Waters

news.abstract: Bodies of six illegal immigrants, believed to have suffocated in truck, are found dumped on side of highway in southern Italy; it is grim reminder of perils of trying to immigrate to Europe; Italy is major port of entry to Europe for desperate would-be immigrants from Albania, Turkey, Iraq and Africa; photo (M)
news.title: Bodies of 6 Remind Italy of Migrants' Plight

news.abstract: EUROPE    ITALY: VOTING ABROAD -- A constitutional amendment was approved to allow Italians overseas to elect their own legislators, including candidates who live abroad. Twelve seats in the 630-seat lower house and six in the 315-seat Senate are to be allocated to representatives of Italians abroad, of whom there are about 4 million, with more than 300,000 in the United States and Canada. First, however, a law must be passed setting up candidates' procedural rules. Voting by absentee ballot is not allowed.    Alessandra Stanley (NYT)    FRANCE: CABINET RESIGNATION -- Martine Aubry, the cabinet minister who shepherded the introduction of the government's 35-hour workweek policy, has quit her cabinet post to run for mayor of Lille. The widely expected move is seen as a steppingstone to run for higher office in 2002. If Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, who is expected to run for president in 2002, were to win, Mrs. Aubry could well replace him as prime minister. Mr. Jospin named his justice minister, Elisabeth Guigou, to take over Mrs. Aubry's portfolio.    Suzanne Daley (NYT)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Israeli soldiers at army outpost at Kfar Darom in Gaza strip live under siege; they do not leave heavily guarded outpost unless packed inside armored jeeps; Palestinians frequently hurl stones and gasoline bombs into outpost, which protects small Israeli settlement; Israeli soldiers in Gaza complain that they have been ordered to restrain their fire and are often held back from putting down protests; Palestinians contend Israeli troops use excessive force to quell disturbances; photos; map (M)
news.title: Living Under Siege in Israeli Bunker

news.abstract: Yemeni and American teams investigating bombing of destroyer Cole center their inquiry on two safe houses and car found abandoned across harbor from where ship was attacked, killing 17 sailors; Aden's main newspaper reports that bomb-making equipment was found in at least one of houses, and that traces of explosives were found in car; chief of Saudi Arabia's intelligence services, Prince Turki bin al-Faisal, arrrives in Aden, apparently to help with investigation; Turki has monitored leftist and Islamic radical groups for last two decades; recovery of 8 more bodies leaves 4 of 17 dead sailors from USS Cole still unaccounted for; maps (M)
news.title: Ship Bomb Inquiry Focuses on Safe Houses and Deserted Car

news.abstract: Hong Kong customs agents discover 26 illegal Chinese migrants hidden in shipping container bound for Long Beach, Calif (M)
news.title: Illegal Migrants Bound for U.S. Found in Box at Hong Kong Port

news.abstract: PARIS—  Wim Duisenberg, the president of the European Central Bank, acknowledged Thursday that a loose-lipped blunder had undermined the euro, but he answered questions about whether he would resign with a terse "no."
news.title: Bank Chief Admits Euro Gaffe As Currency Hovers Near Low : Duisenberg Acts To Limit Damage

news.abstract: Defense Department announces that investigation into possible security lapses in connection with US warships visiting Yemen will be focus of independent investigation led by two former commanders, Adm Harold W Gehman and Gen William Crouch; Gen Anthony C Zinni, who retired as commander of US forces in the region in August, takes responsibility for having chosen Yemen as refueling stop, calling it safer and more strategically placed than other ports he had considered; photo (M)
news.title: Possible Lapses in Security At Yemen Port Investigated

news.abstract: US intelligence officials say they received reports in late May that militant Egyptian group Islamic Jihad was in final stages of preparing a terror attack against US targets, and that they passed on warning to all US posts and foreign governments in Middle East; Islamic Jihad, a faction of which is closely associated with Osama bin Laden, is under scrutiny as possible culprit in bombing of USS Cole in Yemen (M)
news.title: U.S. Says It Was Warned On Egyptian Islamic Group

news.abstract: Crown Prince Alexander, heir to Yugoslav throne, is making tour of Serbia to make it clear that he intends to help his country now that Slobodan Milosevic, whom he openly criticized, has left power; Alexander meets with Pres Kostunica, Serbian Orthodox Church leader Patriarch Pavle, and opposition groups; promises to return to live in his homeland, but brushes off questions of a return to monarchy; photo (Belgrade Journal) (M)
news.title: Belgrade Journal; From the Wings, a Prince Takes the Stage in Serbia

news.abstract: UN Sec Gen Kofi Annan asks General Assembly to make 'real difference' by helping bring end to fighting between Israel and Palestinians; Assembly later discusses and adopts resolution condemning Israel for 'excessive use of force' against Palestinians; urges both sides to return to negotiating table (M)
news.title: U.N. Assembly Adopts Resolution Condemning Israel for an 'Excessive Use of Force'

news.abstract: NEW YORK—  It is every museum director's dream.
news.title: Masterpieces From an Unparalleled Collection : A Treasure Trove From Japan

news.abstract: john worsley, 81, artist wh
news.title: John Worsley, 81, Artist Whose Wartime Creation Outfoxed the Nazis

news.abstract: NEW YORK—  Last September, a marked shift in the balance of commercial power between auction houses and the art trade could be observed in the international scene within a specific area that has never had it so good — Chinese art.
news.title: In Lean Times for Chinese Art, Dealers Triumph Over Auctioneers

news.abstract: Jose M Bustani, director of Organization for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons, makes plea in UN General Assembly to Israel, Egypt, Palestinians and others in Middle East to adhere to treaty banning use of such weapons as way to reduce tensions in region (M)
news.title: Mideast States Urged to Use An Arms Pact To Build Trust

news.abstract: New Yugoslav leader Vojislav Kostunica will visit Sarajevo, first such visit by Yugoslav president since Bosnia declared independence in 1992 (S)
news.title: New Leader Of Yugoslavia Due in Bosnia

news.abstract: Military violence remains part of daily routine of Grozny, Chechnya, months after Russia declared conclusion of the military phase of 'counterterrorist' operation; city is caught between a war that Russians cannot end and a peace that cannot take hold until a new Chechen leadership emerges to tame or supplant the warlords and 'bandits' whom Moscow is determined to crush; 150,000 people who have returned to live in Grozny complain that they live in repressive conditions of undeclared martial law, subjected to random searches, arrests, extortion and intimidation at more than 100 checkpoints; about 7,000 Russian troops are stationed in city, choking movement of people and basic foodstuffs; photo (M)
news.title: Chechnya Caught In Unending Limbo Of War and Peace

news.abstract: Hindu nationalist hard-liners continue pressing anti-Muslim policies, despite efforts by new party president Bangaru Laxman to distanceparty from chauvinist thinking; photos (M)
news.title: Hindu Hard-Liners Pressing To Keep Excluding Muslims

news.abstract: Elderly Ukrainian named Bogdan Tarnavsky claims in interview that he was anti-Nazi fighter who arrested Raoul Wallenberg, legendary Swedish diplomat who helped thousands of Jews escape Nazis before vanishing in Soviet hands in 1945; Tarnavsky, whose story differs from accepted account that Wallenberg drove off with Soviet guards, says he was stopped Wallenberg in Hungarian countryside and brought him back to his partisan unit; says intelligence operatives had Wallenberg whisked onto airplane to Lviv and then Moscow that night (S)
news.title: Ukrainian Says He Arrested Wallenberg

news.abstract: Officials representing nearly 150 governments lay groundwork at World Health Organization summit in Geneva, Switzerland, for new global treaty to control tobacco use and stamp out adolescent smoking; agency is pushing for strong international accord with goal of finalizing treaty by 2003 (M)
news.title: 150 Nations Move to Curb Tobacco Use

news.abstract: Prime Min Ehud Barak moves to heal rift with Israel's Arab citizens by announcing inquiry into deaths of 13 Israeli Arabs in current unrest and unveiling four-year development plan for Arab communities; move is met with skepticism among Israeli Arab leaders, who say inquiry, by committee of experts and retired judges instead of official state commission, will lack binding authority; say Barak's plan fails to address roots of inequality of Israel's one million Arab citizens (S)
news.title: Barak Seeks To Heal Rift With Inquiry And New Aid

news.abstract: American officials caution against conclusions that they are close to identifying group responsible or to retaliating militarily for bombing of destroyer Cole in Aden, Yemen, despite new clues suggesting that attack may have involved more than two men who died in blast; Yemeni officials working with US investigators report discovery of three more safe houses, bringing total discovered so far to five; Yemeni security sources say group of officials have been detained for allegedly allowing government offices to issue identity documents with assumed names used in conspiracy; photo (M)
news.title: Investigators Discouraging Speculation In Cole Attack

news.abstract: China's defense minister, Chi Haotian, arrives in North Korea hours before of US Sec of State Madeleine K Albright; is accompanied by senior military officials for five-day visit (S)
news.title: Chinese Official Beats Albright to North Korea

news.abstract: Chinese authorities are working to muffle Yu Jie, 25-year-old scholar whose writings, notably 1998 book Fire and Ice, have denounced country's official culture as vacuous; he has been denied job at state-controlled Chinese Modern Literature Institute, and appears to be effectively blackballed from paying position as scholar; faces expulsion to his small hometown in Sichuan Province, since he is ineligible for Beijing residency certificate unless he secures job; travails exemplify tighter constraints on many of country's livelier thinkers, who have not courted prison with direct activism, but whose careers are in jeopardy because they write so pointedly about China's shortcomings; photo (M)
news.title: Beijing Journal; Chinese Scholar Learns the Danger of Criticizing

news.abstract: Prime Min Jean Chretien calls for new elections in Canada, apparently counting on booming economy and popular new tax-cutting package to make him nation's first leader since World War II to win third consecutive mandate (M)
news.title: With Economy Booming, Canadian Leader Calls for Elections

news.abstract: Rafik Hariri, Lebanese billionaire, is named Lebanon's Prime Minister by Pres Emile Lahoud; he and supporters won landsilde victory in parliamentary elections in August (S)
news.title: Lebanese Businessman Once Again is Premier

news.abstract: Prime Minister Ehud Barak of Israel formally opens talks with Ariel Sharon, rightist opposition leader, on forming coalition government, but talks recess for day after first disagreements crop up; Barak, who has lost majority in Parliament, hopes move will enable him to escape vote by lawmakers for early elections and win broad public support for his policies in confrontation with Palestinians; Sharon is seeking veto on future concessions in any peace talks; would improve political chances against main rightist rival, former Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu, by entering cabinet; Barak argues current wave of Palestinian protests and rising tensions on Israel's border with Lebanon require broad-based government; Israeli peace advocates and Palestinian officials warn bringing Sharon into government will effectively bury any hope of peace, sending final signal that Barak has given up on negotiations; guns battles erupt between Israeli troops and Palestiniana erupt again on edge of Jerusalem, with no end in sight to violence; photo (M)
news.title: Barak and Sharon Open Talks on Forming a Coalition

news.abstract: Dr Sybil H Milton, leading scholar of Nazi Germany and the Holocaust and senior historian at United States Holocaust Memorial Museum in Washington, dies at age 59 (M)
news.title: Sybil Milton, 59, Scholar of Nazis and Holocaust

news.abstract: Former intelligence chief Vladimiro Montesinos returns to Peru, month after fleeing for asylum in Panama, plunging government of Pres Alberto K Fujimori into disarray; First Vice Pres Francisco Tudela, close ally of Mr. Fujimori, resigns; police clash with protestors in downtown Lima; opposition leaders, fearing coup attempt by Montesinos and military high command, pledge to take to streets; Washington warns any attempt to disrupt constitutional order will lead to Peru's isolation; reasons behind Montesinos's return remain unclear; arrived in Peru without official flight plan; landed at air force base in Pisco after officials at airport in Lima refused landing permission; government officials respond with surprise and confusion; Fujimori is silent; summons cabinet and military commanders; later visits military and intelligence installations around Lima; military analysts characterize Montesinos's landing as direct challenge to Fujimori's authority by military; photos (M)
news.title: Intelligence Chief Returns, Sending Peru Into Disarray

news.abstract: Results of October 22 Ivory Coast presidential election are delayed without explanation after early results show junta leader, Gen Robert Guei, trailing main opponent Laurent Gbagbo by 11 percentage points; Ivoirians express fears military government may be manipulating outcome (M)
news.title: With General Trailing, Ivory Coast Vote Tally Suddenly Dries Up

news.abstract: Scene in Pyongyan, North Korea, described; streets are spotlessly clean; women and children wear brightly hued clothes, many of them apparently sewn at home; reporters are denied access to countryside, where life reportedly is far harsher; photo (M)
news.title: Totalitarian Chic Reigns in Spotless Pyongyang

news.abstract: KUALA LUMPUR—  The challenge for any investor in a bear market is to escape the galloping herd: thousands of people reacting to the same bad news by hitting sell buttons within seconds of one another.
news.title: Bear Market Encourages Alternative Investments

news.abstract: Gen Robert Guei declares self winner of presidential election, dissolving electoral commission that showed him trailing opposition leader Laurent Gbagbo and halting vote counting; move stirs widespread protests in Abidjan and several other cities; Gbagbo urges supporters to stand up against Guei; security forces seem to remain loyal to Guei; center of Abidjan is quiet at night after government declares state of emergency and imposes nighttime curfew throughout nation; European Union, including France, and United States score Geui move; photo (M)
news.title: Ivory Coast Ruler Declares Himself Winner

news.abstract: Navy says destroyer Cole was at medium-level alert, which is routinely in force in Persian Gulf, when it was bombed in Aden, Yemen, despite general warning of possible terrorist attack on American warship; says there were only handful of sailors with rifles mounting watch on deck as ship entered harbor and no boats guarding waters around ship as flotilla of service boats moved in to aid with mooring and refueling; Yemeni security officials confirm finding house overlooking harbor from which conspirators apparently monitored Navy ships entering Aden and possibly directed attack (M)
news.title: No Special Alert for Cole Before Bombing

news.abstract: Pres Clinton calls Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat to urge him to bring rioting in West Bank and Gaza under control quickly; gets no assurances and no response to invitation for Arafat to visit United States soon to map way back to peace talks; plans to speak promptly with Israeli Prime Min Ehud Barak, with similar call for restraint and invitation to separate meeting; Russian Pres Vladimir V Putin also calls Arafat to urge restraint, after hearing from Barak; Palestinian rioting abates somewhat; Israeli military officials expect violence to continue for months; say nature of conflict is changing from street battles to low-level warfare; photo (M)
news.title: Clinton Urges Arafat to Calm Rioting in the West Bank

news.abstract: Pres Alberto K Fujimori orders military units to hunt down former intelligence chief, Vladimiro Montesinos, who has returned to Peru from monthlong exile in Panama; Fujimori suggests that elements of security forces probably helped Montesinos escape; Montesinos, who had been Fujimori's closest aide, is suspected of committing variety of crimes involving corruption and human rights violations; it is not clear exactly what Fujimori hopes to gain from search operation for Montesinos; photo (M)
news.title: Fujimori Orders Military To Arrest His Former Spy Chief

news.abstract: Congress approves $100 million aid package to Serbia, but makes it contingent on new Yugoslav government's cooperation in apprehending those indicted on charges of war crimes, including former Pres Slobodan Milosevic; Congressional experts acknowledge it may be difficult for Yugoslavia's new president, Vojislav Kostunica, and his deputies to comply with some of provisions (M)
news.title: $100 Million Voted for Serbia, but With War-Crimes Strings

news.abstract: Pres Clinton comes close to blaming Yasir Arafat, Palestinian leader, for failing to rein in violence, and he offers some of his warmest praise of Israeli Prime Min Barak; Clinton is trying to have both men visit Washington for separate consultations on restarting peace effort; White House officials say privately that any chance of resuming peace talks would end if Barak forms emergency government with Ariel Sharon, hard-line opposition leader; American officials fear that any seeming meddling in internal affairs of Israel would weaken Barak (M)
news.title: Clinton Almost Blames Arafat for Not Controlling Violence

news.abstract: American ambassador to United Nations, Richard Holbrooke, says Yugoslavia will soon apply to join UN, indicating clear change in policy under its new president, Vojislav Kostunica; Holbrooke is first prominent member of Clinton cabinet to meet with Kostunica; says Kostunica said he is working on releasing 800 Kosovo Albanians being held in Serb prisons, and suggests that law granting them amnesty is possibility (M)
news.title: Yugoslavia, Turning a Page, Is Expected to Rejoin United Nations

news.abstract: Reporter's Notebook vignettes from Secretary of State Madeleine K Albright's visit to North Korea to meet with Kim Jong Il (M)
news.title: Reporter's Notebook; Poverty, Paradox and a 'Dear Leader'

news.abstract: Palestinian suicide bomber, heading on his bicycle toward an Israeli Army outpost in Gaza Strip, succeeds only in killing himself but raises anxiety in Israel that violence is shifting into new phase; Islamic Jihad claims responsibility for attack by Nabil al-Arair; photos (M)
news.title: Suicide Attack in Gaza Strip Increases Tension in Mideast

news.abstract: Peruvian Pres Alberto K Fujimori is in apparent high-stakes chase after his spy chief Valdimiro Montesinos; Fujimore spends much of day in police helicopter directing manhunt against former aide, who is said to be at large in suburbs of Lima; all members of armed forces who are not involved in operation have been ordered to stay in their barracks, suggesting that Fujimori does not have full confidence in his army; search leads many people to wonder what is really going on, and some observers suspect search is really coordinated farce, saying Fujimoro's current relationship with Montesinos is unclear (M)
news.title: Playing Cat and Mouse, With Copters, in Peru

news.abstract: Residents of Ivory Coast who came together to topple military dictator now turn against one another in series of deadly clashes; violence between supporters of two of main political parties is sparked by religious and ethnic difference and leaders' ambitions; it begins in capital city Abidjan and spreads to smaller cities; winner of disputed election, Laurent Gbagbo, is sworn in as president, with backing of security forces; he rebuffs calls for new election from country's two major parities, United Nations, United States and Organization for African Unity; Alassane D Ouattara, former prime minister who was barred from running in election, takes refuge in German ambassador's residence after security forces surround his house and fire tear gas and ammunition; Ouattara claims attack was led by supporters of Gbagbo and backed by paramilitary gendarmes; photo (M)
news.title: Dictator Gone, Violence Erupts In Ivory Coast

news.abstract: LONDON—  An official investigation of Britain's "mad cow" crisis criticized government officials Thursday for misleading the public with a "campaign of reassurance," saying they played down potential risks to human health for years in order to prevent consumer panic and protect the country's beef industry.
news.title: Report Calls Officials to Task For Having Misled the Public : U.K. Understated 'Mad Cow' Threat

news.abstract: Militant tone of unalloyed hostility toward Israel and deep distrust of US policy continues in state-controlled media of Arab countries, mirroring flood of public sympathy and political activity in support of Palestinians; reminders of the conflict are everywhere, stirring sense of pan-Arab solidarity, and impact on regional politics could be substantial; attitudes toward United States are also hardening, and there is talk of boycotting US products (M)
news.title: Anti-U.S. Fever: Arab Bitterness and Boycott Talk

news.abstract: THE AMERICAS    ARGENTINA: SEEKS TO EXTRADITE PINOCHET  A judge asked Chile's Supreme Court to extradite the former dictator Augusto Pinochet for the killing of a former Chilean army chief, Carlos Prats, and his wife in Buenos Aires in 1974. General Pinochet, 84, is already fighting a possible trial in Chile for rights abuses during his 17-year rule. He returned home this year after 503 days under arrest in Britain. General Prats, who opposed General Pinochet's coup against President Salvador Allende in 1973, was killed by a car bomb.    (Reuters)

news.abstract: Doctors say that small towns in Henan Province are experiencing AIDS epidemic; Chinese officials deny there is AIDS in Henan; prohibit news media and government health workers from discussing issue and block outside researchers from studying it; covert studies suggest that Henan has some of highest localized rates of HIV infection in world; doctors say that poor farmers have illegally sold their blood to people whose unsterile collection methods have left many infected with HIV virus; map; photo (M)
news.title: In Rural China, a Steep Price Of Poverty: Dying of AIDS

news.abstract: Yemen reportedly is barring Federal Bureau of Investigation agents probing bombing of destroyer Cole from questioning suspects or witnesses, attending interviews with them or moving at will around Aden to follow clues, raising fears that evidence-gathering may be delayed or suppressed; Pres Clinton, State Sec Madeleine K Albright and FBI Dir Louis J Freeh have appealed for broader cooperation; FBI has moved its remaining 40 to 50 agents in Aden to Navy ships at sea outside city; some 100 others have returned home; photo (M)
news.title: Yemen Restricting F.B.I. Access to Suspects in Cole Bombing

news.abstract: RICHMOND, Texas -- A construction trench collapsed Saturday, killing three workers who were buried in 14 feet of dirt, authorities said.
news.title: 3 Killed in Trench Collapse

news.abstract: Colombia's villages are swept by campaign festivities in advance of nationwide municipal elections; Marxist guerrillas have been active for months in perhaps half of villages, quietly manipulating electoral process by giving their tacit approval to some candidates, forcing some to withdraw and assassinating few others; effort compromises nation's fragile democracy and strengthens position of Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia, nation's largest rebel movement; paramilitary gunmen have struck back, killing candidates believed to be rebel sympathizers; map; photo (M)
news.title: Behind Colombia's Election Hoopla, Rebels Wield Power

news.title: Persecution Charged in Ex-Soviet Republic

news.abstract: Israeli Prime Min Ehud Barak fails to forge emergency unity government with right wing; is unlikely to face immediate dismissal when Parliament reconvenes on October 30 after three-month recess; ultra-Orthodox Shas Party, which pulled out of government before Camp David peace talks in July, says it will grant Barak temporary 'safety net' while violence continues to rage between Israeli troops and Palestinians; three more Palestinians die in confrontations in West Bank; Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat says people will remain steadfast in struggle (M)
news.title: Barak Gets a Breather as He Tries to Form a Unity Government

news.abstract: American investigators still lack concrete evidence in bombing of destroyer USS Cole in Aden harbor in Yemen, despite trail of clues suggesting ship was bombed by Islamic militants, possibly associated with Osama bin Laden; say they are being slowed by Yemeni officials' refusal to allow questioning of scores of people detained so far; Clinton administration seems content to give investigators time to build stronger case before retailating, which could defer potentially divisive question of military response until after November 7 election (M)
news.title: Investigation of Attack on U.S. Destroyer Moving Slowly

news.abstract: Campaigning for Italy's 2001 parliamentary elections, which will determine whether country stays center-left or veers to center-right, is fixated on looks; Silvio Berlusconi, media tycoon and leader of center-right Sforza Italia, is perennially tanned with glossy good looks and Continental charm; Francesco Rutelli, 46-year-old Mayor of Rome, evinces dash of Paul Newman glamour; is hailed as having face that would not look out of place among busts of Roman emperors in Capitoline museums; each candidate claims to be face of new Italy, modern democracy shaking itself loose from lingering economic rigidity, red tape and corruption to meet challenges of global economy; photos (M)
news.title: Italy's New Politics: The Beauty Contest

news.abstract: Relations between the United States and Indonesia have deteriorated rapidly after a series of high-profile disputes between the American ambassador here and Indonesian officials and lawmakers, who have accused the United States of meddling.     Apparently as a result, protests and threats against American citizens, companies and facilities are on the rise in this country, which has the world's fourth-largest population and the largest Muslim population. Fearing what it called a ''credible threat of attack,'' the United States Embassy in Jakarta has closed its doors to the public for the foreseeable future.
news.title: U.S. Braces for Trouble in Indonesia as Relations Rupture

news.abstract: Venezuela's Pres Hugo Chavez and visiting Cuban Pres Fidel Castro hold four-hour gabfest on Chavez's weekly radio program in Caracas; take turns criticizing world order dominated by US, answer phone calls and even sing song together; photo (M)
news.title: Venezuelan Leader Finds a Teammate in Castro

news.abstract: Family doctors in Netherlands stage protest in the Hague, charging they are overworked and underpaid; charge Health Ministry with ignoring urgent pleas to reduce 70-hour weeks and for more subsidies to hire extra staff members because demands on primary care physicians are expanding year after year (S)
news.title: Family Doctors In Netherlands Stage a Protest

news.abstract: LEGHORN, Italy -- An Italian military police helicopter crashed off a Tuscan island overnight, killing at least six officers. The search was resuming Tuesday morning for the other two people aboard.
news.title: 6 Dead After Italian Military Helicopter Crashes

news.abstract: Sasabe, Mexico, is one of newest and fastest growing gateways to US for illegal Mexican immigrants as border enforcement is stepped up, particularly in cities; desert region on Arizona border is one of most inhospitable in North Americ, known for fierce winter storms and soaring temperatures; Immigration and Naturalization Service reports 369 immigrants have died trying to cross border since October 1999 and that 100 of deaths occurred along Arizona border--up from 19 deaths in 1998; map; photo (M)
news.title: The Desperate Risk Death in a Desert

news.abstract: Neighbors recall two Arab strangers suspected in bombing of US destroyer Cole in port of Aden, Yemen, seemed out of place but were never incongruous, after renting apartment on hillside overlooking port on June 9; neighbors cite their their thick accents, Islamic-style dress, seeming obsession with privacy, frugality with food they bought in local market and curious comings and goings in dead of night; say men described themselves as fish merchants, but recall they were never seen in local market; say neither went to prayers in new, whitewashed mosque that is pride of neighborhood; eyewitness descriptions of men who boarded boat matches exactly appearance, accents and clothing of those who lived in rented apartment; neighbors are convinced men and suicide bombers are same people; ramming of destroyer on October 12 during refueling stop killed 17 soldiers and wounded 39 others; map; photos (M)
news.title: Ship Attack Suspects Seemed Out of Place

news.abstract: US Navy ships are ordered to avoid Suez Canal; order comes in wake of bombing of destroyer Cole during refueling stop in Aden, Yemen, on October 12 in which 17 soldiers died (S)
news.title: Navy Ships Avoiding Suez Canal Since Destroyer Bombing

news.title: Grieving Relatives Seek Kin Among Taiwan Crash Victims

news.abstract: Mexican police continue to evict over 200 retirees, most of them Americans, from their homes in Baja Beach & Tennis Club, Ensenada, Baja California; Mexico's Supreme Court, which ruled in 1996 that land leased to resident was illegally seized by government in 1970's, has newly ordered government to carry out its original finding; many residents seek to negotiate leases with new owners of land (M)
news.title: Americans Find Their Beachfront Dreams Washed Out in Mexico

news.title: Israel Agrees With Palestinians to Halt Violence

news.abstract: Flora Brovina, prominent doctor, poet and activist for Kosovo Albanians, is freed from Serbian prison by special pardon from new Yugoslav president, Vojislav Kostunica, and crosses into Kosovo, her home province; she had been arrested outside her Pristina apartment by Serbian police on Apr 20, 1999, during NATO bombing campaign; she was sentenced to 12 years in Serbian court on charges of conspiring to commit terrorism and aiding rebel force, Kosovo Liberation Army; her release indicates that Pres Kostunica regards issue of detainees who had been transferred from Kosovo when Serbian forces withdrew as one of human rights (M)
news.title: Kosovo Albanians Cheer the Return of a Doctor Freed in Serbia

news.abstract: Federal jury will decide whether two former military commanders in El Salvador will be held accountable for kidnappings, rapes and murders of four American churchwomen there 20 years ago; women's relatives are seeking $25 million a victim in damages (M)
news.title: Suit in Nuns' 1980 Deaths in El Salvador Goes to Florida Jury

news.abstract: Alasdair Denvil letter, commenting on Oct 31 article on Vice Pres Al Gore's populist appeals in Wisconsin, says it is pity he lacks forum in which to answer Ralph Nader's criticisms and win back some of support that has deserted him
news.title: Ralph Nader's High-Wire Politics

news.abstract: About 120,000 laborers from West Bank and Gaza Strip are unable to reach their jobs in Israel since borders were shut by Israelis when Palestinian unrest erupted five weeks ago; their lost wages are estimated at nearly $3.5 million a day; border closings and isolation of Palestinian towns behind Israeli Army checkpoints are preventing imports of raw materials and goods, blocking exports and disrupting marketing; as new uprising takes mounting economic toll, Palestinians insist they are prepared to pay price as long as necessary to end Israeli occupation and win independence (M)
news.title: West Bank Tightens Its Belt, Defiantly

news.abstract: Recent violence has sidetracked thriving tourist industry in Palestinian-controlled West Bank city of Jericho; it is surrounded by Israeli tanks and military roadblocks and littered by burnt tires and spent bullets, result of nightly rituals of sniping at Israeli soldiers and retaliation by Israeli tanks; photo (M)
news.title: Israeli Missiles Hit Jericho, Where Gamblers Used to Hit Jackpots

news.abstract: Car bomb kills two Israelis after it explodes near open-air market in Jerusalem, threatening early morning truce agreement between Israel and Palestinians; bombers flee on foot; site of bomb has been favorite target of Islamic groups during previous waves of terrorism; despite cease-fire pact, Palestinian gunmen open fire once more on Gilo, southeastern Jerusalem neighborhood, and Israeli troops return machine-gun fire toward shooting in Palestinian town of Beit Jala; 17-year-old Palestinian is shot dead in clash in village of Hizme near Jerusalem; Prime Min Ehud Barak of Israel calls Yasir Arafat, Palestinian leader, to express consolences; death toll from monthlong conflict rises to 168; photos; map (M)
news.title: Car Bomb Kills 2 Israelis and Threatens Truce Effort

news.abstract: EUROPE    RUSSIA: PUTIN OPENS DOOR TO PAST -- President Vladimir V. Putin has agreed to permit a search of Soviet archives for data on the millions who died or were jailed under Stalin's rule, a leader in the effort to rehabilitate Stalin's victims said. Aleksandr Yakovlev, a former adviser to Mikhail S. Gorbachev, said the president ''takes to heart this tragic period in our history,'' and had ordered military and intelligence agencies to open their archives to help clear the names of unfairly persecuted citizens.      Michael Wines (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: New concern about mad cow disease is set off in France by arrest of father and son who tried to sell diseased cow for slaughter and succeeded in getting hundreds of pounds of suspect meat onto supermarket shelves; government, prompted by insistent calls for stricter protective measures, says it will increase testing of cattle headed for slaughterhouses, including random testing of even healthy-looking cows; so far this year, French officials habe detected 78 cases, more than twice number detected in 1999 (M)
news.title: Arrests Spur French Fears Over Spread Of Mad Cow

news.abstract: Palestinians in Ramallah in West Bank feel grim satisfaction viewing television images of dead and wounded Israelis in Jerusalem car bombing, after so much bloodshed on Palestinian side in recent weeks; they oppose cease-fire and doubt that agreement between Shimon Peres and Yasir Arafat will not work; Palestinians throughout West Bank and Gaza bitterly denounce any idea of easing up their monthlong intifada (M)
news.title: On the Streets, Palestinians Vow to Keep Fight Going

news.abstract: MANILA, Nov. 3 — The crisis surrounding Philippine President Joseph Estrada deepened on Friday as a number of key government allies deserted the embattled leader, leaving him almost certain to be impeached over a gambling pay-offs scandal.
news.title: Estrada Crisis Deepens but He Vows to Fight

news.abstract: MIDDLE EAST    IRAN: PROTEST CROWDS DIMINISH  With traditional chants of ''Death to America!'' Iranians marked the anniversary of the United States Embassy seizure in 1979, but in much smaller numbers than in previous years. The small size of the crowd -- about 6,000 instead of the tens of the thousands seen in the mid-1990's -- was seen as proof of a growing desire among Iranians for better ties with the outside world.    (AP)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Physics of Higgs boson is so hard to explain that scientists once competed in contest to see if anyone could do it in less than one page; excerpts from one entrant's explanation (S)
news.title: So Boson Arrives At the Party . . .

news.abstract: Vast majority of members of Congress hold passports and use them, traveling overseas at least twice a year on trips that are largely business with some pleasure; nearly one-third of them have studied or worked abroad, and one in five claims to speak foreign language will enough to conduct business beyond America's borders; these statistics seem to contradict popular notion that members of Congress are homebound and uninterested in world; but statistics cannot serve as indicator of how any member of Congress is likely to vote on issues of foreign or national security (M)
news.title: Insular Congress Appears to Be Myth

news.abstract: South Africa's museums and universities will open their archives to relatives of 2,000 members of Khoisan people whose dead bodies were taken, over their families' protests, for examination by scientists in early 1900's; for museums, it is act of penance, frank condemnation of their feverish race to collect and classify bones of so-called 'primitive races' including Khoisans, known then as Bushmen and Hottentots; museum curators will also arrange for proper burials of bones, in hope of restoring dignity taken from people who were denigrated in life and in death; photo (M)
news.title: Cape Town Journal; Bones in Museum Cases May Get Decent Burials

news.abstract: Physicians for Human Rights, based in Boston, reports on its independent investigation into past month's violence in Israel; report echoes many Palestinian accusations against Israel, but Palestinian officials criticize study for finding that one well-publicized Palestinian death was result of traffic accident, rather than torture-death at hands of Israeli settlers and soldiers; report also includes detailed analysis of 31 deaths over 24 days in Gaza; 38 percent of deaths are of children younger than 18; group says half the fatal gunshots in Gaza cases it studied were to the head (M)
news.title: Doctors Back Many Palestinian Accusations, but Not All

news.abstract: Friedrich Merz, leading conservative, ignites political storm in Germany by saying that millions of foreigners in country must adopt German 'Leitkultur,' or guiding culture; critics like Foreign Min Joschka Fischer see such ideas as inflammatory departure from Germany's postwar embrace of muted identity within unifying Europe (M)
news.title: Call for 'Guiding Culture' Rekindles Political Debate in Germany

news.abstract: FBI agents investigating terrorist bombing of US destroyer Cole in port of Aden, Yemen, visit country's remote, and fundamentalist, Wadi Doan region in search for clues to character of Osama bin Laden, Saudi dissident who is prime suspect in bombing which killed 17 American sailors; father who was born in area migrated to Saudi Arabia in 1950's; bin Laden, who never lived in Wadi Doan, is 17th of more than 50 children born to his father; maps; photos (M)
news.title: Remote Yemen May Be Key to Terrorist's Past and Future

news.abstract: Israel marks fifth anniversary of assassination of Prime Min Yitzhak Rabin even as new crisis with Palestinians threatens his legacy as peacemaker; his daughter Dalia Rabin-Pelosoff, Oslo negotiator Uri Savir and those at memorial rally mourn in heavy mood, while at Labor Party memorial service the famous photo of Rabin's handshake with Yasir Arafat is absent from elegiac slide show; photos; Rabin's widow is hospitalized, gravely ill with lung cancer (M)
news.title: In Marking Slaying Of Rabin in 1995, Israel Seeks Lessons

news.abstract: Violence in Mideast leads Switzerland to hastily postpone diplomatic conference to pave way for Israel's Magen David Adom to join Red Cross; 189 nations that have signed Geneva Conventions need to approve neutral emblem alongside red cross and red crescent; traditional cross was not intended as religious symbol but as honor to Swiss who helped found organization in mid-1800's (S)
news.title: Mideast Unrest Stalls Israel's Role in Red Cross

news.abstract: Runaway youths, male and female, in shelters and public places in Iran are embarrassing testimony to failure of 21-year-old Islamic revolution to produce new generation of obedient, chaste 'warriors for Islam'; government ignored problem for years but is forced into action as more and more children take to streets, and fall prey to prostitution, crime and heroin addiction; city of Tehran now finances shelter for girls fleeing abusive homes; photo (M)
news.title: Runaway Youths a Thorn in Iran's Chaste Side

news.abstract: Fifty thousand surplus assault rifles that were sold by Jordan to Peruvian military in 1998 with CIA's approval end up with Colombian guerrillas in deal involving ousted Peruvian intelligence chief, Vladimiro Montesinos, crucial CIA ally in region; disclosure raises new questions about Montesinos's ties to agency and has deepened rift in Clinton administration over how closely it should be dealing with official linked to human rights abuses and other crimes; Montesions has been implicated in arms deal by two of men who organized it since his ouster in September; Peruvian government is moving to prosecute him in connection with large personal fortune he apparently hid in Swiss banks; photo (M)
news.title: C.I.A. Links Cited on Peru Arms Deal That Backfired

news.abstract: White House says Prime Min Ehud Barak and Yasir Arafat will meet separately with Pres Clinton in coming days; expectations of success are low since Clinton, who is lame-duck president, may be unable to achieve much beyond trying to exercise calming influence (M)
news.title: Hopes Are Low for Clinton's Talks With Barak and Arafat

news.abstract: Prime Min Ehud Barak and Yasir Arafat are greatly weakened leaders who will try to revive moribund Israeli-Palestinian peace negotiations in coming series of meetings in Washington; both face sharp criticism from their own people; Palestinians are angry at Israel for still expanding settlements in West Bank and Gaza and controlling roads into Palestinian areas seven years after Oslo peace accord on which peace effort has been built; Israelis are disillusioned over recent outbreak of violence, called new intifada by Palestinians; many Israelis say violence proves they cannot live in peace with Palestinians; clashes between Palestinian protestors and Israeli troops continue; two Palestinians are shot and killed in Gaza; photo; map (M)
news.title: Dubious Mandates at Home For Players in Mideast Talks

news.abstract: WASHINGTON—  Governor George W. Bush on Sunday appeared to have survived, with only minor political scratches, the revelation last week of a past drunken driving conviction as he and Vice President Al Gore kept up vigorous last-minute efforts to energize party bases and assure crucial voter turnouts.
news.title: Just Scratched by 1976 Arrest, Bush Keeps Lead in Polls

news.abstract: Tensions are rising between Christians and Moslems in Ivory Coast, once envy of other African countries because of its religious and ethnic tolerance (M)
news.title: 2 Religions Clashing in Ivory Coast

news.abstract: Clashes between Palestinian protesters and Israeli forces continue in West Bank; two Palestinian youths are shot dead by troops; death toll since start of unrest on September 28 rises to 176; Israeli officials express concern over pattern of nightly gunfire from Palestinian areas toward Israeli settlements and other areas; say violence persists, despite truce agreement reached between Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat and Israeli elder statesman Shimon Peres; photo (M)
news.title: New Clashes In West Bank And Gaza Put Israel on Edge

news.abstract: Reestablishment of rail links between North and South Korea, cut off since start of Korean War 50 years ago, raises hopes among South Koreans who are stuck at end of peninsula at edge of Asian continent and feel almost as cut off from world geographically as Communist North has been isolated economically and politically; reconnection is intended to do away forever with notion of 'hermit kingdom' as Korea has been long known; maps; photos (M)
news.title: Kumchon Journal; Railroad Trip to Europe? Koreans Savor the Idea

news.abstract: MANILA—  The impeachment complaint against President Joseph Estrada cleared the House Justice Committee in less than four hours Monday, and the stock market and Philippine currency soared in anticipation that he would resign or be removed.
news.title: Philippine House Panel Clears Impeachment of Estrada

news.abstract: Interview with Catherine Phiri, honored by UN for her anti-AIDS campaign in Malawi; she is founder of support group for people not only suffering from disease in country with one of highest infection rates in Africa, but also from neglect of society unschooled about malady; was diagnosed HIV-positive in 1990 after husband died from disease; photo (M)
news.title: Nurse in Malawi Wages War on AIDS and Apathy

news.abstract: SINGAPORE—  For years pilots flying into Taiwan had complained about lighting and markings on the airstrip at Chaing Kai Shek Airport where a Singapore Airways jumbo jet crashed a week ago, killing or injuring all but 40 of the 179 people on board, according to two pilots familiar with the airport.
news.title: Markings Failed to Distinguish Fatal Runway : Pilots Have Long Faulted Taipei Airport's Hazard

news.abstract: Iraq asks for meeting with UN Sec Gen Kofi Annan in move to break impasse over arms inspections; Annansays he will meet with representatives of Iraqi government in summit-level meeting of Islamic nations in Qatar on November 11 (M)
news.title: Iraq Seeks Talks With U.N. Chief on Arms-Inspection Impasse

news.abstract: Dennis B Ross, leading American peace negotiator in Middle East for more than decade, will leave post in January 2001, at end of Clinton administration; has served under administrations of Presidents Reagan, Bush and Clinton; cites stress on family from 12 years of travel as main reason for decision (M)
news.title: Chief U.S. Mediator in Mideast Plans to Leave in January

news.abstract: Criticism has grown year after Abdurrahman Wahid assumed power as Indonesia's president and pledged to end flagrant cronyism rampant under predecessor Pres Suharto; many say he has done little to change Indonesia's notoriously corrupt bureaucracy and legal system; public opinion poll finds 65 percent of those surveyed favor special legislative session to impeach him; critics are troubled that Wahid himself is now embroiled in embarrassing string of scandals that have damaged his credibility and hurt efforts to establish rule of law in young democracy; scandal involving his masseur, who is accused of bilking government of $4 million, discussed; photo (M)
news.title: Scandals Sully Indonesian Leader's Reform Image

news.abstract: Doctors in Manchester, England, separate 3-month-old twin girls in court-approved operation that knowingly sacrificed life of one to save other; surviving twin is in critical but stable condition following 20-hour operation; both were born with fused spines, joined at abdomen with arms and legs at right angles to their upper bodies (M)
news.title: Siamese Twin Is Separated; 'Sadly Dies' To Save Sister

news.abstract: Canadian writer Margarat Atwood wins 2000 Booker Prize, Britain's most prestigious literary award for fiction, for book The Blind Assassin; has been nominated three times before (M)
news.title: Margaret Atwood Is the Winner of Britain's Top Fiction Award

news.abstract: Russia's deputy prime minister, Ilya Klebanov, says divers investigating cause of explosion that sank Russian submarine Kursk found 'serious visual evidence' pointing to collision between Kursk and another object; says investigative panel has still not ruled out other possible causes of disaster, which killed 118 sailors; senior Russian officials have said they believe Kursk collided with foreign submarine that was monitoring Russian naval exercises; American military officials have flatly denied that any of their boats came in contact with Kursk (M)
news.title: Russian Official Says Evidence Points to Collision With the Sub

news.abstract: Events on Election Day in Florida (local time):
news.title: A Night to Remember:Indecision 2000

news.abstract: Critics of Pres Hugo Chavez of Venezuela point to his new school system as most troubling sign of creeping militarization of government; new system offers three free meals and after-school care, under soldiers' supervision; in most cases, classes are still taught by civilians, and military is supervising schools; Constitution drawn up to Chavez's specifications last year makes teaching of 'Bolivarian ideology' obligatory in all schools; leading Bolivar scholars, educators and even retired generals are alarmed that it is Chavez and his government who define what is Bolivarian and what is not; photo (M)
news.title: Caracas Journal; Salutes, Some Skeptical, as Schools Go 'Bolivarian'

news.abstract: Putumayo, province of coca-growing jungle, is crucial battleground in Colombia's civil conflict; rebels have imposed travel ban there, strangling local economy and underscoring challenge that Pres Andres Pastrana faces as he works with American government in imposing $7.5 billion plan to curtail lucrative coca trade and weaken rebels; both rebels and paramilitaries appear firmly established and prepared to fight for months on end; photos; map (M)
news.title: Coca Conflict in Colombia Snares the Innocent

news.abstract: Chinese courts convict 84 people of corruption, smuggling and other charges, handing out 11 death sentences to government officials; these are first punishments meted out in connection with embarrassing multi-billion-dollar smuggling scandal in port city of Xiamen in Fujian Province; many of convicted officials are from Xiamen customs service; customs officials have recently been investigated in number of cities, including Tianjin and Shantou; Chinese experts say corruption may be equally widespread in other government bureaucracies (M)
news.title: China Sentences 11 Officials to Death in Smuggling Scandal

news.abstract: Israeli helicopter gunships fire missiles at vehicle carrying Palestinian paramilitary commander on West Bank, killing him and two women who happened to be nearby; this is Israel's first targeted, planned slaying of Palestinian militia leader since six-week-old violent confrontation on West Bank and Gaza began; Israeli Army spokesman says militia leader, Hussein Obaiyat, was suspected of being mastermind behind many shooting attacks on Israeli soldiers and civilians that emanated from Bethlehem area; says army received permission for killing from 'highest political level'; Fatah paramilitary field officer confirms that Obaiyat was commander of southern Bethlehem area; says Fatah will take 'escalatory measures and revenge' for his killing; paramilitary units of Fatah operate independently; Yasir Arafat's police and security services are supposed to disarm and restrain them under terms of many agreements with Israel; photos; map (M)
news.title: Israelis Track Down and Kill a Fatah Commander

news.abstract: Kremlin says it plans to shrink its three-million-strong armed forces by 600,000 people, led by deep cuts in main Defense Ministry forces; Pres Vladimor V Putin says he wants to rein in unwieldy and extravagant military machine; move may also presage deeper reshuffling of defense apparatus and more direct control of military by Putin (M)
news.title: Putin Cuts Forces by 600,000, Promising Military Overhaul

news.abstract: Correction of Nov 9 article on Brown University's selection of Ruth J Simmons as its president, regarding day of its decision and Simmons's age, which is 55
news.title: Corrections

news.abstract: Chidambaram Subramaniam, political architect of the 'green revolution' in India, which made nation self-sufficient in wheat production, dies at 90; photo (M)
news.title: Chidambaram Subramaniam, India's 'Green' Rebel, 90, Dies

news.abstract: Since mid-October, Britain has been pummeled by rain, whipped by winds and buffeted by storms that have caused untold millions of dollars in damage, wreaked havoc with roads and trains, and left thousands of people without habitable homes; at least 12 people have been killed, mostly from trees falling on their cars as they tried to drive through wind and rain; in Yalding, Kent, flooding has been so severe that firefighters swim down streets, cars float away, houses have been destroyed and residents have been evacuated by boat; photos; map (M)
news.title: Yalding Journal; England Is Half-Drowned and Wholly Fed Up

news.abstract: Argentina Pres Fernando de la Rua says multinational credit agencies and international banks will back effort to revive stagnant economy, televised speech; outlines steps to help restore confidence; reiterates his support for Economy Min Jose Luis Machinea; analysts say plan could involve added credit line from International Monetary Fund and other lenders (M)/
news.title: Argentina Says Lenders Pledge to Help Lift Economy

news.abstract: General elections are set for Bosnia; Western officials who run nation are closely watching vote; Wolfgang Petritsch, who heads international administration, has urged people to reject nationalist parties (M)
news.title: Bosnia Holds Broad Elections Today, and Western Officials Fret

news.abstract: an endangere
news.title: An Endangered Species: Liberal in Canada's West

news.abstract: Prosecution tries to establish alibi for Mohamed Abo Talb, Palestinian defense plans to blame for bombing of Pan Am flight 103 over Lockerbie, Scotland; he testifies after delay of over month caused by still secret evidence concerning him after defense again tries to block testimony; serves life sentence for fatal Copenhagen bombing (M)/
news.title: Lockerbie Prosecutors Work to Head Off Move to Shift Blame

news.abstract: Eric Morley, who organized and promoted Miss World contest and made parade of pretty girls in swimsuits into televised international sport with millions of fans, dies at 82; photo (M)
news.title: Eric Morley, 82, 'Miss World' Promoter, Dies

news.abstract: Prof John S Morrison, scholar whose boyhood vision of ancient Greek boats known as triremes inspired modern re-creation of that juggernaut, dies at 87; photos (M)
news.title: John S. Morrison, Scholar, 87; Rebuilt a Lost Greek Warship

news.abstract: Number of black South African students commuting to white schools has soared in the five years since lifting of last vestiges of government-enforced segregation opened public schools to all races; more than third of all schools are said to be integrated; unprecedented mingling of black and white children has been overwhelmingly peaceful as black students savor first taste of quality education; photos (M)
news.title: Hesitantly, Students in South Africa Reach Across the Racial Divide

news.abstract: Bitter dispute erupts within Clinton administration over whether to accept Yemen's limits on American investigation of bombing of the destroyer Cole off Aden or press for wider-ranging inquiry that FBI officials believe could potentially lead to powerful people linked to Yemeni government itself; disagreement reportedly exists between FBI Dir Louis J Freeh and Amb Barbara K Bodine; photo (M)
news.title: Cole Inquiry Provokes Bitter U.S. Dispute

news.abstract: Bosnians vote in general elections without excitement, with many expressing determination to try to bring change to country almost five years after signing of Dayton peace accord; polls suggest multiethnic Social Democratic Party, which has rejected nationalist politics and campaigned on trying to mend shattered economy, may gain power in several regions and become kingmaker on national level (S)
news.title: Bosnia Votes With Hope to Break Ethnic Parties' Rule

news.abstract: Hudson Bay's polar bear population is fast becoming worldwide symbol of climate change as ice floes that are home to seal pups melt three weeks earlier than 25 years ago; bears have three weeks less each year to capture and gorge on pups; are 10 percent thinner and have 10 percent fewer cubs than they did 20 years ago; maps; photo (M)
news.title: Canada's 'Gentle Giants' Await Vanishing Winter

news.abstract: Hutomo Mandala Putra, youngest son of Pres Suharto, who was sentenced to 18-month prison term in corruption case, vanishes after request for clemency from Indonesian Supreme Court is rejected; remained free following conviction through series of legal maneuvers and mistakes by prosecution that constitutional scholars describe as absurd; Indonesians say handling of case raises questions over government's commitment to establishing new rule of law after decades of corruption under Suharto's dictatorial rule (M)
news.title: Suharto Son, Now a Fugitive, Flamboyantly Evades Capture

news.abstract: MANILA—  As the Philippines braced for a stormy week of strikes and street protests, lawmakers said Sunday that President Joseph Estrada would very likely be impeached as early as Monday and his case sent to the Senate for trial.
news.title: Foes, Poised for Impeachment, Plan a Strike : Rally Backing Estrada Attracts Over a Million

news.abstract: For globe-trotting frequent travelers, the holidays can mean taking precious time out to shop in unfamiliar cities — but returning home laden with treasure. Here are suggestions for great gifts to pick up during your travels, compiled by our correspondents.
news.title: Exotic Gifts From Far Away:Holiday Shopping on the Road : JAKARTA (folo)

news.abstract: Whether you want a serious night on the town or a quiet drink in a congenial bar, Europe's club scene has it all.
news.title: European Nights:Dance the Dark Away : AMSTERDAM (folo)

news.abstract: Pres Clinton and Prime Min Ehud Barak meet at White House to discuss ways to prevent further violence in West Bank and Gaza that has taken more than 200 lives over past six weeks; somber mood is far cry from heady mood 16 months ago, when Barak came as peacemaker willing to negotiate with Clinton and Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat; photo (M)
news.title: Clinton and Barak Meet With Reduced Expectations

news.abstract: Walter Patrick McConaughy, specialist on Far East for State Department who had high-profile postings in Burma, Pakistan and Taiwan, dies at age 92; photo (M)
news.title: Walter McConaughy, 92, Envoy in Asia, Dies

news.abstract: EUROPE    RUSSIA: AMERICAN LOSES COURT ROUND -- A court rejected an appeal by an American accused of spying to call additional experts to determine whether documents about torpedoes that he received were top secret, as prosecutors allege. The American, Edmond Pope, was arrested in April and charged with trying illegally to obtain plans for the torpedo. He says the information had already been sold abroad.   (Associated Press)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Russian media mogul Vladimir V Gusinsky, fierce critic of government and deeply in debt, tentatively agrees to give up control of publishing and broadcasting empire to country's natural gas monopoly Gazprom, which is controlled by Russian government; agreement, subject to court review, raises questions about level of independence Gusinsky's company, Media-Most, will retain after gas company becomes its largest shareholder; Gusinksy is wanted for questioning by prosecutors in criminal case; left country in July after brief imprisonment for fraud, and warrant has been issued for arrest; he is perhaps single biggest target in campaign of legal and political pressure by Pres Vladimir Putin against prominent Russian businessmen who influenced politics in 1990's; is only one among Putin's opponents required to give up property; lawyers say he will not return to Russia to face questioning (M)
news.title: Putin Critic Yields Control of His Media Empire to the Kremlin

news.abstract: Isra eli-Palestinian violence continues in West Bank and Gaza; Palestinian snipers kill two Israeli soldiers and civilian on West Bank highway and Palestinian gunman kills Israeli truck driver in Gaza; two Palestinian youths are fatally shot by Israeli soldiers; one-day toll is worst for Israel since start hostilities over six weeks ago; Prime Ehud Barak condemns attacks;; vows prompt and 'focused' military response; Israeli Army orders clampdown on movements in and out of Palestinian-governed areas; scours West Bank and Gaza for suspects in attacks; maps; photo (M)
news.title: The Day's Death Toll: Four Israelis and Two Palestinians

news.abstract: Newark, NJ, Federal Dist Judge William G Bassler dismisses 45 of the 49 lawsuits against German companies that used forced labor under Nazis; moves toward disbursing $5.1 billion already established in trust for victims (S)
news.title: Nazi Labor Case Gains
